On 15 April 2019, in Nalgonda district (Telangana), TRS (presently known as BRS) and 30 Congress members clashed at Nayakuni thanda of Tirumalgiri (Sagar) mandal after Congress members allegedly humiliated a TRS (presently known as BRS) leader. At least 4 were injured, 3 in serious condition, and 30-40 houses and furniture were damaged from country-made bombs and stones. Police later intervened.

On 15 April 2019, near Peraiyur taluk (Madurai, TN), residents of Mangammalpatti village staged a protest at the collectorate against the lack of basic infrastructure in the village. They also threatened to boycott the upcoming general elections.
On 15 April 2019, in Perundurai tehsil (Erode, TN), villagers chased and captured a man who was found with a bag stuffed with the legs of a woman he just murdered.

On 15 April 2019, in Salem district (TN), farmers staged a protest and held black flags in Pullavari village against a BJP leader and Union minister for Road Transport and Highways for his support for the implementation of the Chennai-Salem expressway despite a court order staying the project.

On 15 April 2019, in Tadpatri area (Anantapur, AP), rioters set fire to a car owned by a Telugu Yuvatha president (Khader). The rioters were identified by the police but their affiliation was not disclosed. Police also attributed the incident to a personal dispute during the AP general elections.
On 15 April 2019, near Udumalapipettai (Tiruppur, TN), locals and relatives of a boy who drowned in a well staged a brief protest against the delays in finding the body of the boy.
On 15 April 2019, in Visakhapatnam city (Visakhapatnam, AP), AIDWA members staged a protest against the murder of a B. Tech student (S. Jyostna), alleging that the attack was pre-planned.

Assumed on 15 Apr, in Nellimarla mandal (Vizinagaram, AP), leaders of various journalist assocations, including an Uttarandhra Sadhu Parishad president, staged a protest at the Collectorate demanding a probe into the insult made to journalists by a Simhachalam temple Executive Officer at the Ramateertham temple.

On 15 April 2019, BJP workers staged protests outside a police station in Khorda town (Odisha) demanding immediate arrest of the killers of a Bhartiya Janata Party leader was shot dead by unidentified armed men.

On 15 April 2019, farmers who had come to sell their fennel seed produce at Halvad Market Yard in Morbi district (Gujarat) staged a road block and held a demonstration when they did not get the fair price.

On 14 April 2019, Jet Airways' pilots body National Aviator's Guild protested against the airlines for not giving salaries to its employees for the last three months and organised a solidarity meeting in Mumbai city (Maharashtra).
On 15 April 2019, Bhartiya Janata Party and Congress workers clashed at a rally being addressed by Congress Mumbai North candidate and Bollywood actress Urmila Matondkar in Mumbai city (Maharashtra).

On 15 April 2019, the BJP Mahila Morcha burned the effigy of Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan for making derogatory remarks against his contender and BJP nominee for the seat Jaya Prada in Patna city (Bihar).

On 15 April 2019, residents of Asansol of Paschim Bardhaman district (West Bengal) hurled stones at the participants of a Ram Navami rally organized by VHP who were passing through the city. Rallyists retaliated, sparking a clash with residents. The first clash led to a second one, that happened between the rallyists and police, who were trying to take the situation under control. Stones were throw at several police vehicles and at least one motorcycle was set on fire by rallyists.

On 15 April 2019, suspected TMC workers vandalised three booth offices of the BJP in Siliguri city (Darjeeling, West Bengal), ahead of the second phase of the Parliamentary elections, to be held on April 18.
On 15 April 2019, a driver was injured when rioters threw stones at a JKPDP cavalcade containing former CM Mehbooba Mufti at Khiram village (Anantnag, J&K).

On 15 April 2019, a large number of PHE daily wagers staged a protest near the Press Club in Jammu city (J&K), demanding regularisation and the release of unpaid wages. Police prevented protesters from carrying out a march.
On 15 April 2019, women staged a protest at the markets in Bandipora town (J&K) in response to the suicide of a girl who had been alleged sexually abused by her father.
On 15 April 2019, a group of people staged a protest in Kishtwar town (J&K) against the killing of an RSS worker and his PSO, amid the relaxation of a curfew in the area.

On 15 April 2019, the BJP's Bengal observer and his supporters were assaulted by Trinamul supporters and forced to lock himself up at his hotel room near the New Jalpaiguri Station in Siliguri city (Darjeeling, West Bengal), ahead of the second phase of the Parliamentary elections, to be held on April 18.

On 15 April 2019, suspected TMC workers attacked the house of a Congress leader of Bamangola block, at Harishankarpur village (West Bengal), ahead of the second phase of the Parliamentary elections, to be held on April 18.

On 15 April 2019, a clash broke out between two groups participating in Ram Navami rally in Barakar of Asansol (Paschim Bardhaman district, West Bengal). Three people were injured, three two-wheelers set on fire and several auto-rickshaws and shops vandalised. The situation was brought under control after police arrived to the spot.

On 15 April 2019, villagers beat up the husband of a Trinamul gram panchayat member in Bakcha village in Moyna area (Purba Medinipur, West Bengal), when they opposed the installation of a submersible pump by the gram panchayat. Later, the police reached the spot and there was a clash with more than 3000 villagers. Attack on civilian coded as separate event.
On 15 April 2019, family members beat up the employees of a nursing home in Islampur city (North Dinadjpur, West Bengal), after a patient died under their care.

On 15 April 2019, a group of five persons chased and assaulted a PRTC driver near Ludhiana city (Punjab) after a minor traffic accident. No injuries were reported but the driver's uniform was damaged.

On 15 April 2019, villagers locked down the Naga Heritage Village in Kisama complex, located near Phesama village (Kohima, Nagaland), banning visits and any kind of activity in the site, after a man was found dead within the complex. The villagers demanded the stationing of sufficient security personnel at the Complex.

On 15 April 2019, the district vice-president of Congress in Murshidabad was beaten by suspected Trinamul workers and Trinamul youth wing members in Burwan city (Murshidabad, West Bengal), ahead of the second phase of the Parliamentary elections, to be held on April 18. He was severely injured.

On 15 April 2019, two police vehicles were vandalised and set on fire in Barakar Station Road in city in Kulty city located in Asansol area (Paschim Bardhaman, West Bengal), during a Ram Navami rally (Hindu festival). Ten people were later arrested.

On 15 April 2019, a scuffle broke out between AIUDF workers and Congress supporters during an election campaign at Algapur area (Hailakandi, Assam), ahead of the second and third phases of the Parliamentary elections.

On 15 April 2019, a Congress candidate and his supporters held a demonstration in Chanchol city (Malda, West Bengal), in protest against attacks of TMC workers against Congress supporters. The incidents happened ahead of the second phase of the Parliamentary elections, to be held on April 18.

On 15 April 2019, at least five Trinamool Congress workers received injuries following a clash between the TMC and BJP cadres, in Sainthia block area (Birbhum, West Bengal). About a dozen bombs were hurled from both sides. The incident happened ahead of the second phase of the Parliamentary elections, to be held on April 18.

Within the month of Apr, in Sulthanbathery (Wayanad, Kerala), two leaders of the Thovarimala landless tribe were arrested by police following a protest for unknown reasons. No further information was provided.

Within the month of Apr, within AP state, a few incidents of election-related violence (clashes, manhandling, stone pelting, or attacks on convoys) between BJP and NPP were reported. No further information was provided.
Around 15 April 2019 (month of), a mob lynched an Adivasi man in Gumla district (Jharkhand) for cutting a dead bull. Three others were injured in the incident.
On 15 April 2019, demonstrators pelted stones at JKPDP cavalcade at Sirhama village (Anantnag district, J&K).
On 16 April 2019, hundreds of locals demonstrated in Badi Majra village (Yamunanagar, Haryana) after a statue of Ambedkar (former Dalit leader) was vandalised and destroyed.
On 16 April 2019, unidentified persons vandalised and destroyed a statue of Ambedkar (former Dalit leader) in Badi Majra village (Yamunanagar, Haryana).

On 16 April 2019, BKU-affiliated farmers demonstrated outside the Tata Motor agency in Bathinda city (Punjab) to oppose services provided by the vehicle agency during the warranty period, which have resulted in engine damages.

On 16 April 2019, ABVP members demonstrated outside the VC's office on the campus of Panjab University campus in Chandigarh city (Chandigarh) to press for several demands including regularisation of the fee structure, and modernisation of laboratories.
On 16 April 2019, CPI-M members demonstrated in New Delhi (NCT of Delhi) to demand repolling in 464 polling booths in Tripura West.

On 16 April 2019, approximately 600 persons affiliated with Karnataka Gani Avalambithara Vedike demonstrated at Jantar Mantar in Delhi - Connaught Place (New Delhi, Delhi) to demand non-discriminatory practices in iron ore trade among other demands.
On 16 April 2019, IYC workers burnt the effigy of a BJP leader in Dharamsala city (Kangra, Himachal Pradesh) to demand a public apology for language he used against the Congress president.
On 16 April 2019, BJP members demonstrated in Ludhiana city (Punjab) to oppose the alleged failure of the sitting MP and area MLA to implement the Shivaji Nagar nullah project.
On 16 April 2019, INC workers burnt the effigy of a BJP leader in Mandi town (Himachal Pradesh) to demand a public apology for language he used against the Congress president.
On 16 April 2019, INC members shouted slogans against a BJP leader and demonstrated in Shimla city (Himachal Pradesh) to demand action against him for language he used against the Congress president.

Between 10 April and 16 April, INC members shouted slogans against a BJP leader and demonstrated outside the district headquarters in Una town (Himachal Pradesh) to demand a public apology for language he used against the Congress president.

On 16 April 2019, in Andipatti town (Theni, TN), AMMK workers attempted to attack an election flying squad and prevent them from entering their party office to conduct a search over illegal money distribution to voters for the upcoming general elections. The police fired shots in the air to disperse the crowd. 2 received minor injuries. Cash was also recovered.

Assumed on 16 Apr, in Andipatti (Theni, TN), the AMMK staged a demonstration against raids by an election flying squad based on information concerning money distribution to voters for the upcoming general elections. Police resorted to lathi-charge to disperse the demonstrators.

On 16 April 2019, in Karur town (Karur, TN), DMK, including a Congress candidate (Jothimani), clashed with AIADMK cadres near a campaign venue for the upcoming general elections in Vengamedu. At least 15 people, including a policeman, were injured, two in critical condition. A vehicle from the Congress candidate was also damaged.

On 16 April 2019, in Karur town (Karur, TN), following a rioting event in the town, the public, including DMK members, blocked the roads and engaged in stone-throwing, damaging a a TNSTC bus and a few propaganda vehicles of DMK and AMMK candidates. Police dispersed the demonstrators.

Assumed on 16 Apr, in Mysuru area (Mysuru, Karnataka), supporters of a JD(S) observer for the upcoming general elections in Mysuru-Kodagu constituency (Sadolalu Swamy) staged a protest at the Bengaluru-Mysuru highway to protest against the Income Tax Department raids conducted at the office and residences of the leader.

On 16 April 2019, in Ongole (Prakasam, AP), the AP State Road Transport Corporation (APSRTC) Prakasam Regional JAC, including leaders of EU, SWF, and traffic and garage departments, staged a protest at Ongole RTC depot demanding the fulfillment of an agreement made by the Minister and chairman on the clearance of arrears.
Assumed on 16 Apr, in Raichur district (Karnataka), students and locals staged a took out a rally and torchlight parade, demanding justice for a rape and murder victim in their locality.

On 16 April 2019, in Thoothukudi (Thoothokudi, TN), DMK cadres staged a protest in Kurinji Nagar against Income Tax Department raids conducted in the office and residence of a DMK candidate for the upcoming general elections. Police later cordoned off the area.
On 16 April 2019, near Tiruvallur (Tiruvallur, TN), women workers assaulted two men who were caught in the act of raping and assaulting a girl. The men were later arrested.

On 16 April 2019, in Vijayawada (Krishna, AP), the AP Unemployed JAC staged a protest at the AP Public Service Commission (APPSC) office, demanding that the government postpone Group II and Group III examinations. Police arrested the protesters.

On 16 April 2019, in Vizianagaram district (AP), leaders of the All-India Postal and Telecom SC and ST Employees Welfare Association staged a protest against workplace harassment (denial of allowance, leaves, among others) in the Postal Department in the district.
On 16 April 2019, Congress supporters in Gandhinagar (Gujarat) took part in Khedut Aakrosh Rally over a number of farmer issues.
On 16 April 2019, residents demonstrated at the Mini-secretariat in Rohtak city (Haryana) to oppose the discontinuation of ration camps after an earlier stampede resulted in the death of a woman.
On 16 April 2019, polling staff staged a protest in Ramban town (J&K) against the district administration over its failure to make arrangements for meals and accommodation for staff during elections.

On 16 April 2019, students of the Chai Government Middle School of Zone Panchari and local villagers staged a protest in Udhampur district (J&K) over a lack of teachers and drinking facilities at the school.

On 16 April 2019, relatives of Central Jail prisoners staged a protest at the Press Enclave in Srinagar city (J&K), demanding the withdrawal of FIRs against prisoners following an earlier prison riot and any plans to shift them outside the Kashmir Valley.

On 16 April 2019, locals staged protests in Kishtwar town (J&K) against the killing of an RSS worker and his PSO, as well as the killing of a BJP leader and his brother in 2018. The protests came as a curfew in the area was lifted.

On 16 April 2019, locals staged protests in various locations in Kishtwar district (J&K) against the killing of an RSS worker and his PSO, as well as the killing of a BJP leader and his brother in 2018. The protests came as a curfew in the area was lifted.
On 16 April 2019, relatives of a deceased cab driver staged a protest in Pattan town (Baramulla, J&K) and blocked the Srinagar-Muzaffarabad highway, demanding justice over his alleged killing.

On 16 April 2019, near Ramanathapuram (Ramanathapuram, TN), a group from Thennavanur village threw ink on the portrait of Ambedkar during a Scheduled Caste (Dalit) function celebrating the birth anniversary of Ambedkar. The SC group attacked those involved in the incident.

On 16 April 2019, three BJP offices were vandalized in different wards of Balurghat city (Dakshin Dinajpur, West Bengal), by suspected TMC members, ahead of the second phase of the Parliamentary elections, to be held on April 18.

On 16 April 2019, four persons from Laitkyrhong village were assaulted by locals in Mawkynring village (East Khasi Hills, Meghalaya), on the suspicion they were chasing some girls. The locals also accused them of being Menshohnoh (local legend of killers who make sacrifices for wealth).

On 16 April 2019, members of the CPI-M staged a protest in Agartala city (West Tripura, Tripura), to demand repolling in 464 booths, for the Parliamentary elections. They alleged there were several episodes of rigging and violence during the April 11 voting.

On 16 April 2019, two workers of the BJP were injured in a group clash between the workers of the Congress and BJP in Kanishail village near Karimganj city (Karimganj, Assam), ahead of the second phase of the Parliamentary elections, to be held on April 18.
On 16 April 2019, people protested at Pulwama district (J&K) against midnight arrests in Pulwama.

On 17 April 2019, BJD workers attacked a BJP candidate hurling stones at the candidate's car in Kandhara village of Bijepur (Bargarh district, Odisha). Neither the candidate nor his associates who were in the vehicle were injured.
On 17 April 2019, BJD workers attacked BJP leaders and party members in Kadalijhola village of Lathipada (Ganjam district, Odisha). A young supporter of BJP was allegedly beaten to death.
On 17 April 2019, BJD supporters attacked BJP leaders and workers in Bhatli area (Bargarh district, Odisha), leaving some of the BJP members injured.

On 17 April 2019, in Gajendragarh taluk (Gadag, Karnataka), residents blockaded roads with empty pots and vehicles, preventing campaigners for the upcoming general elections to enter, to demonstrate against lack of supply of drinking water. Demonstration still ongoing as of 18 Apr. Day 1

On 17 April 2019, a mob of over 12 persons attacked the home of a BJP worker in New Puneet Nagar in Ludhiana city (Punjab) over an alleged old rivalry connected to social services. No injuries were reported but vehicles were vandalised and threats were made.
On 17 April 2019, persons affiliated with the All BTC Welfare Association demonstrated in Agra city (Uttar Pradesh). The demonstrators held banners demanding jobs.

Between 11 April and 17 April, Sikh activists affiliated with various outfits demonstrated outside the Sangrur deputy commissioner's office in Sangrur town (Punjab), to demand the cancellation of the transfer order for a IGP. The demonstrators also burnt the effigies of the PM, CM and the Akali Dal chief.
On 17 April 2019, following the killing of a young BJP supporter by BJD workers, BJP supporters staged road blockade in protest in Kadalijhola village of Lathipada (Ganjam district, Odisha).

On 17 April 2019, BJD workers attacked BJP members during poll campaigning of a BJP candidate in a slum area of Niladri Vihar in Bhubaneswar town (Khordha district, Odisha). During the attack nine BJP workers sustained critical injuries.

On 17 April 2019, in Coimbatore (Coimbatore, TN), relatives of a woman who died while delivering a stillborn child staged a protest at the Coimbatore Medical College Hospital demanding a probe into the death of the mother and child, alleging medical negligence from the doctor who was assigned to her.

On 17 April 2019, in Jagtial town (Jagtial, Telangana), the Telangana State Union of Working Journalists (TSUWJ) staged a dharna in front of the Collectorate condemning the registration of false cases against nine journalists who reported about the transportation of EVMs in a private vehicle recently.
On 17 April 2019, people who had recently been relocated from the Tansa pipeline area to a heavy industrial area in Mahul held a protest in Mumbai against BJP candidate Manoj Kotak.
On 17 April 2019, traders and local residents staged a protest in Baramulla town (J&K) against a delay in the reconstruction of a SRTC bridge damaged in 2014 floods.
On 17 April 2019, a local AIP leader was hospitalised after being attacked by RSS political workers in Bhadarwah town (Doda, J&K). At least one was armed with a metal rod.

On 17 April 2019, communal-based rioters threw stones at the shops of a rival community in Bhadarwah town (Doda, J&K). The rioting followed an attack on an AIP activists by RSS activists. No further information on the identity of the rioters reported.

On 17 April 2019, rioters attacked and hospitalised a constable assigned as the PSO for a senior JKNC activist while they inspected a polling booth in the Anchar area of Srinagar city (J&K). The activist escaped unharmed.
On 17 April 2019, rioters threw stones at an election duty vehicle at Gogo in the Humhama area (Srinagar, J&K).

On 17 April 2019, unidentified persons set fire to Kawmohalla Khanyar Government Boys High School. Stones and petrol bombs were also thrown at Gurgari Mohalla Government Higher Secondary School in Srinagar city (J&K). The two schools are hosting polling booths.
On 17 April 2019, stone throwing was reported in pre-election violence at (Chanthan) Gulabpura village (Ganderbal, J&K). It is unclear who was targeted by the violence (assumed civilians).
On 17 April 2019, stone throwing was reported in pre-election violence at Lar town (Ganderbal, J&K). It is unclear who was targeted by the violence (assumed civilians).
On 17 April 2019, villagers staged a protest at Kulwanta village in Ramnagar tehsil (Udhampur, J&K) against the poor condition of the under-construction PMGSY road to Bari Ladana.

On 17 April 2019, Trinamul and BJP workers clashed in Balapara and Jamidarpara areas, under Rajganj Assembly area (Jalpaiguri, West Bengal), one day before the voting of the second phase of Parliamentary elections. At least eight persons were injured.

On 17 April 2019, women and girls staged a protest march in Magrahat II block area (South 24 Parganas, West Bengal), against the assault on a 16-year-old girl from the block by a man, on April 13. They demanded street lights, better police surveillance and a check on liquor shops for women's safety.

On 17 April 2019, villagers staged a protest and demanded an investigation in Kallapara village under Palasbari Tehsil area (Kamrup, Assam), after a man, working with the Assam Police, was shot by a Meghalaya Police personnel during a public meeting.

On 17 April 2019, local people staged a protest and prevented polling personnel from entering the polling station in Abdulghata village under Raiganj area (Uttar Dinajpur, West Bengal), one day before the second phase of the Parliamentary elections. The locals demanded the deployment of paramilitary forces for peaceful voting.

On 17 April 2019, local people staged a protest and prevented polling personnel from entering the polling station in Chatrapur village under Raiganj area (Uttar Dinajpur, West Bengal), one day before the second phase of the Parliamentary elections. The locals demanded the deployment of paramilitary forces for peaceful voting.

On 17 April 2019, local people staged a protest and prevented polling personnel from entering the polling station in Lahujgram village under Raiganj area (Uttar Dinajpur, West Bengal), one day before the second phase of the Parliamentary elections. The locals demanded the deployment of paramilitary forces for peaceful voting.

On 17 April 2019, local people staged a protest and prevented polling personnel from entering the polling station in Sukdeppur under Chopra area (Uttar Dinajpur, West Bengal), one day before the second phase of the Parliamentary elections. The locals demanded the deployment of paramilitary forces for peaceful voting.
As reported on April 17, Jet Airways employees started a dharna before the old domestic terminal at Kolkata airport, in Kolkata city (Kolkata, West Bengal), to demand the payment of their salaries.

On 17 April 2019, locals and the Naga Peoples Coordination Committee (NPCC) staged a protest demonstration in Churachandpur city (Churachandpur, Manipur), against the opening of the strong room at the district, on April 12, a day after the polling for the Parliamentary elections.

On 17 April 2019, thousands of villagers staged a protest in the National Highway in Chapar city (Dhubri, Assam), in protest after a BJP worker was killed by unidentified men on April 16. The incident occurred ahead of the polling in Dhubri district, to be held during the third phase of the Parliamentary elections, on April 23.

Assumed on 18 Apr, in Basheerabad mandal (Vikarabad, Telangana), aspirants of the Telangana police recruitment examinations staged a dharna demanding cancellation of the main examination scheduled on April 28 and asked to re-conduct physical exams, alleging a scam.
On 18 April 2019, a group of Jansatta Party workers assaulted BJP workers during a public meeting in the Kalyanpur area (Allahabad, Uttar Pradesh). No injuries were reported.
On 18 April 2019, members of Biju Yuva Bahini attacked the campaign rally of a BJP candidate at Brahmanadeo village of Krushna Prasad block (Puri district, Odisha). At least 24 persons were injured.

On 18 April 2019, supporters of an unidentified political party attacked a journalist while he was covering second phase polls at a booth in Kantamala area (Boudh district, Odisha). The assaulters damaged the journalist's equipment and beat him.

On 18 April 2019, about 100 of MahaMetro employees gathered in front of the makeshift office of MahaMetro in Pune city (Maharashtra) to protest against unpaid salary of five months and start a strike.
On 18 April 2019, a man threw a shoe at a BJP leader during a press briefing in Delhi (NCT of Delhi). He was then assaulted by a group of BJP workers before being detained by police.

On 18 April 2019, in Doddarasinakere in Maddur tehsil (Mandya, Karnataka), supporters of a JD(S) candidate and a BJP-backed independent candidate clashed during the Karnataka general elections over the issue of holding a road show. Police resorted to lathi-charge to disperse the rioting groups.
On 18 April 2019, in Basavanpura in Malavalli tehsil (Mandya, Karnataka), JD(S) workers assaulted a BJP-backed independent candidate (Sumalatha), injuring him, during the Karnataka general elections.
On 18 April 2019, residents and plot owners of Model Town Phase 4 and 5 demonstrated at PUDA's office in Bathinda city (Punjab) to oppose the extra charges for the purchased plots.
On 18 April 2019, Jet Airways staff demonstrated at Jantar Mantar in Delhi - Connaught Place (New Delhi, Delhi) to demand that the government and banks save the airline from shutting down.

Between 12 April and 18 April, a large number of truck operators raised slogans against the state government and demonstrated outside the deputy commissioner office in Sangrur town (Punjab). The demonstrators demanded the arrest of the accused who earlier attacked a former truck union president.
On 18 April 2019, cane growers demonstrated inside and outside the Deputy Commissioner's office in Sangrur town (Punjab) to demand the release of dues owed to them.
On 18 April 2019, BKU affiliated farmers held a dharna on the premises of Rajiv Gandhi Education City in Sonipat city (Haryana) to demand proper procurement facilities.

On 18 April 2019, relatives of three youth who were found dead in a canal in UP, parked a tractor-trolley with one of the bodies and blocked the Sonepat-Gohana highway in Sonipat district (Haryana). The demonstrators believe the youth were murdered and their bodies discarded in the canal.

On 18 April 2019, near Boothapandi in Thovala tehsil (Kanyakumari, TN), BJP and AMMK workers clashed at a booth in Veeravanallur government higher secondary school during the TN general elections. Police dispersed the clashing groups.

On 18 April 2019, in Vallam area (Thanjavur, TN), Moopatheru (or Monnayampatti) residents staged a protest and blocked the Thanjavur-Tiruchi (or Vallam-Tiruchy) Road against a lack of basic amenities in their area. They also threatened to boycott the TN general elections but policemen and revenue officials pacified them.

On 18 April 2019, in Ponparappi village in Sendurai tehsil (Ariyalur, TN), PMK workers, including a caste group from the Vanniyar community, Hindu Munnani and AIADMK members, clashed with VCK workers and Dalits after a group of volunteers torched a VCK symbol during the TN general elections. This resulted to 20 damaged houses and a torched vehicle. A heavy group of police intervened. A journalist covering the event was also assaulted by Dalits.
On 18 April 2019, in Ponparappi area in Sendurai tehsil (Ariyalur, TN), a Dalit group pushed a PMK worker down and abused him following an argument during the TN general elections.

On 18 April 2019, in Alur (Chamarajanagar, Karnataka), villagers staged a protest and threatened to boycott the Karnataka general elections, demanding that the government release water to canals for minor irrigation and agriculture activities in their village.

On 18 April 2019, in Ambur tehsil (Vellore, TN), AIADMK men allegedly damaged the sideview mirror of a car belonging to an AMMK candidate (Balasubramanian) during a clash between the AIADMK and AMMK. Police resorted to mild lathi-charge to disperse the clashing groups.

actor2: Police Forces of India (2014-) Central Industrial Security Force
text: On 18 April 2019, near Arcot (Vellore, TN), a Central Industrial Security Force officer opened fire in the air to disperse PMK workers attempting to barge into a polling booth at the Panchayat Union Primary School at Keezhvisharam during the TN general elections. No one was injured in the incident.

On 18 April 2019, in Asifabad (Komaram Bheem Asifabad, Telangana), the Telangana State Union of Working Journalists (TSUWJ) staged a dharna in front of the Collectorate, condemning the registration of false cases against nine journalists who reported about the transportation of EVMs in a private vehicle recently.

Assumed on 18 Apr, in Bengaluru (Bengaluru Urban, Karnataka), people gathered near Ambedkar college in Pulkeshinagar shouting slogans against the government and election commission for being unable to vote during the Karnataka general elections as their names were not included in the voters' list.

On 18 April 2019, in Chennai area (Chennai, TN), Pulianthope and Purasawalkam locals staged a protest outside the Basinbridge Corporation Office after not being allowed to vote during the TN general elections as they were not able to receive their booth slips.

On 18 April 2019, in Chennai (Chennai, TN), passengers staged a road blockade at the Chennai Mofussil Bus Terminus (CMBT) over non-availability of buses which caused some passengers not being able to cast their vote for the TN general elections. Police resorted to lathi-charge to control the crowd.
On 18 April 2019, in Chitradurga district (Karnakata), Congress and BJP workers clashed during the Karnataka general elections, leaving one person injured. No further information was provided.
On 18 April 2019, in Dharmapuri district (TN), unidentified rioters captured a poll booth at Nathamedu village during the TN general elections. No further information was provided.
On 18 April 2019, near Gudiyatham (Vellore, TN), DMK and PMK volunteers clashed at Kallar village. Police resorted to lathi-charge to disperse the clashing groups.
On 18 April 2019, in Gudiyatham area (Vellore, TN), AIADMK and AMMK workers clashed at the constituency. No further information was provided.

On 18 April 2019, in Hosur area (Krishnagiri, TN), passengers blocked the Bengaluru-Chennai national highway near Hosur bus stand to protest against bus conductors not allowing them to board buses. Transport officials pacified the protesters.
On 18 April 2019, in Hyderabad (Hyderabad, Telangana), angry residents of Wadi-e-Mustafa staged a protest at the streets of Old City demanding daily water supply to their locality.

On 18 April 2019, in Kallakurichi district (TN), a person accused of murder was attacked and his vehicle damaged by relatives of the victim when the former came to cast his vote at Thenkeranoor for the TN general elections.
On 18 April 2019, in Maddur taluk (Mandya, Karnataka), youths raised slogans over Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) not working during the Karnataka general elections in Pannedoddi.

On 18 April 2019, in Malavalli tehsil (Mandya, Karnataka), supporters a JD(S) candidate assaulted a polling agent accusing him of urging citizens to vote for a rival candidate during the Karnataka general elections.
On 18 April 2019, in Mandya town (Karnataka), a minor clash occurred between BJP and JD(S) workers at Hasahalli during the Karnataka general elections.
On 18 April 2019, near Melur (Madurai, TN), AIADMK and AMMK workers clashed near a polling booth at Kottakudi during the TN general elections, leaving 3 injured.

On 18 May 2019, a SAD booth agent was assaulted and injured by a group of alleged Congress workers in Gurusar Saine Wala village (Bathinda, Punjab).

On 18 May (assumed), an AAP MP and a SAD former government minister sat on dharna along with their supporters on the Patiala-Patran road in Samana city (Patiala, Punjab) after a country-made liquor producer attempted to remove illegally stored liquor.

On 18 May 2019, the All Parties Migrant Coordination Committee (APMCC) staged a protest at Pratap Park in Srinagar city (J&K), accusing the state and central governments of neglecting the needs of PM package employees and Pandits in general.
On 18 May 2019, rioters clashed with state forces (assumed police) in Anantnag town (J&K), amid a shutdown in response to state forces engaging a local militant in a nearby village.
On 18 May 2019, mourners raised anti-India and pro-separatist slogans during the funeral of a slain HM militant at Panzgam village (Pulwama, J&K).

On 18 May 2019, mourners raised anti-India and pro-separatist slogans during the funeral of a slain HM militant at Tahab village (Pulwama, J&K). Clashes between youths and state forces (assumed police) were reported following the funeral.
On 18 May 2019, residents staged a protest in the Mantrigam area (Bandipora, J&K), appealing for police to increase efforts to locate a missing teacher.

On 18 May 2019, villagers staged a protest with the body of an electrocuted man at Mehari village in Kalakote tehsil (Rajouri, J&K), demanding action against PDD staff that they accuse of being responsible for his death and compensation for his family.

On 18 May 2019, members of the Asom Jatiyatabadi Yuba-Chatra Parishad (AJYCP) and the Noa-Dihing Bandh Suraksha Sangram Samity staged a sit-in-demonstration in Kakopathar city (Tinsukia, Assam), in support of the demand for early construction of the Dirak-Sumani dyke along the Noa-Dihing river under the Doomdooma area.

On 18 May 2019, four suspected cattle smugglers (likely Muslim based on name) were beaten by mob led by cow vigilantes near Mairwa Dham village (Siwan district, Bihar). Two of the four received critical injuries.

On 18 May 2019, in Bengaluru (Bengaluru Urban, Karnataka), homebuyers across the state, including the Forum for Peoples Collective Efforts (FPCE) and various resident welfare associations and organizations, staged a protest at the Town Hall demanding the government to properly implement the Real Estate Regulatory Authority (RERA).
On 18 May 2019, in Yadgir (Yadgir, Karnataka), Congress workers staged a protest against the BJP and the Union Minister for their remarks against Nathuram Godse.

On 18 May 2019, in Kozhikode (Kozhikode, Kerala), the Bharathiya Dalit Congress and relatives of a man who died from health deterioration after laparoscopy staged a protest alleging medical negligence and demanding a post-mortem.

On 18 May 2019, men's right activists and members of a rights NGO held placards and demonstrated at India Gate in Delhi - Connaught Place (New Delhi, Delhi) to demand justice for men facing accusations of sexual assault. The demonstrators included a contingent of women.
On 18 May 2019, a SAD worker was beaten and injured by a group of alleged Congress workers in rural Bathinda district (Punjab) after he refused to promote for the Congress party.
On 18 May 2019, SAD workers blocked the Bathinda-Goniana road in Bathinda district (Punjab) to demand the registration of a case against an INC worker who allegedly abducted a SAD worker.

On 18 May 2019, in Chidambaram (Cuddalore, TN), farmers, including the Cauvery Delta Farmers' Association and Delta Water Resources Protection Front, staged a protest march to the to the Sabapathy temple seeking divine intervention against the hydrocarbon project of the government.

On 18 May 2019, in Ramanathapuram district (TN), two groups of Dalit youths clashed when the group from Pappakudi village barred the group from Kavarankulam village to visiting the former's village. These villagers had a longstanding enmity between them due to love marriages involving the youths in their village.
On 18 May 2019, in Rayanallur in Thiruthuraipoondi tehsil (Tiruvarur, TN), farmers staged a protest meeting to oppose the hydrocarbon project of the government.

Assumed on 18 May, in Hyderabad area (Hyderabad, Telangana), National Urban Health Mission (NUHM) employees working as accountants and clerks staged a protest against their pending salary hike. About 80 employees were detained by police officers when they attempted to meet the Chief Minister.

On 18 May 2019, people staged a demonstration and blocked the Jhansi-Mirzapur highway in Mahoba district (Uttar Pradesh) after a man was found hanging outside the SDM office. Rioters threw stones at vehicles but no injuries were reported.

On 18 May 2019, in Thiruvananthapuram (Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala), the Thovarimala landless tribe composing of Dalits and Adivasi groups, including the CPI ML Red Star, BSP, IDF, SUCI, RMP, Western Ghats Protection Board, Pothanpara Forest Protection Committee and Democratic Protection committee, staged a protest at the Secretariat demanding land to the landless families in Wayanad.
On 18 May 2019, rioters clashed with state forces (assumed military and police) during a CASO at Kojar village (Kulgam, J&K).

On 18 May 2019, the car of a BJP candidate was attacked by suspected TMC members in Dongaria area of Diamond Harbour area (South 24 Parganas, West Bengal), one day before the seventh and final phase of voting for the Parliamentary elections.

On 18 May 2019, traders took out a protest rally in Hailakandi city (Hailakandi, Assam), to appeal to shopkeepers to open shutters. The shops had been closed after one person died while several others were hurt in clashes which broke out between two different communal groups outside the mosque, on May 10.

On 18 May 2019, a mob of villagers stormed a police station in Kalyanpur city (Khowai, Tripura), to rescue a man who had been detained on the charge of involvement in illegal drug trade. At least seven policemen, including Tripura Rifles (TSR) were injured.
On 18 May 2019, a mob assaulted a lawyer and vandalized Lamphel Court Complex in Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur). The group was agitating against the murder of a man in Bamon Kampu.
On 19 May 2019, a man was beaten by a group of persons in Phulo Kheri village (Bathinda, Punjab) during a disagreement over voting days earlier. No injuries were reported.

On 19 May 2019, a Congress sarpanch was assaulted by a group of as many as 20 persons believed to be affiliated with the BJP near Bakhu Shah village (Ferozepur, Punjab). The sarpanch was on his way to vote when he was assaulted with stones; no injuries were reported. .
On 19 May 2019, a BJP executive committee member was attacked by a group of 17 persons in Awankha village (Gurdaspur, Punjab). No injuries or motive were reported.
On 19 May 2019, four persons were injured after Congress and SAD workers clashed in Kot Mohan Lal village (Gurdaspur, Punjab).
On 19 May 2019, Congress and SAD workers clashed in Ladoi village in Bhogpur area (Jalandhar, Punjab). No injuries were reported but a poll booth was damaged.
On 19 May 2019, Congress and BSP workers clashed at a booth in Kingra village (Jalandhar, Punjab) during polling. No injuries were reported.

On 19 May 2019, three persons were injured during a clash between two Congress supporters and a supporter of the Punjab Democratic Alliance during polling in Kalal Majra village (Ludhiana, Punjab). The clash is believed to be as a result of political differences.
On 19 May 2019, Congress workers were attacked with stones by a group of approximately 6 SAD workers in Chainewala village (Mansa, Punjab).
On 19 May 2019, Congress and SAD workers clashed outside the polling station in Gajiana village (Moga, Punjab) during polling. No injuries were reported.
On 19 May 2019, Congress and SAD workers clashed during polling in Bari village (Sahibzada Ajit Singh Nagar, Punjab). No injuries were reported.
On 19 May 2019, two groups of Congress workers clashed during polling in Ealwal village (Sangrur, Punjab). Three persons were injured in the clash.

On 19 May 2019, a Sikh man was attacked by a group of persons making caste-based remarks against him and removing his turban in Ghurkwind village (Tarn Taran, Punjab). The assault is believed to be poll-related; no injuries were reported.

On 19 May 2019, in Costi in Sanguem tehsil (South Goa, Goa), mining employees staged a protest, blocked the entrance to the mine and denied entry to the officials demanding alternative employment by the company in any of its other units after some of its employees were reinstated.

On 19 May 2019, in Khanapur in Chincholi taluk (Kalaburagi, Karnataka), four supporters of a Congress candidate, including a panchayat member, clashed with BJP workers during the by-elections after the former was caught distributing money to voters. The Congress supporters were then handed over to the police.

On 19 May 2019, residents, SP and BSP workers demonstrated outside the police station in Alinagar village (Chandauli, Uttar Pradesh) to oppose the alleged bribery by the BJP workers. The demonstrators alleged that people were being bribed to skip votes.
On 19 May 2019, SP and BJP activists clashed at a polling booth in Parashurampur village (Chandauli, Uttar Pradesh) over the installation of flags at the polling station.
On 19 May 2019, family members were assaulted by a group of approximately 20 persons in Raipur Khadar village (Gautam Buddha Nagar, Uttar Pradesh) over a property dispute.

On 19 May 2019, in Kannampalaiyam in Palladam tehsil (Coibmatore, TN), voters who did not make it to the cut-off time during the by-elections staged a protest demanding permission to cast votes. AIADMK functionaries joined their protest. They also did not allow the officials to take out the voting machines.

On 19 May 2019, in Chittoor district (AP), a TDP candidate and his followers attacked a general agent over accusations of seeking votes and canvassing for a YSRC candidate at the voting station during the re-polling for the general elections in Pulivarthipalle village. The general agent is a close relative of a YSRCP candidate.

On 19 May 2019, a group of 7 persons assaulted three people of the same family in Mullana village (Ambala, Haryana) over a land dispute. No injuries were reported but a television and a car were damaged.

On 19 May 2019, relatives of a doctor who was killed last year demonstrated at Sadar Bazaar in Karnal city (Haryana) to oppose the alleged police inaction. The demonstrators demanded the arrest of the attackers.

On 19 May 2019, in Holalkere taluk (Chitradurga, Karnataka), the Karnataka Rajya Raitha Sangha staged a protest procession and dharna outside the Block Education Office in the taluk demanding action against private schools collecting huge donations from parents for admitting their children.

On 19 May 2019, in Mysuru city (Mysuru, Karnataka), two groups clashed after a hotel owner and a cloth shop owner from two communities, known to have a longstanding dispute, had an argument over a minor issue. Police intervened to pacify the clashing groups. Vehicles and properties were damaged. 2 were injured and 6 were arrested.
On 19 May 2019, over 50 Sector 23 residents demonstrated in Delhi-New Delhi (NCT of Delhi) to oppose the cutting of trees for a road widening project.

On 19 May 2019, a police constable was beaten by a group of persons at the railway station in Delhi-New Delhi (NCT of Delhi) while he was executing his duties. He was rescued by other security personnel; no injuries were reported.

On 19 May 2019, police personnel were attacked with stones and injured in Wazirabad in Delhi - Civil Lines (Central Delhi, Delhi) after they attempted to intervene in a clash between two groups at the location. A constable was injured in the attack.

On 19 May 2019, in Puducherry, the Puducherry Agro Service and Industries Corporation (PASIC) staged a protest in front of its head office at Thattanchavady demanding disbursement of their salaries. They have not received their salaries in the past 57 months.

On 19 May 2019, in Puducherry, Hindu Munnani members attempted to burn an effigy in front of Swadeshi Cotton Mills in protest against an MNM by-elections candidate and his remarks about Naturam Godse as a Hindu and the first extremist of India when he assassinated Mahatma Gandhi. Police seized the effigy from the protesters.
On 19 May 2019, Congress and SAD supporters clashed in a village in Amritsar district (Punjab). No injuries were reported.
On 19 May 2019, a woman was assaulted by alleged SAD workers in Mohalla village in Bathinda district (Punjab) after she supported the Congress in the elections. No injuries were reported.
On 19 May 2019, a Congress worker was assaulted by a group of approximately 13 SAD workers at DAV College in Bathinda city (Punjab) during polling. No injuries were reported.
On 19 May 2019, eight persons were injured during a clash between SAD and Congress workers in (assumed) Bathinda city (Punjab).
On 19 May 2019, Congress and SAD workers clashed in several places in Budhlada city (Mansa, Punjab) during polling. No injuries were reported.
On 19 May 2019, the car of a former SAD minister was attacked and damaged by Congress workers in Faridkot city (Punjab). No injuries were reported.
On 19 May 2019, Congress and SAD-BJP workers clashed on several occasions during polling in Ferozepur district (Punjab). No injuries were reported.
On 19 May 2019, Congress and SAD-BJP workers clashed on several occasions during polling in Gurdaspur district (Punjab). No injuries were reported.

On 19 May 2019, two brothers were injured after they were attacked with baseball bats by a group of approximately 12 persons in Gurdaspur city (Punjab). The brothers were on their way to a polling station when they were attacked.
On 19 May 2019, Congress and SAD supporters clashed in a village in Hoshiarpur district (Punjab). No injuries were reported.
On 19 May 2019, Congress and SAD-BJP workers clashed on several occasions during polling in Jalandhar district (Punjab). No injuries were reported.

On 19 May 2019, a senior citizen and her relatives sat on dharna in front of the polling booth at Narotam Vidya Mandir School in Khanna city (Ludhiana, Punjab) after her name was missing from the voters list.
On 19 May 2019, Congress and SAD-BJP workers clashed on several occasions during polling in Ludhiana district (Punjab). No injuries were reported.

On 19 May 2019, a social activist and a Congress councillor and supporters clashed during polling in Ludhiana city (Punjab). Conflicting accounts were provided as the activist alleged that he and his father (a LIP leader) were assaulted by Congress workers, while the Congress councillor accused the activist of being abusive and making false accusations due to political rivalry. No injuries were reported.

On 19 May 2019, a social activist and a large number of his supporters demonstrated at Shivpuri Chowk in Ludhiana city (Punjab) to demand action against a Congress councillor and his supporters. The activist's father is a LIP leader.

On 19 May 2019, SAD-BJP and Congress workers clashed at the polling station near Bharat Nagar Chowk in Ludhiana city (Punjab). Conflicting reports suggest that BJP activists were assaulted by a group of over 24 Congress affiliated youth, while others state that it was the Congress workers who were attacked and the party agent's booth ransacked by SAD-BJP activists. No injuries were reported.

On 19 May 2019, a man was allegedly beaten by the BJP general secretary and a group of persons outside the polling centre at Bhartiya Vidya Mandir in Ludhiana city (Punjab). It is believed that the attack is connected to a property dispute; no injuries were reported.
On 19 May 2019, an Akali activist was beaten and injured by a group of alleged Congress workers near Charik village (Moga, Punjab). He was admitted to hospital.
On 19 May 2019, Congress and SAD-BJP workers clashed on several occasions during polling in Moga district (Punjab). No injuries were reported.
On 19 May 2019, Congress and SAD workers clashed in several places in Muktsar city (Punjab) during polling. No injuries were reported.
On 19 May 2019, demonstrators including a BSP sarpanch waved black flags in Phillaur town (Jalandhar, Punjab) to oppose the Congress candidate and sitting MP during polling.
On 19 May 2019, two SAD polling agents were assaulted by a group of unidentified persons during polling in Kangar village (Bathinda, Punjab). No injuries were reported.
On 19 May 2019, a SAD former minister was attacked and his car damaged by alleged Congress workers during polling at Kangar village (Bathinda, Punjab) after an earlier attack on SAD workers.
On 19 May 2019, SAD workers were allegedly attacked by unidentified persons in Rampura Phul city (Bathinda, Punjab). One person was injured in the attack.
On 19 May 2019, Congress and SAD-BJP workers clashed on several occasions during polling in Sangrur district (Punjab). No injuries were reported.
On 19 May 2019, SAD workers demonstrated outside a polling station in Talwandi Sabo town (Bathinda, Punjab) after 3 SAD workers were injured in a firing by alleged Congress workers.

On 19 May 2019, in Ramanathapuram district (TN), Kavarankulam villagers, armed with wooden clubs, attacked houses and two-wheelers at Pappakudi village in retaliation to the clash against youths in Pappakudi the previous day. 4 persons were severely injured. These Dalit groups had a longstanding enmity between them due to love marriages involving the youths in their village.

Assumed on 19 May, in Ramanathapuram district (TN), a Dalit group from Pappakudi village staged a protest and blocked the roads demanding action against Kavarankulam villagers who damaged their houses and set fire to two-wheelers.

On 19 May 2019, near Sulur (Coibmatore, TN), Lord Muruga devotees and voters staged a protest against a security guard at Jallipatti after they were not allowed to vote during the by-elections because of their vesti-in-green and saffron-colour outfits.

On 19 May 2019, in Tiruchirappalli (Tiruchirappalli, TN), the HMK staged a protest and attempted to burn an effigy of an MNM by-elections candidate over his remarks about Naturam Godse as a Hindu and the first extremist of India when he assassinated Mahatma Gandhi. Police arrested the protesters.

On 19 May 2019, in Hyderabad (Hyderabad, Telangana), organizations Arunodaya, Progressive Organisation of Women (POW), Telangana Sahithi, including a professor, staged a protest at Sundarayya Vignana Kendram against attempts to brand people who are helping in sexual harassment cases as Maoists.

On 19 May 2019, in Hyderabad (Hyderabad, Telangana), a patient's companions punched and attempted to strangulate a doctor at Nizam's Institute of Medical Sciences (NIMS) after alleged delays in treatment of the patient. The companions were reportedly in an inebriated state when the incident happened.
On 19 May 2019, BJP and SP workers clashed near a polling booth in Sikitiya area in Chandauli district (Uttar Pradesh). No injuries were reported.

On 19 May 2019, eight farmers were detained after they took tractors filled with sugarcane to two polling booths in Kushinagar town (Uttar Pradesh) to demonstrate against a sugar mill who had stopped cane crushing, resulting in their produce perishing.
On 19 May 2019, passengers stopped the train in Bhubaneswar (Khordha district, Odisha) and staged a protest over defunctioning air conditioning system in the vehicle.
On 19 May 2019, in Panaji tehsil area (North Goa, Goa), sporadic incidents of violence by unknown groups were reported during the Panaji by-election. No further information was provided.
On 19 May 2019, the local Beopar Mandal staged a protest in Udhampur town (J&K) against a hike in the toll at Ban Toll Plaza.

On 19 May 2019, the youth wing of the JKNPP led a protest by locals at Om Nagar in Jammu city (J&K) against the Jammu Municipal Corporation (JMC), the PHE department, and the PWD department over the poor condition of a road and water supply in the area.

On 19 May 2019, locals assaulted a youth in Shibnagar village under Melaghar police station area (Sepahijala, Tripura), on the suspicion of killing his friend. The police rescued the suspect from the mob and arrested him. The victim's body was found in the morning. The reason behind the killing is being investigated.

On 19 May 2019, voters including BJP supporters staged a protest outside booth number 189 in Basirhat area (North 24 Parganas, West Bengal), after being beaten up by suspected TMC workers on their way to the polling booth, during the seventh and final phase of voting for the Parliamentary elections.

On 19 May 2019, a CPI-M leader and supporters staged a protest demonstration in Belgachia area in Kolkata city (Kolkata, West Bengal), after CPI-M polling agents were beaten up and not allowed to sit inside the booths, during the seventh and final phase of voting for the Parliamentary elections.

On 19 May 2019, voters including BJP supporters were beaten up by suspected TMC workers on their way to booth number 189 in Basirhat area (North 24 Parganas, West Bengal), during the seventh and final phase of voting for the Parliamentary elections. The car of a BJP aid was also vandalized by TMC supporters in Tatra area of Basirhat.

On 19 May 2019, a BJP mandal president was beaten up by TMC workers in booth numbers 150 and 137, in Mukundapur in Kolkata city (Kolkata, West Bengal), during the seventh and final phase of voting for the Parliamentary elections. TMC also rioted in the city, and crude bombs were hurled in Posta area and in Rabindra Sarani.

On 19 May 2019, there were reports of violence led by TMC workers in polling booths in Dum Dum area (North 24 Parganas, West Bengal), during the seventh and final phase of voting for the Parliamentary elections.

On 19 May 2019, there were reports of violence led by TMC workers in polling booths in Diamond Harbour area (South 24 Parganas, West Bengal), during the seventh and final phase of voting for the Parliamentary elections.

On 19 May 2019, TMC workers vandalized a CPM booth camp at Baghajatin under Jadavpur in Kolkata city (Kolkata, West Bengal), during the seventh and final phase of voting for the Parliamentary elections. CPI-M polling agents were also beaten up and not allowed to sit inside the booths in North Kolkata area. A CPI-M agent was chased out and beaten in Belgachia area.

On 19 May 2019, there were reports of crude bombs being hurled as voters queued up in polling booths 66 and 67 in Gilaberia area of Deganga area (North 24 Parganas, West Bengal), during the seventh and final phase of voting for the Parliamentary elections. The BJP claimed the attackers were TMC supporters.

On 19 May 2019, there were reports of crude bombs being hurled by suspected TMC workers as voters queued up in polling booths in Raidighi area under Mathurapur Constituency area (South 24 Parganas, West Bengal), during the seventh and final phase of voting for the Parliamentary elections.

On 19 May 2019, BJP supporters were beaten up and its camp office vandalised by suspected TMC workers in Kultali area (South 24 Parganas, West Bengal), during the seventh and final phase of voting for the Parliamentary elections.

On 19 May 2019, a BJP camp office was set ablaze by suspected TMC workers in Kamapur area in Rajarhat/New Town city under the Barasat constituency area (North 24 Parganas, West Bengal), a few hours before the start of the seventh and final phase of voting for the Parliamentary elections.

On 19 May 2019, a BJP candidate was pelted with stones by suspected TMC workers in Park Circus in Kolkata city (Kolkata, West Bengal), during the seventh and final phase of voting for the Parliamentary elections. The cameraperson of a local news channel was injured.

On 19 May 2019, a TMC MP and candidate staged a protest outside the police station in New Town/Rajarhat city (North 24 Parganas, West Bengal), during the seventh and final phase of voting for the Parliamentary elections. She claimed that Central forces were intimidating voters and chanting the slogan Jai Shri Ram.

On 19 May 2019, BJP and TMC workers clashed and hurled bombs in Kakinara area under Bhatpara area (North 24 Parganas, West Bengal), during the seventh and final phase of voting for the Parliamentary elections. Police resorted to baton charge and Rapid Action Force was deployed.

On 19 May 2019, two BJP workers were assaulted by TMC workers in Sagar area (South 24 Parganas, West Bengal), while they were returning to their homes at night. The incident occurred during the seventh and final phase of voting for the Parliamentary elections.

On 19 May 2019, the houses of three BJP activists were attacked at Gosaba area (South 24 Parganas, West Bengal), during the seventh and final phase of voting for the Parliamentary elections. TMC supporters retaliated and damaged houses of two BJP activists.

On 19 May 2019, BJP local leaders attacked the car of a TMC panchayat leader in Kultala area in Habra under Barasat Constituency area (North 24 Parganas, West Bengal), during the seventh and final phase of voting for the Parliamentary elections.

On 19 May 2019, a Trinamool office was vandalized and 10-12 people were injured in a clash between two groups of TMC activists in the Maniktala area in Kolkata city (Kolkata, West Bengal), during the seventh and final phase of voting for the Parliamentary elections.

On 19 May 2019, a clash took place between supporters of the BJP and Trinamul near a booth over alleged intimidation of voters, in Tiljala area of Kolkata city (Kolkata, West Bengal), during the seventh and final phase of voting for the Parliamentary elections.

On 19 May 2019, BJP supporters staged a protest on NH31 in Madaripur village in Islampur area (Uttar Dinajpur, West Bengal), seeking security to cast their votes for the bypolls of the Parliamentary elections. After they lifted the protest, they were attacked by suspected TMC workers, who hurled crude bombs at the polling booth and highway. A group of journalists was also attacked (VAC coded as a separate event).

On 19 May 2019, a group of BJP workers attacked a Congress's Seva Dal meeting in South Tripura district (Tripura). The attack occurred during the seventh and final phase of the Parliamentary elections in the country.

text: On 19 May 2019, villagers clashed with paramilitary troopers in Sashan village (North 24 Parganas, West Bengal), during the seventh and final phase of voting for the Parliamentary elections. They claimed the troopers were threatening locals to cast their votes for BJP. One of the villagers suffered multiple fractures.

On 19 May 2019, a youth was beaten up by locals people after he attacked several persons and damaged vehicles parked on the road at Garanga Tiniali village (Golaghat, Assam). The youth was mentally disturbed after having cleared the Teacher Eligibility Test (TET) seven years ago, but with no offer of employment.
On 19 May 2019, a Quick Response Team was attacked in Haroa area (North 24 Parganas, West Bengal), during the seventh and final phase of voting for the Parliamentary elections.

On 19 May 2019, at least hundred voters ghearoed the Nirvachan Bhawan and staged a protest in Itanagar city (Papum Pare, Arunachal Pradesh), demanding re-poll of the State Assembly and Parliamentary elections in the Rakso polling station. They claimed they were deprived of their voting rights through booth capturing and use of force during the fresh polls held on April 27.

On 20 May (assumed), Congress workers demonstrated at the Government Girls College in Bhodia Khera village (Fatehabad, Haryana) after they saw a truck of EVMs entering the location. There have been several demonstrations after polling to oppose an alleged ploy to tamper with votes.

On 20 May 2019, villagers locked the government school and raised slogans against the Education Department in Bodiwala village (Fatehabad, Haryana) to oppose the Class X exam results. The demonstrators demanded the transfer of the school's headmaster.
On 20 May 2019, parents demonstrated outside the Government High School in Kutubpur village (Kaithal, Haryana) to oppose the poor Class X results.

On 20 May 2019, police personnel were attacked with stones by up to 70 villagers in Roopraka village (Palwal, Haryana) when they tried to arrest a murder suspect. A police officer received head injuries and a police vehicle was damaged.

On 20 May 2019, relatives of a woman who was found dead and residents raised slogans against the police and demonstrated outside the Moga rural police station in Ghall Kalan village (Moga, Punjab). The demonstrators demanded that a murder case be made against the woman's husband.

On 20 May 2019, in Kandamakuntla in Tuggali mandal (Kurnool, AP), a clash occurred between two groups over drawing of water resulting to the death of a woman. The source did not mention weapons used in the clash.
On 20 May (assumed), villagers demonstrated at the police station in Thathiya locality (Ambedkar Nagar, Uttar Pradesh) after a man died shortly after being released from police custody.

On 20 May 2019, ten students were injured after they were assaulted by a group of 15-20 persons at the Bhagwant Institute of Technology in the Mirapur area (Muzaffarnagar, Uttar Pradesh). The assault is believed to be connected to student rivalry.
On 20 May 2019, unspecified party members demonstrated again in Domariyaganj town (Siddharth Nagar, Uttar Pradesh) after they alleged that EVMs were being changed in the strong rooms.
On 20 May 2019, residents of several villages assaulted BDO in Rajgir (Nalanda, Bihar) and smashed the electronic voting machine and his car while boycotting polls over lack of basic amenities.

On 20 May 2019, voters pelted stones at voting booths in Ekauna village of Barhara block (Bhojpur, Bihar) over claims of bogus voting. Government Railway Police's (GRP) Assistant and home guard trooper were injured in the stone pelting.

On 20 May 2019, residents of Paliya village of Sanwer Tehsil (Indore district, Madhya Pradesh) staged a 'chakka-jam' protest on the Indore-Ujjain highway demanding immediate arrest of the perpetrators of the killing of a senior BJP worker.

On 20 May 2019, about 350 local villagers from Bhama Askhed and adjoining areas staged a protest in front of the district collector's office in Karanja Vihire of Khed Tehsil (Pune district, Maharashtra), demanding the removal of police pickets posted in their villages.
On 20 May 2019, members of the PGI Employees Union held a black flag demonstration march in Sector 17 in Chandigarh city (Chandigarh) to press for pending demands including cadre review among others.

Assumed on 20 May, in Belagavi city (Belgaum, Karnataka), farmers of Mudalagi and Gokak Taluk formed a human chain and blocked the roads at Kittur Rani Chennamma Circle and marched to the Deputy Commissioner's office demanding the government to stop the release of water from Hidkal Reservoir to Krishna River.

On 20 May 2019, in Bengaluru (Bengaluru Urban, Karnataka), two groups clashed over taking the lead for the upcoming village festival preparations in KHB Colony, Tilaknagar. One person was killed and another one injured after they were stabbed by the rival group.

On 20 May 2019, near Payyanur in Taliparamba tehsil (Kannur, Kerala), unidentified rioters hurled crude bombs at a house of a voter (KJ Shalet) and a UDF and Congress polling agent (VTV Padmanabhan) for the by-elections at Pilathara. No one was injured but properties were damaged. Congress workers alleged that the attack was done by CPM supporters.

On 20 May 2019, about 450 resident doctors at the Hindu Rao went on strike and sat on dharna at the hospital in Delhi-New Delhi (NCT of Delhi). The demonstrators opposed the non-payment of salaries on time among other demands.

On 20 May 2019, in Puducherry, the youth wing volunteers of the BJP (BJYM) staged a protest at Avvai thidal Saram against an MNM by-elections candidate over his remarks about Naturam Godse as a Hindu and the first extremist of India when he assassinated Mahatma Gandhi.

On 20 May 2019, striking lawyers staged a protest and shouted slogans against the police in (assumed) Amritsar city (Punjab) after a lawyer was assaulted by an ASI the previous day. The demonstrators demanded strict action against the ASI.

On 17 April 2020, locals held a protest in Mango suburb of Jamshedpur city (East Singhbhum, Jharkhand) against a district administration team who went on a survey for coronavirus cases in the area.

On 18 April 2020, prisoners of Jalpaiguri Central Correctional Home (Jalpaiguri district, West Bengal) attacked the jail officials with bricks and pelted stones when they were asked to maintain government guidelines of maintaining social distance inside the prison due to coronavirus pandemic. The prisoners started the clash demanding they be released on bail immediately. Deployment of police and RAF later controlled the situation.

On 18 April 2020, 70-odd inmates of Jalpaiguri correctional home (Jalpaiguri district, West Bengal) staged a demonstration by locking all entrances leading to a block of the correctional home and detained five wardens and 11 sweeping staff demanding immediate release on bail as they fear the spread of the coronavirus inside the prison.

On 18 April 2020, unidentified assailants attacked and assaulted non-local migrant workers in various places of Dimapur town (Dimapur district, Nagaland), as revealed by video clips circulated on social media. Although the reason of the attack was not reported it is suspected to be related to the fear of spread of coronavirus.

On 18 April 2020, local tea garden labourers attacked a team of police personnel in Rangapara town (Sonitpur district, Assam) and injured one of them for initiating a lathi charge on several labourers earlier. Police had to open blank fire to control the situation.

On 18 April 2020, leaders of 17 Left parties including CPI(M), wearing masks and maintaining social distancing, stood holding placards along Red Road in Kolkata city (Kolkata district, West Bengal) to protest on various issues, including the lack of coronavirus testing, improper distribution and black-marketing of ration supplies in the State.

On 18 April 2020, a group of 7 youths allegedly violating the lockdown order of the government amid coronavirus epidemic attacked and assaulted two journalists in Siliguri city (Darjeeling district, West Bengal) while they were reporting coronavirus lockdown measures in various parts of the city.
On 18 April 2020, health workers and pharmacists boycotted work and protested in the rural areas near Amritsar (Punjab) demanding better safety and protection kits to deal with coronavirus.
On 18 April 2020, a large number of migrant labourers staged a protest in Mandi Gobindgarh (Punjab) against World Wide Foods Private Limited demanding pay and food during the coronavirus lockdown.

As reported on 18 April 2020, four men took the stick of a police officer and assaulted him in Ahmedabad city (Ahmedabad, Gujarat) as the officer was about to book them for violating the coronavirus lockdown.

As reported on 18 April 2020, locals attacked police officer in Raghopur block (Vaishali, Bihar), while he was inquiring about a group of people who had been violating the coronavirus lockdown orders.
On 18 April 2020, sanitary workers attacked a YSRCP leader in Kakinada city (East Godaveri, AP) due to the leaders alleged negligence about the bat menace in the area.

On 18 April 2020, police preventively arrested several people protesting at Srinagar city (J&K) who were demanding shifting of quarantined students in Rajasthan amidst the lockdown due to outbreak of coronavirus.

On 18 April 2020, members of two groups clashed with each other using sharp-edged weapons and stones, in Ludhiana (Punjab), after a mob attacked a vegetable vendor the previous day, for allegedly charging exorbitant prices during coronavirus. 7 injured.
On 18 April 2020, a mob of local residents attacked a government doctor, in Meerut (UP), who lived in their neighbourhood asking him to vacate over fears of him spreading coronavirus.
