text: On 18 April 2020, a mob of about 100 people assaulted two personnel of India Reserve (IR) Battalion at Zomuantlang (Mamit district, Mizoram) while they were keeping a vigil along the Mizoram-Tripura border in the wake of coronavirus pandemic.

As reported on 18 April 2020, local residents of Top Khongnangkhong under Khurai Assembly staged a sit-in-protest at Imphal (Imphal East district, Manipur) against the alleged non-receipt of rice under National Food Security Act (NFSA) as assured by the state chief minister during the first phase of 21-day-long lockdown amid coronavirus pandemic.

On 18 April 2020, villagers kidnapped and assaulted block development officials in the Kuakhia village (Jajpur, Odisha), who were enforcing the coronavirus lockdown measures. They were rescued later. Eight people were arrested the next day over the incident.

On 18 April 2020, many migrant labourers held a protest in the industrial areas of Sachin in Surat city (Surat, Gujarat) demanding that they should be allowed to go to their native places during the coronavirus lockdown. Police convinced them to end the protest.

On 18 April 2020, BJP workers and locals held a protest in Bengaluru city (Bengaluru, KN) against the shifting of members of a religious group under quarantine and suspected of having coronavirus to their neighbourhood.
On 18 April 2020, a JD(S) MLC and four others held a protest in Mandya city (Mandya, KN) against the coronavirus testing of journalists.
As reported on 19 April 2020, a mob of around 6 people attacked a civilian with rods and sticks, in Chandigarh city, for reasons unreported. 6 people booked.
On 19 April 2020, a mob of shop keepers clashed with the police in Ferozepur (Punjab) while police were attempting to close down shops violating the lockdown imposed to prevent coronavirus.

On 19 April 2020, private doctors held a protest at SVP hospital in Ahmedabad city (Ahmedabad, Gujarat) against keeping them with coronavirus symptomatic patients, while they had also tested positive.

On 19 April 2020, relatives of a patient who died of coronavirus vandalized medical equipment and assaulted health workers at a quarantine ward in a hospital in Malegaon town (Nashik, Maharashtra), angry about the death of their relative.
On 19 April 2020, two families clashed with swords, knives, scythes and iron pipes in Malia village (Morbi, Gujarat) over a land property dispute. One person died and four were injured.

On 19 April 2020, eight persons attacked a police officer with iron rods at Baronda border post in Sonahatu police limits (Ranchi, Jharkhand), after some of them had been questioned about riding on the same bike during the coronavirus lockdown. They were arrested 3 days later.

On 19 April 2020, locals held a demonstration in Bengaluru city (Bengaluru, KN) as health workers attempted to take 58 secondary contacts of a coronavirus positive patient to quarantine centres. Rioters attacked health workers and the policemen and destroyed pandals. Next day at least 54 people were arrested over the incident.
On 19 April 2020, a man was beaten up by 10 locals in Gidi town (Hazaribagh, Jharkhand) on the suspicions of being a child lifter, while on his way to another town. Four people were arrested.

On 20 April 2020, nurses and health workers, who were attending to a coronavirus patient, staged a protest in Ghaziabad (UP), demanding that they be tested for coronavirus as they came in contact with the patient.

On 20 April 2020, a mob clashed with another group, in Killi Boda Village, near Ferozepur (Punjab), who were trying to restrict entry of outsiders to their village during the coronavirus outbreak. 1 killed, 1 injured. 6 booked.

On 20 April 2020, around 100 Arthiyas (commission agents) staged a protest from their rooftops by banging pots and pans and raising slogans in Uchana, Jind (Haryana) against direct payment to farmers, demanding the state government revert to the system in which money is routed through them.

On 20 April 2020, around 300 villagers staged a blockade at Basirhat-Malancha road in Kaharpara (North 24 Parganas district, West Bengal) to protest against the local panchayat for not providing them with rations despite the state government's assurance of the same during the ongoing lockdown amid coronavirus pandemic.

On 20 April 2020, a group of villagers with sticks beat up three men travelling in a pick-up vehicle in Bhamaiya village in Godhra Taluka (Panchmahal, Gujarat) on the suspicion that they were 'thieves'.
On 20 April 2020, residents clashed with police in Dholpur district (Rajasthan), as officers were trying to enforce the coronavirus lockdown. Four people were arrested.

On 20 April 2020, around 60 residents held a protest outside the Central Hospital in Gandhinagar city (Gandhinagar, Gujarat) against setting up of an isolation ward for coronavirus positive patients. Police dispersed the demonstrators.

On 20 April 2020, employees of National Engineering Works in Gamharia Industrial Area held a protest at the factory gate in Jamshedpur city (East Singhbhum, Jharkhand), demanding payment dues pending since last March.

On 20 April 2020, a man was shot by armed residents in Khajekala police area of Patna city (Patna, Bihar), after he advised them to maintain social distancing during the coronavirus lockdown. He died of injuries a day later.

On 20 April 2020, workers at a prison led by head warden held a protest in Chennai city (Chennai, TN) demanding safety equipment for staff members to prevent the spread of coronavirus while visiting the quarantine blocks.

On 20 April 2020, at least close to 50 local residents held a demonstration against the burial of a coronavirus positive doctor in Chennai city (Chennai, TN). Rioters attacked hospital staffs including doctors and the ambulance.

On 20 April 2020, family members and residents held a protest in Sattenapalle town (Guntur, AP) against the death of a local who had been beaten up by the police for violating the coronavirus lockdown.
On 20 April 2020, Kranti Dal protested at Jammu city (J&K) against the PHE department over not ensuring smooth supply of water.

On 20 April 2020, three Gujjar community members engaged in stone pelting at a police and village defence committee member at Ramgarh sector area (Samba district, J&K) over being stopped during the lockdown due to breakout of coronavirus. Both of them were injured in the attack.

Around 20 April 2020, residents and police clashed in Raghogarh town (Guna, Madhya Pradesh), as the former had gathered to watch a leopard stranded in a well and were in violation of the coronavirus lockdown.
On 21 April 2020, CITU members demonstrated on the rooftops and outside houses, in Dehradun (Uttarakhand) demanding that labourers be given financial assistance during coronavirus.

On 21 April 2020, CITU members staged a protest by holding placard and sloganeering on rooftops and outside their houses, in Shimla (Uttarakhand) demanding that labourers be given financial assistance and rations during coronavirus.

On 21 April 2020, a mob attacked an Accredited Social Health Activist (ASHA) worker in Faridabad (Haryana) while she was conducting door to door surveillance and collecting information about coronavirus cases. 5 policemen who intervened were also attacked. 3 people including 2 policemen and the ASHA worker, injured. 5 people arrested.

On 21 April 2020, a mob attacked police and pelted stones at them in Saharanpur (UP), as the police team went to arrest a person accused of assaulting a farm owner and his wife who objected to them defecating in their area. 2 policemen injured. 1 arrested.
On 21 April 2020, a mob of around 3-4 youth attacked the police in Ludhiana (Punjab) while he caught them violating the lockdown imposed to prevent coronavirus transmission.
On 21 April 2020, a clash occurred over a property dispute where two groups attacked each other with sticks in Jamalpur Kalan village of Kankhal, Haridwar (Uttarakhand). Several injured.

On 21 April 2020, members of the Anganwadi Mulajazam Workers Union, staged a protest by holding posters and raised slogans from their rooftops, in Tarn Taran (Punjab), demanding better wages and insurance especially during coronavirus.

On 21 April 2020, a group of 12 youths attacked a police team at Chanchal (Malda district, West Bengal) when the latter tried to enforce the lockdown protocol amidst coronavirus pandemic. The police later arrested one of the alleged attackers.

On 21 April 2020, members of at least five Left organisations including CITU, DYFI, SFI, All India Democratic Women Union and others staged protests with placards in their hands from inside their homes across Assam demanding more steps to contain the spread of coronavirus and reduce people's woes. They also submitted a memorandum to Assam chief minister through e-mail.

On 21 April 2020, a man was stabbed by four unknown assailants in Bapunagar area of Ahmedabad city (Ahmedabad, Gujarat), over an argument when he advised them to remove a barricade at the gate of his residential society during the coronavirus lockdown.

On 21 April 2020, members of the Centre of Indian Trade Unions and left-backed trade outfits protested from their balconies in Bokaro district (Jharkhand), demanding government relief and food and shelter for migrants, among others amidst the coronavirus lockdown.

On 21 April 2020, members of the Centre of Indian Trade Unions and left-backed trade outfits protested from their balconies in Chatra district (Jharkhand), demanding government relief and food and shelter for migrants, among others amidst the coronavirus lockdown.

On 21 April 2020, dozens of residents from Sarasdangal village held a protest at Dumka-Rampurhat road in Dumka town (Dumka, Jharkhand), saying they had not received their dry food ration from the government during the coronavirus lockdown.

On 21 April 2020, members of the Centre of Indian Trade Unions and left-backed trade outfits protested from their balconies in Hazaribagh district (Jharkhand), demanding government relief and food and shelter for migrants, among others amidst the coronavirus lockdown.

On 21 April 2020, five migrant workers staying in a quarantine centre assaulted teachers with sticks and stones in Nokha village of Jaisalmer district (Rajasthan), as the latter criticized them for hunting protected birds and stopped them from cooking the meat, as the laborers were out of food during the coronavirus lockdown. The laborers were arrested.

On 21 April 2020, residents pelted stones from a building at police in Sadar Bazar area of Jodhpur city (Jodhpur, Rajasthan), who were searching for a woman, during the coronavirus lockdown. Two people were arrested and one officer was injured.

On 21 April 2020, members of All India Kisan Sabha protested from their balconies in Rahe village (Ranchi, Jharkhand), demanding government relief for farmers and payment of pending wages, among others amidst the coronavirus lockdown.

On 21 April 2020, members of All India Kisan Sabha protested from their balconies in Sonahatu town (Ranchi, Jharkhand), demanding government relief for farmers and payment of pending wages, among others amidst the coronavirus lockdown.
On 21 April 2020, contract labourers held a protest at a government hospital in Karur city (Karur, TN) as they have not been paid in the last two months.
On 21 April 2020, members of the Youth Congress held a protest at the toll bridge in Salem city (Salem, TN) against toll collection. Police used force to disperse the protesters, injuring one.

On 21 April 2020, CITU activist and farmers groups held a protest in Srikakulam city (Srikakulam, AP) against the loss of livelihood of 2.6 lakh workers amidst the coronavirus outbreak in the country.

On 21 April 2020, members of the CITU and AITUC held protests in various parts of Tirupati city (Chittoor, AP) demanding the government take action to help unorganized sector workers amidst the nation-wide coronavirus lockdown.
Around 21 April 2020, laborers of a mill took to the streets to protest in Burhanpur district (Madhya Pradesh) due to non-availability of water since four days.

Around 21 April 2020, a large number of RSS cadres held a protest in Kharwali village (Dhar, Madhya Pradesh) demanding immediate action for the accused of the death of a local RSS leader and his nephew.

On 22 April 2020, health workers, paramedics, under the banner of UP Lab Technician's Association (UPLTA) of Lady Lyall Hospital and SN Medical College (SNMC) staged a protest in Agra (UP) demanding better safety and protection gear for health workers during coronavirus.

On 22 April 2020, occupants of a coronavirus quarantine facility (assumed Muslim) staged a protest in Sultanpuri, Delhi - Saraswati Vihar (North West Delhi, Delhi), over the death of a 50-year-old diabetic man in quarantine (he had participated in the Tablighi Jamaat congregation), accusing the authorities of not providing medical attention and food on time.

On 22 April 2020, a mob clashed with the police and pelted stones at them, in Aligarh (UP), as the police intervened in a local scuffle at the vegetable market, and tried to enforce the lockdown imposed to prevent coronavirus transmission. 1 policeman injured.

On 22 April 2020, a mob of 15 people attacked a doctor working in the coronavirus ward of a local hospital in Pinjore town, Panchkula (Haryana). Reason for the attack not reported, but assumed to be due to the fear of the doctor spreading coronavirus in the area.

On 22 April 2020, kin of a victim, along with nearly 50 residents, staged a protest in Aligarh (UP) against police brutality which led to the death of a vegetable vendor for violating the coronavirus lockdown even though he was providing 'essential' services.

On 22 April 2020, a group of villagers assaulted and stoned police personnel injuring four of them at Baduria (North 24 Parganas district, West Bengal) when police personnel enforcing the lockdown amid the coronavirus pandemic asked them to lift their road blockade in the area.

On 22 April 2020, a group of villagers staged a protest by blocking a road at Baduria (North 24 Parganas district, West Bengal) demanding relief and food material from the state government amidst the coronavirus lockdown.
On 22 April 2020, two groups of people clashed with each other at Balarampur (Purulia district, West Bengal) over distribution of free rations amidst the ongoing lockdown due to coronavirus pandemic.

On 22 April 2020, a mob assaulted a ration dealer at Balarampur (Purulia district, West Bengal) for failing to provide the quantity of food grain promised by the state government amidst the ongoing lockdown due to coronavirus pandemic.

On 22 April 2020, a mob lynched two persons at Aathiyabari (Baksa district, Assam) and burnt their house over harassing local people in the area. The deceased were earlier imprisoned for attacking some people without any reason and were released due to the lockdown amid coronavirus pandemic.

On 22 April 2020, few people who had returned from Bengal attacked an ASHA health worker, a government worker, and a local sarpanch in Jajpur district (Odisha), as they advised them to stay in a coronavirus quarantine facility.

On 22 April 2020, three men were attacked by a dozen assailants in Gadhadaka village of Jamjodhpur taluka (Jamnagar, Gujarat) over a political rivalry, as one of them was a brother to the village sarpanch. One man succumbed to his injuries a day later.
As reported on 22 April 2020, four persons attacked police personnel in Nasvadi town (Chhota Udepur, Gujarat), while the latter were enforcing coronavirus lockdown measures.

On 22 April 2020, members of a family attacked a team of police and physicians in Sheopur town (Sheopur, Madhya Pradesh), as they requested to test for coronavirus a member of their family, who had returned from Guna. One officer sustained a head injury.
On 22 April 2020, a group of women held a protest in Coimbatore city (Coimbatore, TN) demanding the supply of drinking water.

On 22 April 2020, a group of people held a protest in a locality in Dindigul city (Dindigul, TN) against the poor supply of essential goods and their high prices amidst the coronavirus lockdown in the country.

On 22 April 2020, members of the BJP and Congress held a protest in Madappally village (Kottayam, KL) against the PDS (public distribution system) shop owners for diverting free food kids to Community Party of India (Marxist) offices.
On 22 April 2020, residents of Mangalam village (Tiruppur, TN) held a protest against the police for detaining youth suspected of violating the coronavirus lockdown in the country.
On 22 April 2020, as many as 12 Dalit villagers held a protest in a Muthandipalayam village near Palladam town (Tiruppur, TN) against being denied a burial ground.

On 22 April 2020, doctors silently staged a protest at Srinagar city (J&K) against the administration for sacking a doctor who asked standard accredited gear for combating the outbreak of coronavirus.
On 22 April 2020, journalists protested and sat on dharna at Udhampur city (J&K) over the mishandling of their colleague by the police force amidst the lockdown due to breakout of coronavirus.

On 23 April 2020, a mob of more than 100 people attacked the police by pelting stones at them in Panipat (Haryana) as the police tried to enforce the lockdown imposed to prevent coronavirus transmission in a Muslim dominated area. 1 injured.

On 23 April 2020, a mob of youths attacked a policeman in Lucknow (UP) while he caught them violating the lockdown imposed to prevent coronavirus transmission. FIR's registered against 5 identified and 10 unidentified individuals.

On 23 April 2020, around 300 women staged a protest at Kashung Bungdung village (Ukhrul district, Manipur) and stopped around 200 Assam Rifles troops along with the paramilitary forces from crossing the village, reportedly to raid NSCN-IM hideouts in the border villages. The women stopped the forces to avoid any unwanted incidents to take place, especially during the ongoing lockdown amid coronavirus pandemic.

On 23 April 2020, local residents of Top Khongnangkhong under Khurai Assembly staged a protest in Imphal (Imphal East district, Manipur) against distribution of less quantity of rice under Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY). The PMGKAY promised provision of five kilograms of rice/wheat free of cost to each individual as part of relief measures for people during the nationwide lockdown amid coronavirus pandemic.
As reported on 23 April 2020, locals pelted stones at police in Sardarnagar area of Ahmedabad city (Ahmedabad, Gujarat) as officers were enforcing the coronavirus lockdown. 15 people were detained.

On 23 April 2020, a family assaulted an ASHA health worker and his family at their home in Balasore town (Balasore, Odisha) in disagreement over collecting details on coronavirus cases in the Niliabag containment zone.
On 23 April 2020, students from Bihar held a silent protest in Kota city (Kota, Rajasthan), demanding to return home, as they had been stuck in a coaching hub during the coronavirus lockdown.

On 23 April 2020, nearly 35 truck operators protested and blocked the national highway at Kargil city (Ladakh) to demand equal share in ferrying of essential commodities amidst the lockdown due to outbreak of coronavirus.
On 23 April 2020, more than 400 cleaners protested at Srinagar city (J&K) against the administration for not releasing their salaries for the past five months.

On 23 April 2020, over 500 people, gathered at Noorani Masjid area for a funeral procession, clashed with police in Malegaon town (Nashik, Maharashtra), refusing to abide by the coronavirus lockdown orders.

On 24 April 2020, a mob of Muslims attacked the police in Baundi village, Bahraich district (UP) as the police prevented them from offering prayers to prevent coronavirus transmission and enforced the lockdown. 32 arrested.
On 24 April 2020, a group of 3 men attacked a policeman near Manesar (Haryana) while the latter was trying to enforce the lockdown imposed to prevent coronavirus transmission. 3 booked.

On 24 April 2020, local villagers attacked and pelted stones at police and forest department personnel injuring one police officer and some staff in Macheng village at Mantripukhri area in Imphal city (Imphal West district, Manipiur). Police resorted to firing tear gas shells to disperse the villagers who were demonstrating against the eviction drive amid the coronavirus lockdown.

On 24 April 2020, a large number of local women residents staged a road blockade and torch rally at Honpei village (Ukhrul district, Manipur) protesting against the entry of IRBN and Assam Rifles personnel to Kashung Budung village reportedly to raid NSCN-IM hideouts in the border villages. The women stopped the forces to avoid any unwanted incidents to take place, especially during the ongoing lockdown amid coronavirus pandemic.

On 24 April 2020, about 60 Muslims, who had gathered at a mosque, pelted stones at police in Mandro Bazar locality under Thakur Gangti police limits (Godda, Jharkhand), as the latter attempted to disperse their gathering during the coronavirus lockdown. One constable was injured.

On 24 April 2020, more than 100 rioters pelted stones at police at Drabgam village (Pulwama district, J&K) when police tried to stop them from congregating for Friday prayers amidst the lockdown due to coronavirus outbreak.

On 24 April 2020, residents held a protest at a village in Supaul district (Bihar) against corrupt practices during ration distribution meant for people affected by the lockdown due to coronavirus epidemic.
On 25 April 2020, medical and sanitation staff staged a protest in Firozabad (UP) demanding better safety and protection gear for health workers during coronavirus.

On 25 April 2020, members of 16 farmer, labour and student unions, including BKU, staged a protest from their rooftops across Punjab, against the government accusing it of mismanagement during coronavirus.
On 25 April 2020, farmers staged a protest in Bhodiwala village, Moga district (Punjab), against the government's failure to ensure wheat procurement.

On 25 April 2020, three people suffered critical injuries during the clash of two groups in Jamalpur area of Ahmedabad city (Ahmedabad, Gujarat) in a dispute over opening the gate of a locality for Muslims to go out during Ramzan amidst the coronavirus lockdown.

On 25 April 2020, a man was beaten to death with sticks and rods by seven or eight persons in Angai village (Dholpur, Rajasthan) on suspicion of having an affair with a minor related to one of the accused. The man died 5 days later in hospital of his injuries.
On 25 April 2020, residents pelted stones at police personnel at Dehgam village in Jambusar taluka (Bharuch, Gujarat), who were trying to enforce the coronavirus lockdown. Five people were arrested.

On 25 April 2020, Rashtriya Lok Samta Party (RLSP) chief and his supporters staged a sit-in protest at a library in a village in Patna district (Bihar) to present a seven-point charter of demand before the government, including ensuring return of students and migrant workers stranded outside due to coronavirus lockdown, extending ration to poor people and resolution of problems of striking teachers.

On 25 April 2020, a mob assaulted autorickshaw drivers and damaged vehicles in Yerawada area of Pune city (Pune, Maharashtra) in an argument, during which one driver spat in disdain against the mob. 1 person was arrested and 12 more booked.

On 25 April 2020, five Congress leaders, including an MP staged a protest in Pathanamthitta city (Pathanamthitta, KL) against the government for leaving Keralites stranded in different parts of the world amidst the coronavirus crisis.

On 25 April 2020, members of the Congress staged a protest in Thiruvananthapuram city (Thiruvananthapuram, KL) against the government for leaving Keralites stranded in different parts of the world amidst the coronavirus crisis.
On 25 April 2020, a youth, suspected to be mentally unstable, was beaten up by locals in Silao police area of Patna city (Patna, Bihar), who suspected him to be infected by the coronavirus.

On 26 April 2020, hundreds of locals staged a protest in Allahabad city (UP) against setting up a coronavirus quarantine center in the area.

On 26 April 2020, leaders of BJP staged a sit-in protest at their respective residences in Cooch Behar town (Cooch Behar district, West Bengal) accusing the State government of hiding the seriousness of the coronavirus crisis in the state by reducing the figure of the total positive cases. They also alleged that they were not allowed to step outside to provide rations and other relief material to the masses.

On 26 April 2020, leaders and activists of BJP carried out a 'demonstration at home' event in West Bengal to protest against the alleged atrocities on party leaders and workers in the state during the ongoing lockdown amid coronavirus pandemic.

On 26 April 2020, several party leaders carrying posters, staged a protest organized by BJP state unit president Dilip Ghosh outside his residence at Salt Lake in Kolkata city (Kolkata district, West Bengal) alleging that the state government is trying to hide the real figures of coronavirus patients and not providing enough protection to medics dealing with the cases.

On 26 April 2020, a group of 10-12 people armed with sharp-edged weapons attacked and killed a daily wage labourer at Safala village under Nilambazar police station (Karimganj district, Assam) allegedly over a land-related dispute. Police later arrested ten persons in this connection.

On 26 April 2020, a group of people staged a protest at Umkdait in Nongmynsong (East Khasi Hills district, Meghalaya) holding placards and banners alleging discrepancies in the distribution of rations during the ongoing lockdown amid coronavirus.
On 26 April 2020, a man was tied to a tree and beaten to death by a mob in Bhanda village (Udaipur, Rajasthan) on the suspicion of theft. Eight people were arrested.

On 26 April 2020, a mob of 50 people raised slogans against the police and assaulted a police team patrolling in Govandi town (coded to Mumbai Suburban - Kurla, Maharashtra), who attempted to disperse them during the coronavirus lockdown. One officer was hospitalized with injuries.

On 26 April 2020, members of various tribal groups held a protest in Polavaram village (West Godavari, AP) demanding only tribal people should be recruited for teacher posts in tribal areas as per the GO No.3.
On 26 April 2020, a youth was assaulted with bamboo sticks by locals in the Khandakpur locality of Patna city (Patna, Bihar), as they suspected him to be infected by the coronavirus.

On 14 May 2020, hundreds of migrant laborers pelted stones at police on a highway in Bijasan village (Barwani, Madhya Pradesh), after discovering there were no more buses to return to their home states during the coronavirus lockdown. No injuries reported.
On 14 May 2020, migrant laborers from Bihar held a protest in Gandhidham city (Kachchh, Gujarat), demanding to return home during the coronavirus lockdown. Police booked 4 of them later.
On 14 May 2020, migrant laborers beat up a person at Katihar town railway station (Katihar, Bihar), while he/she received food ration before them during the coronavirus lockdown.

On 14 May 2020, three policemen sustained injuries after a mob of around 15-20 people attacked a patrolling police party with sharp weapons in Antop Hill area in Mumbai city (Mumbai City, Maharashtra), as police questioned them about violation of the coronavirus lockdown and social distancing. 15 people were booked.
Around 14 May 2020 (as reported), migrant laborers in quarantine held a protest in Muzaffarpur district (Bihar), alleging lack of basic facilities during the coronavirus lockdown.
Around 14 May 2020 (as reported), migrant laborers in quarantine held a protest in Nawada district (Bihar), alleging lack of basic facilities during the coronavirus lockdown.

Around 14 May 2020 (as reported), 92 migrants came out of their quarantine camp from Nawalpur village (Pashchim Champaran, Bihar) and marched to Yogapatti police station, protesting insanitary conditions, alleging that 25 of them were kept in a room without masks, sanitisers or soaps during the coronavirus lockdown.

On 14 May 2020, villagers held a protest in Patharpada village in Oupada block (Balasore, Odisha) against the return of a tribal woman who had just given birth at a hospital in Soro town, fearing she might spread the coronavirus.
Around 14 May 2020 (as reported), migrant laborers in quarantine held a protest in Saharsa district (Bihar), alleging lack of basic facilities during the coronavirus lockdown.
Around 14 May 2020 (as reported), migrant laborers in quarantine held a protest in Sitamarhi district (Bihar), alleging lack of basic facilities during the coronavirus lockdown.

On 14 May 2020, dozens of locals demonstrated outside the house of a deceased civilian and pelted stones at the police in Beerwah city (Budgam district, J&K) after a person was earlier shot by CRPF personnel for allegedly jumping check posts.
Around 14 May 2020 (as reported), locals protested at Jammu city (J&K) over illegal sand mining.
Around 14 May 2020 (as reported), rioters pelted stones at police party in Jammu city (J&K) when police came to stop illegal sand mining.

On 14 May 2020, police lathi charged protesting women of Chuchot Yogma village at Leh city (Ladakh) when they raised slogans demanding their relatives, who were returning to Ladakh, be sent directly to their homes rather than being kept in coronavirus quarantine centres. Four women were injured in the incident.
On 14 May 2020, a protest was held in Quepem town (South Goa, Goa) against the rash driving and heavy movement of trucks from Colomb mine.

On 14 May 2020, migrant laborers at a coronavirus quarantine center attacked a local mukhiya (village body head) and held a nurse hostage in Araria district (Bihar), angry about the living conditions at the center.

On 14 May 2020, more than 100 migrant workers at a coronavirus quarantine centre staged a protest in Raniganj town (Araria, Bihar), demanding proper food, soap and masks and alleged that authorities were ignoring them after they were quarantined.
On 14 May 2020, hundreds of migrant workers staged a protest in Sendhwa town (Sendhwa, Madhya Pradesh), demanding food and transport arrangements to go back home during the coronavirus lockdown.

On 14 May 2020, a mob of 50 villagers assaulted a couple in Vilad village (Ahmednagar, Maharashtra), who had recently moved to a house in the village and were digging a hole for a toilet, while the locals suspected they used the hole for human sacrifice. Police rescued the couple.

On 15 May 2020, a group of people attacked and pelted stones at a police team at Beckbagan area of Kolkata city (Kolkata district, West Bengal) when the latter went to the locality following reports that a man armed with a dagger was trying to attack neighbors. Although no specific reason of the attack is reported, Police arrested eight persons in this connection.
On 15 May 2020, Dalit labourers under the banner of Dehati Mazdoor Sabha staged a protest in Bathinda (Punjab) alleging faulty and biased distribution of rations during coronavirus.
On 15 May 2020, doctors and medical staff staged a protest at the Civil Hospital in Tarn Taran (Punjab) against the locking of two medical officers in the isolation ward with coronavirus patients.

On 15 May 2020, Punjab State Power Corporation Limited (PSPCL) and the Punjab State Transmission Corporation Limited (PSTCL) employees, staged a protest in Ludhiana (Punjab) against the MNC, Teleperformance India and PSPCL officials who left a worker when he was electrocuted and sustained severe burns.
On 15 May 2020, migrant labourers, led by the Zameen Prapati Sangharash Committee staged a protest near Ghabdan village, on the Sangrur-Bhawanigarh road, Sangrur (Punjab) against delays in salaries.
On 15 May 2020, shopkeepers, led by YAD and Business Bachao Morcha, staged a protest and conducted a march in Ludhiana (Punjab) demanding permission to open shops during coronavirus.
On 15 May 2020, lawyers staged a protest in Hyderabad city (Hyderabad, TS) demanding financial assistance for all needy lawyers during the nationwide coronavirus lockdown.
On 15 May 2020, scores of migrant workers held a protest in Mangaluru city (Dakshina Kannada, KN) demanding to be sent back to their hometowns amidst the coronavirus lockdown.

On 15 May 2020, vendors at a market in Panaji city (North Goa, Goa) protested against police action being taken against them to remove them from the weekly market citing concerns about lack of social distancing being observed in the market during the ongoing coronavirus pandemic.
On 15 May 2020, 84 farmers staged a protest in Theni town (Theni, TN) demanding to be sent back to their hometown amidst the nationwide coronavirus lockdown.

On 15 May 2020, members of the Youth Congress staged a protest in Wadakkanchery town (Thissur, KL) demanding home quarantine for a local minister who had welcomed Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) at a coronavirus quarantine centre. Police arrested and removed the protesters.

On 15 May 2020, around 400 migrant laborers took out a protest march in Botad town (Botad, Gujarat), demanding to return home during the coronavirus pandemic. Police convinced the protesters to wait for travel confirmation and the protest ended peacefully.
On 15 May 2020, around 150 migrant laborers pelted stones as police, who used tear gas, near Dahej village (Bharuch, Gujarat), demanding to return home during the coronavirus lockdown.

On 15 May 2020, demonstrators belonging to Muslim community pelted stones at the police forces and the CRPF who used tear gas to stop the rioters in Pulwama district (J&K) over congregating for prayers amidst the lockdown imposed due to coronavirus outbreak.

On 15 May 2020, rioters pelted stones at police and CRPF who fired with pellet guns in Qaimoh area (Kulgam district, J&K) during the enforcement of the lockdown amidst coronavirus outbreak. Five civilians passing by in the area were injured.
On 15 May 2020, security guards started a sit in protest in Kurnool city (Kurnool, AP) demanding payment of pending salaries. The sit in is still ongoing as of 29 May 2020.

On 15 May 2020, police led a cane charge when inmates at a coronavirus quarantine center protested at Dhalwas Dhaino village (Ramban district, J&K) over inadequate supply of water. Three protestors sustained minor injuries.
On 15 May 2020, villagers staged a protest at Pihanagadia village in Balasore district (Odisha), after a couple returned to the village from Surat without staying at a coronavirus quarantine centre.

On 15 May 2020, a brother and sister were killed in a clash with stones and knives between neighbors in Prem Nagar area of Bhind town (Bhind, Madhya Pradesh), as one of the families blamed a person from the other of violating quarantine during the coronavirus lockdown. Six people were arrested after the incident.

On 15 May 2020, nearly 400 migrant workers at a coronavirus quarantine center assaulted a Block Development Officer and vandalized the center in Ladania block (Madhubani, Bihar), alleging that they were served stale rice.

On 15 May 2020, more than 100 migrant workers at a coronavirus quarantine centre staged a protest for a second day on a road in Raniganj town (Araria, Bihar), demanding proper food, soap and masks and alleged that authorities were ignoring them after they were quarantined.

On 15 May 2020, thousands of migrant labourers, mostly from Jharkhand and Uttar Pradesh, who have been trying to get back to their home states during the coronavirus lockdown, staged a protest on the national highway at Satna town (Satna, Madhya Pradesh), after the administration offered them no help and unseasonal showers left them stranded on roads.

On 16 May 2020, members of the All East Kameng District Students' Union (AEKDSU) took out a massive bike rally in Seppa (East Kameng district, Arunachal Pradesh) demanding a permanent additional deputy commissioner (ADC) for the headquarters of East Kameng district and filling up vacancies of nearly 60 head and admin-rank officers in the district.

On 16 May 2020, local residents of Rajganj Belakoba area staged a protest outside a ration shop at Belakoba (Jalpaiguri district, West Bengal,) accusing the dealer of over charging for rations during the ongoing coronavirus lockdown. Police intervened and brought the situation under control.

On 16 May 2020, supporters of Lourembam Sanjoy, projected contender of the upcoming By-Election of Andro Assembly Constituency, staged a mass protest at various area of Andro (Imphal East district, Manipur) shouting slogans against his detention at Porompat Police Station.
On 16 May 2020, a mob of demonstrating migrant workers clashed with the police in Bathinda (Punjab) demanding to be sent to their home states during the coronavirus lockdown.
On 16 May 2020, silk farmers held a protest at the Bengaluru Mysuru highway in Ramanagara city (Ramanagara, KN) against the reelers boycott of the auctioning of cocoons.
On 16 May 2020, BJP's farmer wing BJP Kisan Morcha protested at Jammu city (J&K) against in charge of police post at Chinore accusing him of backing bovine smugglers and demanded action against him.

On 16 May 2020, local residents staged a protest in Kalimpong town (Darjeeling district, West Bengal) demanding institutional quarantine for a mother and her daughter after they arrived in the town from Calcutta. The locals fear that the duo might carry the coronavirus and spread the infection.

On 16 May 2020, local residents staged a protest in Siliguri town (Darjeeling district, West Bengal) demanding institutional quarantine for 114 students after they arrived in the town from Andhra Pradesh. The locals fear that the students might carry the coronavirus and spread the infection.

On 16 May 2020, around 300 migrant labourers clashed with the police and pelted stones, in Karera Khurd village, Yamunanagar (Haryana), demanding that they be sent back to their home states during the coronavirus lockdown.

On 16 May 2020, residents staged a protest in Bir (Himachal Pradesh) against the district administration's decision to host doctors treating coronavirus cases in a hostel as many old people live nearby.

On 16 May 2020, members of the SDPI staged protests in Ukkadam and Athupalam in Coimbatore city (Coimbatore, TN) under the slogan 'lockdown politics'. Police filed cases against 35 SDPI members over the protest for violating the coronavirus lockdown.

On 16 May 2020, more than 50 nurses held a protest at the Dharmapuri district government medical college and hospital in Dharmapuri city (Dharmapuri, TN) demanding the hospital set up retiring rooms for them on hospital premises.
On 16 May 2020, hundreds of villagers held a protest in Telagarahalli village (Bengaluru Urban, KN) against the arrival of coronavirus quarantined passengers.
On 16 May 2020, people at a coronavirus quarantine center protested at Jammu city (J&K) over inadequate arrangements.

actor2: Police Forces of India (2014-) Central Reserve Police Force
text: On 16 May 2020, locals pelted stones at CRPF police, who lathi-charged them and fired rubber pellets in Hindpiri area of Ranchi city (Ranchi, Jharkhand) over a trivial issue. The clash escalated after police personnel assaulted a former ward counselor of the area after he challenged the police action.

On 16 May 2020, police cane charged migrant workers squatting on a highway in Chakghat area of Rewa district (Madhya Pradesh), who demanded food and water, as they were refused from entering Uttar Pradesh and returning home during the coronavirus lockdown.

On 16 May 2020, a mob (assumed belonging to General caste) hurled casteist slurs and assaulted three Dalits including two women while Dalits were demonstrating in Shergadh village of Keshod taluka (Junagadh, Gujarat), against the sinking of a water stream in their area. The rioters molested one of the women during the incident. 14 persons were booked.

On 17 May 2020, around 12,000 migrant workers staged a protest on the Ambala highway, near Tilakhni village in Saharanpur (UP), alleging police torture at a shelter home and demanding they be sent home during the coronavirus lockdown.

On 17 May 2020, a mob of around 1000 migrant workers set fire to a garbage dump and blocked a road near Raipura Jat, on the Agra-Mathura highway (UP), demanding that they be sent back to their homes during the coronavirus lockdown.

On 17 May 2020, migrant workers staged a protest and blocked a part of the Kanpur-Lucknow Highway, near Jajmau, a suburb in Kanpur (UP) demanding that they be sent back to their homes during the coronavirus lockdown. Police intervened in the protest and used lathis to disperse the protesters.

On 17 May 2020, 150 migrant workers staged a protest, at the Shambhu border to Uttar Pradesh, at Shambhu, Patiala (Punjab) demanding to be sent to their respective home states during the coronavirus lockdown.

Around 17 May 2020, Nepalese citizens staged a protest in Sonauli area between the India-Nepal border, near Maharajganj (UP), demanding they be allowed entry in Nepal as they finished their mandatory quarantine for coronavirus.
On 17 May 2020, migrant workers held protests in 3 parts of Chennai city (Chennai, TN) demanding trains to be sent back to their home towns amidst the coronavirus lockdown.
On 17 May 2020, a protest was held in Kallupallam village near Tiruvarankulam village (Pudukottai, TN) demanding the local liquor shop be shifted.
On 17 May 2020, people protested at Budgam district (J&K) over inadequate arrangements at a coronavirus quarantine center.

On 17 May 2020, AIKS members protested at Salehar village (Jammu district, J&K) alleging that the package announced by the Prime Minister was not enough to benefit the marginal farmers in the rural areas.
On 17 May 2020, unidentified rioters hurled a petrol bomb at the place of worship of the Hindu community in Srinagar city (J&K). Police is investigating the issue.

On 17 May 2020, migrant workers assaulted police personnel and a TV journalist and vandalized private vehicles in Shapar-Veraval area of Rajkot city (Rajkot, Gujarat), as their trains to return home were rescheduled during the coronavirus pandemic. Four police officers and a journalist were injured. 29 migrant workers were arrested and about 200 others were booked.

actor2: Police Forces of India (2014-) Central Reserve Police Force
text: On 17 May 2020, locals clashed with CRPF police for a second day in Hindpiri area of Ranchi city (Ranchi, Jharkhand) as police asked them to follow social distancing rules during the coronavirus lockdown.

Around 17 May 2020 (as reported), four people assaulted a nurse in Lambayat area of Surat city (Surat, Gujarat), preventing her from going to a private hospital where she worked in fear that she would spread coronavirus. The four people resided in the same housing society as the nurse.

On 18 May 2020, members of the Centre of Indian Trade Unions (CITU) observing 'Demand Day' staged protests across Assam raising various demands like providing security to workers willing to return to Assam from other States (during coronavirus), and to pay compensation of INR 1 million to the next of the kin of such workers if they die during their journey back home among others.

On 18 May 2020, a group of 15 members belonging to different Centre of Indian Trade Unions (CITU) affiliated organizations observing 'Demand Day' staged protest at Kaliapani Chariali in Doomdooma (Tinsukia district, Assam) raising various demands like providing security to workers willing to return to Assam from other States (during coronavirus), and to pay compensation of INR 1 million to the next of the kin of such workers if they die during their journey back home among others.

On 18 May 2020, contractual workers of the BSNL staged a protest outside the BSNL office at Siliguri Hospital More (Darjeeling district, West Bengal) demanding payment of their wages which is pending for the past year. They also alleged that no solution was provided despite the administration notified for the same during the ongoing lockdown amid the coronavirus pandemic.

On 18 May 2020, a group of fishers tried to attack the fishery department officials at Numaligarh (Golaghat district, Assam) during a drive against illegal fishing. Due to timely intervention by police, the officials were rescued.

On 18 May 2020, students of Maharaja Bir Bikram University staged protests in Agartala (West Tripura district, Tripura) expressing unhappiness with their marks following the declaration of the results.

On 18 May 2020, members of Wancho Council, Wancho Cultural Society, Wancho Students' Union, Longding District Students' Union and All Wancho Women Welfare Association took out a protest rally in Itanagar town (Papumpare district, Arunachal Pradesh) demanding justice for the killing of a civilian by the Indian Army at Pumao village in Longding district earlier on May 16.

On 18 May 2020, members of the Women Welfare Organization (WWO) staged a protest march at Seppa town (East Kameng district, Arunachal Pradesh) against the inaction of the police in arresting the accused involved in a rape incident at Sunrise Residential School in the locality. They demanded the closure of the school and action against the principal.

On 18 May 2020, women of Lambung Village staged a sit-in protest in the village (Chandel district, Manipur) demanding the state government arrest those involved in the shooting incident that occurred at Chandel on May 14 in which two women were injured.

On 18 May 2020, at least 50 residents and members of various community-based organizations headed by the Wancho Council staged a rally in Longding town (Longding district, Arunachal Pradesh) to protest against the killing of a civilian and injury to six other civilians in Pumao village by the 19th Sikh Regiment on 16 May. They also submitted a memorandum to the Longding deputy commissioner's office demanding justice for the deceased and those injured.

On 18 May 2020, farmers and labourers staged a protest in Bathinda (Punjab) against the new discharge policy of coronavirus patients, which allows patients to go home if they are asymptomatic for 3 days, as it puts family members at risk.

On 18 May 2020, a former BJP minister along with AAP workers staged a protest at Raj Ghat, Delhi - Darya Ganj (Central Delhi, Delhi), demanding migrant workers be sent home and be provided transportation during the coronavirus lockdown. Police intervened and arrested few protesters including Sinha and an AAP MP.

On 18 May 2020, a mob attacked the police and pelted stones at them, in Kaachi Colony, in Dhanas, Chandigarh, following a rumour that a paralytic patient died as he was not allowed to cross a police check post because of the coronavirus lockdown. 4 booked, 1 policeman injured.

Around 18 May 2020, migrant workers staged a protest and shouted slogans in Jhansi (UP), demanding that they be sent back to their home states during the coronavirus lockdown. Police intervened in the protest and resorted to a lathi-charge.
On 18 May 2020, members of the SFI held a protest in Madurai city (Madurai, TN) demanding class X board exams only be held after the coronavirus lockdown ends.
On 18 May 2020, members of the CPI(M), DYFI and AIDWA held a protest in Madurai city (Madurai, TN) demanding the closing of a liquor shop in the area.
On 18 May 2020, members of the CPI(M) held a protest in Srikakulam city (Srikakulam, AP) demanding the withdrawal of the hike in power tariff.
On 18 May 2020, about 50 people held a protest in Telagarahalli village (Bengaluru Urban, KN) at a coronavirus quarantine facility against the poor hygienic conditions in the facility.
On 18 May 2020, members of the UDF held a protest in Thrissur city (Thrissur, KL) against the medical board's decision to send UDF leaders in home quarantine over the fear of coronavirus.
On 18 May 2020, employees of the Tangedco staged a protest in Tiruchirappalli city (Tiruchirappalli, TN) demanding the government not to privatise power distribution.
On 18 May 2020, members of a farmers union held a protest in Tiruchirappalli city (Tiruchirappalli, TN) demanding compensation for crops that perished during the coronavirus lockdown.
On 18 May 2020, members of the CPI(M) held a protest in Visakhapatnam city (Visakhapatnam, AP) demanding the withdrawal of the hike in power tariff.

On 18 May 2020, members of the CITU held a protest in Visakhapatnam city (Visakhapatnam, AP) against the termination of outsourced workers in public transport, and demanded job security and payment of wages during the ongoing lockdown over coronavirus.

On 18 May 2020, people of Jambani village attempted to assault Mayurbhanj Collector and stormed his office in Baripada town (Mayurbhanj, Odisha), demanding a DNA test of a newborn in connection with a baby swapping case at PRM Medical College here. 8 people were arrested.
On 18 May 2020, 15 coal workers held a protest outside the premises of a mining company and burnt effigies in Jharia town (Dhanbad, Jharkhand) against privatization in the coal sector.
On 18 May 2020, over a dozen BJP members protested at Jammu city (J&K) against China and demanded boycott of Chinese products in the country.
On 18 May 2020, people lodged in quarantine centre at Jatwal town (Samba district, J&K) blocked Jammu-Pathankot National Highway over delay in their coronavirus test results.
On 18 May 2020, people protested at Kathua city (J&K) over lack of basic facilities at coronavirus quarantine center.

On 18 May 2020, J&K central non-gazetted electrical employees union protested at Samba city (J&K) against the failure of the government to regularise daily workers working in the department for the past 15 to 25 years.
On 18 May 2020, ambulance workers protested at Shopian city (J&K) over police high-handedness against an ambulance driver the preceding day.
On 18 May 2020, local residents protested at Udhampur city (J&K) over opening of a quarantine centre in the residential area that could put them at risk of contracting coronavirus infection.

On 18 May 2020, over 250-300 migrant workers employed at the IIM Ahmedabad site in Vastrapur area vandalised office property, government vehicles and assaulted police personnel and other workers in Ahmedabad city (Ahmedabad, Gujarat), demanding that they be allowed to return home during the coronavirus lockdown. 35 of them were arrested.

On 18 May 2020, the Communist Party of India (CPI) staged a protest in Bhubaneswar city (Khordha, Odisha) against rise in petrol and diesel prices due to increased rate of Value Added Tax (VAT), imposed by both the Centre and the State Government.

On 18 May 2020, the Communist Party of India (CPI) staged a protest in Cuttack city (Cuttack, Odisha) against rise in petrol and diesel prices due to increased rate of Value Added Tax (VAT), imposed by both the Centre and the State Government.
On 18 May 2020, around 150 locals gathered to protest at Ghatkopar area (coded to Mumbai Suburban - Kurla, Maharashtra) against the setting up of a coronavirus quarantine centre near Cama Lane.

On 18 May 2020, a mob torched vehicles and pelted stones at police outside a police station in Mohangarh village (Jaisalmer, Rajasthan), demanding police to hand over to them culprits involved in the murder of a youth in a dispute between two villages regarding inappropriate behavior.

On 18 May 2020, police lathi-charged villagers over staging a protest near the Gohaldihi railway station under Sadar police limits (Kalahandi, Odisha) against a mining project, due to which they had lost their land. 10 villagers were injured.

On 18 May 2020, two groups of villagers clashed in Mohangarh area (Jaisalmer, Rajasthan), over an eve teasing case. Following the clash one of the members of a group was mowed down and killed by two members of the second group. The two members surrendered to the police.

On 19 May 2020, members of the Assam State council of Communist Party of India (CPI) staged protests in Guwahati city (Kamrup Metropolitan district, Assam) demanding immediate action to facilitate transportation of migrant workers and for alleviating the suffering of the needy sections of society during the ongoing lockdown amid coronavirus pandemic.

On 19 May 2020, members of the SFI Kharibari Local Committee staged a demonstration at Kharibari (Darjeeling district, West Bengal) raising various demands including waiver of school/college fees and arrangement of mid-day meals during the lockdown period amid coronavirus pandemic. They also submitted a memorandum to the Block Development Officer in this connection.

On 19 May 2020, local residents staged a protest and surrounded the health department officials at the Siliguri Ward No. 4 Municipality Primary Health Center in Siliguri town (Darjeeling district, West Bengal) after a swab collecting glass box was spotted in the Health Center. The locals fear that such an initiative can spread coronavirus in the locality. Police arrived and 'brought the situation under control.'

On 19 May 2020, a group of people lynched and killed a man inside a night shelter in Kolkata city (Kolkata district, West Bengal) for allegedly charging money from the family of a cancer patient, claiming to provide a lifesaving drug. Police arrested three persons in this connection.

On 19 May 2020, local villagers in large numbers staged protest in Morangi Gaon (Golaghat district, Assam) against alleged corruption of the officers and workers of Morangi Gaon Panchayat under Morangi Development Block in the district. The villagers demanded an enquiry into the alleged corruption. Police reached the spot and 'controlled the situation.'
On 19 May 2020, doctors, nurses and paramedical staff of Civil Hospital staged a protest in Ludhiana (Punjab) against the poor quality of masks and safety equipment provided to prevent coronavirus.

On 19 May 2020, the UP Congress chief and Congress workers staged a protest in Uncha Nangla area near Agra (UP) at the UP-Rajasthan border demanding that migrant workers be provided buses to be sent back home during the coronavirus lockdown. The UP Congress chief was dragged away from the protest by police.
On 19 May 2020, a clash between two groups involving stone pelting and sticks occurred in the Sachendi suburb of Kanpur (UP) over a land dispute.
On 19 May 2020, members of the TDP, BJP and JSP held protests in various parts of Chittoor district (Chittoor, AP) against high power bills amidst the coronavirus crisis.

On 19 May 2020, migrant workers and members of the CITU staged protests in 60 places in Coimbatore district (Coimbatore, TN) demanding for trains to go back to their home state amidst the coronavirus lockdown and change in labour laws.

On 19 May 2020, cinema theatre employees part of the CITU staged a protest in Hyderabad city (Hyderabad, TS) demanding implementation of the GO 45 and requested the government for action against theatre owners over unpaid full wages during the coronavirus lockdown.
On 19 May 2020, members of the TDP, BJP and JSP held protests in various parts of Kadapa district ( Kadapa , AP) against high power bills amidst the coronavirus crisis.

On 19 May 2020, around 200 migrant workers held a protest in Kannur city (Kannur, KL) stating authorities were not treating them well and they wanted to go back to their home states during the coronavirus lockdown.

On 19 May 2020, a group of migrant workers held a demonstration and reportedly had a scuffle with police as well as local residents near Kuttiadi town (Kozhikode, KL) demanding trains to return back to their home state amidst the coronavirus lockdown. Police arrested three of the demonstrators.
On 19 May 2020, a protest was held by beneficiaries of a housing project in Machilipatnam city (Krishna, AP) demanding the end to the legal battle over the grant of housing sites in the area.
On 19 May 2020, BJP and JSP leaders held a protest in Visakhapatnam city (Visakhapatnam, AP) demanding the withdrawal of the hike in power tariff.

On 19 May 2020, members of a retired persons association held a protest in Visakhapatnam city (Visakhapatnam, AP) alleging the Central government did not provide them sufficient compensation for the coronavirus lockdown.
On 19 May 2020, residents pelted stones at police personnel in Indore city (Indore, Madhya Pradesh), after police arrested a man for violating the coronavirus lockdown orders at a burial ground.

On 19 May 2020, rioters pelted stones on a police party in Budhal city (Rajouri district, J&K) that had gone to the Gabbar village when there was a dispute between two groups over water distribution. Three policemen were injured in the stone pelting.
On 19 May 2020, employees of power department protested at Jammu city (J&K) against the privatisation of the power department.
On 19 May 2020, locals protested in Khrew city (Pulwama district, J&K) when Indian security forces demolished dozens of shops and residential houses. Police fired in the air to disperse protesters.

On 19 May 2020, locals protested in Pampore city (Pulwama district, J&K) when Indian security forces demolished dozens of shops and residential houses in Pampore city (Pulwama district, J&K). Police fired in the air to disperse protesters.
On 19 May 2020, scores of demonstrators at different places clashed with police in Srinagar city (J&K) over the news of killing of two HM militants. Many were left injured in the clash.

On 19 May 2020, around 100 INC members staged a sit-in protest at the Rajasthan-Uttar Pradesh border in Bharatpur district (Rajasthan), demanding the entry of over 250 empty buses supposed to bring Rajasthani migrant laborers from UP during the coronavirus lockdown. Scores of them were arrested and the protest was dispersed.
On 19 May 2020, Hajuri community members (OBC group) held a protest in Jaisalmer city (Jaisalmer, Rajasthan) against using Seva Sedan as a quarantine center for coronavirus patients.

On 19 May 2020, villagers set on fire cattle and shops of another group of villagers in Mohangarh village (Jaisalmer, Rajasthan), following the death of a teenager during a conflict over eve teasing issue between the two settlements. 12 people were arrested.

On 20 May 2020, members of All Adivasi Students' Association of Assam (AASAA), Demow Regional Committee staged protest in tea estates under Thowra constituency (Sivasagar district, Assam) against the State Cabinet's decision to extend working hours of labourers from 8 hours to 12 hours during the lockdown period amid the coronavirus pandemic.

On 20 May 2020, members of the CPI staged a sit-in demonstration in front of its Nazira office (Sivasagar district, Assam) protesting against the privatization of the Public Sector Units. They also demanded that adequate protection measures should be provided to the stranded and exploited working class including release of all anti-Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019 (CAA) protesters who are now in different jails among others.

On 20 May 2020, members of the Dimasa Students Union (DSU), All Dimasa Students Union (ADSU) and Dimasa Mothers Association (DMA) launched a sit-in protest in front of the office of the Deputy Commissioner in Haflong (Dima Hasao district, Assam) demanding the immediate suspension and arrest of former Dima Hasao Deputy and other accused, initiation of a CBI inquiry into the matter, and compensation to the family of a businessman who was abducted and killed by unidentified gunmen earlier during the month of April.

On 20 May 2020, BMS and other workers held a nationwide protest, including some in Delhi and Uttar Pradesh, against the unilateral changes in labour laws in 14 states and demanding better conditions for workers during coronavirus.

On 20 May 2020, Congress workers staged a protest in Noida (UP), demanding migrant workers be sent home and against the arrest of 4 Congress workers earlier in the day while they were arranging buses for the workers during the coronavirus lockdown.

On 20 May 2020, hundreds of labourers clashed with the police and pelted stones at them, at Salahpur Majra village in Delhi - Saraswati Vihar (North West Delhi, Delhi), demanding that they be allowed to cross the inter-state border to reach their workplace but the police refused due to coronavirus lockdown restrictions. 5 policemen reportedly injured.

On 20 May 2020, a clash occurred between upper/general caste and Dalit members of Kaidupur village, Nabha, Patiala district (Punjab) over the auction of reserved common land. 3 Dalit people injured. 2 upper caste people booked.

On 27 February 2023, hundreds of farmers associated with BKU (Ekta), staged a protest at Ramsara minor (sub canal) in Abohar city (Fazilka district, Punjab), against the government and Irrigation Department. They opposed the reconstruction of 'moghas' (outlets), that had been reconstructed much above the old level. They claimed that it would deprive them of existing share of water for irrigation.

On 27 February 2023, five sugarcane farmers associated with Bharatiya Kisan Union (BKU) staged a protest and hunger strike in front of Naraingarh Sugar Mill in Banaundi village (Ambala district, Haryana), against the sugar mill administration. They demanded the release of Rs 100 crore in pending payment and transparency in the mill's payment system.

On 27 February 2023, members of the Moozhikkulam forane church of the Syro-Malabar Church (Catholic) staged a protest at the Bishop house's in Ernakulam city (Kanayannur, Kerala) against the appointment of the new vicar of the parish.

On 27 February 2023, students associated with Chhatra Yuva Sangharsh Samiti (CYSS) staged a protest at Panjab University (PU) in Chandigarh city, against the university administration. They demanded the rollback of the proposed 7.5% fee hike in self-financed courses in the varsity. They also demanded the reopening of canteens at the University Institute of Legal Studies, Arts block, and Basic Medical Sciences (BMS) block.

On 27 February 2023, scores of locals led by Dogra Front members held a protest by burning an effigy at Pulwama city (J&K) against a militant attack targeting a Kashmiri Pandit in Shopian district (coded as a separate event) and demanded action against the militants.

On 27 February 2023, DYFI members staged a protest rally in front of the All India Radio office in Thiruvananthapuram city (Thiruvananthapuram district, Kerala) against Prasar Bharati's decision to use Hindustan Samachar as the only official source, claiming that the BJP is trying to control the national media.
On 27 February 2023, farmers held a protest and stalled an auction for half an hour at APMC in Nandgaon town (Nashik, Maharashtra) over the falling wholesale price of onion.

On 27 February 2023, farmers held a dharna (sit-in protest) and stalled the auction for 10 hours at APMC in Lasalgaon town (Nashik, Maharashtra) over the falling wholesale price of onion. The farmers ended the dharna after the guardian minister assured them that he will take up their demands with CM.

On 27 February 2023, hundreds of farmers under the aegis of 'Jay Kisan Andolan' held a protest rally at Sohela town in Sohela block (Bargarh district, Odisha) demanding free electricity for agriculture. The farmers submitted a memorandum to Chief Minister through Sohela tehsildar listing their demands.

On 27 February 2023, locals led by a farmer leader held a protest at Ranbir Singh Pura city (Jammu district, J&K) against the J&K administration over imposing property tax amidst high inflation and unemployment.

On 27 February 2023, members of Tamil Nadu Vivasayigal Sangam, a farmers' association affiliated with the Communist Party of India, staged a protest in Coimbatore city (Coimbatore South, Tamil Nadu) against the discharge of untreated sewage into the Noyyal river.

On 27 February 2023, ex-servicemen staged a protest at Mini Secretariat in Ludhiana city (Punjab), against the government. They demanded the government reinstate them to the Guardians of Governance (GOG) scheme.

On 27 February 2023, hundreds of former military personnel, working under the Guardians of Governance (GoGs) scheme, staged a protest and burned effigies of the ruling party's leaders outside the Deputy Commissioner's office in Fatehgarh Sahib city (Fatehgarh district, Punjab), against the government over the alleged arbitrary termination of their services. They also demanded a meeting with the CM.
On 27 February 2023, a large number of locals and elected representatives held a protest at Lansi town (Udhampur district, J&K) over vandalization of a temple over a land dispute (coded separately).

On 27 February 2023, UDF councillors of the Kochi Corporation staged a protest meeting in front of the Kerala Water Authority's office in Kochi city (Ernakulam district, Kerala) against the corporation's inaction against the pest menace.

On 27 February 2023, members of Rashtriya Gau Raksha Vibhag (Hindu group advocating for cow protection) held a bike rally protest in Unhel city (Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh) demanding strict legal action under the provision of the National Security Act (NSA), 1980 against cow slaughterers after cow carcasses were found. Police were present during the rally to prevent any untoward incident.

On 27 February 2023, INC members staged a protest in Ainapur town (Belagavi, Karnataka) demanding the arrest of the assailants that knife-attacked the INC Kagawad youth block president that same day (coded as a separate event)

On 27 February 2023, IYC members staged a protest in front of Pro Vice Chancellor and Registrar's office at Kannur University in Kannur city (Kerala) against the university's alleged nepotism in employment and appointment processes.

On 27 February 2023, scores of Kashmiri Pandit package employees held a protest outside the relief commissioner's office in Jammu city (J&K) against the killing of a Kashmiri Pandit in a targeted attack by the militants in Shopian (coded as a separate event) and to demand relocation to safer areas in the Jammu region.

On 27 February 2023, hundreds of MPPSC aspirants staged a sit-in protest outside the MPPSCs office in the Indore city (Indore, Madhya Pradesh) demanding the interviews of State Dental Surgeon 2021, State Engineering Examination-2021, State Assistant Management Examination-2021, and State Veterinary Assistant Surgeon 2021 at the earliest.
On 27 February 2023, voluntary retired transport workers held a sit-in protest at Jammu city (J&K) to demand release of their pending dues under the sixth pay commission.

On 27 February 2023, employees of The Tarn Taran Central Cooperative Bank staged a sit-in protest in front of the bank in Tarn Taran city (Punjab), against the bank administration. They demanded the transfer of the bank's district manager.

On 27 February 2023, pourakarmikas (cleanliness workers) held a protest at the BBMP head office in Bengaluru city (Bengaluru Urban, Bengaluru North, Karnataka) demanding all pourakarmikas to become permanent workers.

On 27 February 2023, about 34 railway employees, patients and students held a protest at an airport in Bagdogra city (Darjeeling district, WB) over not being informed about the cancellation of a flight prior to their arrival at the airport.

On 27 February 2023, members of the District Bar Association staged a protest march towards the office of the UT IGP in Chandigarh city, against the registration of an FIR against the former DBA President. The police stopped them around 500 meters before the district courts complex.

On 27 February 2023, Students Federation of India (SFI) members of the Himachal Pradesh University (HPU) staged a protest in front of the VC office at HPU in Shimla city (Himachal Pradesh), against the university administration and government. They opposed the implementation of CBCS (choice-based credit system) for the postgraduate first-year students under the National Education Policy (NEP). They demanded the government roll back the CBCS or implement it again after rectifying the flaws.

On 27 February 2023, members of the Punjab Agriculture University Teachers' Association (PAUTA) staged a protest in front of Thapar Hall of the university in Ludhiana city (Punjab), against the state government over the delay in salary revision under the 7th Pay Commission, and implementation of the 7th UGC pay scale. They also staged a rally at gate No. 1 and blocked the Ferozepur road.

On 27 February 2023, TMC members held a protest in front of booths 54 and 55 in Sagardighi tehsil (Murshidabad district, WB) over claimed favourable disposition of the police towards INC amidst an ongoing by-election to Sagardighi assembly constituency.

On 27 February 2023, TMC members held a protest by blocking a national highway under the Tufanganj police station area coded at Tufanganj city (Cooch Behar district, WB) to demand arrest of suspected BJP members who vandalised TMC flags in Ghogarkuthi Kalibari area (coded as a separate event).

On 27 February 2023, a group of people led by the president of United Akali Dal staged a protest outside the Dayanand Medical College and Hospital (DMCH) in Ludhiana city (Punjab), against the government. They demanded the release of Sikh prisoners who have completed their terms. They also demanded the Hospital discharge a right activist from the hospital after a proper health check-up.

On 27 February 2023, members of the Central Valmiki Sabha (Dalit community group) staged a protest in Fatehgarh Sahib city (Fatehgarh district, Punjab), against the government over the alleged atrocities being committed on the Scheduled Castes (SCs). They also raised several demands, including resolving the pending applications of the SC people with the police and government departments, investigating the employees working with fake SC certificates, and filling the reserved vacant posts for SCs in all departments.
On 27 February 2023, women held a protest at Kathua city (J&K) over lack of water supply in their village and demanded urgent restoration.

On 27 February 2023, villagers held a dharna (sit-in protest) and blocked the Nabarangpur-Koshagumuda road by putting utensils in Beheraguda village under Agnipur Panchayat (Nabarangpur, Odisha) over a shortage of drinking water.

On 27 February 2023, members of the Rourkela Nagarik Suraksha Manch (local citizens' body) took out protest rallies to mobilize public opinion in Rourkela city (Sundargarh district, Odisha) against the move to hand over Ispat PG Institute and Super Speciality Hospital (IPGISSH), a hospital under PSU, to Apollo Hospitals Enterprise Ltd (AHEL).
On 27 February 2023, dozens of patients held a protest by blocking a road at Sopore tehsil (Baramulla district, J&K) against the hospital authorities over the absence of doctors on duty.
On 27 February 2023, scores of locals held a protest at Srinagar city (J&K) against the installation of smart meters in their area as they increase the power bill.

On 27 February 2023, members of Aam Aadmi Party were arrested by state police forces while staging a demonstration in front of the BJP office at Basistha locale in Guwahati city (Kamrup Metropolitan, Assam). They raised slogans against the arrest of Delhi Deputy Chief Minister by the Central Bureau of Investigation on charges of corruption in the Delhi liquor policy case, and demanded his immediate release.

On 27 February 2023, AAP members held a protest in Indore city (Indore, Madhya Pradesh) against the arrest of Delhi's Deputy Chief Minister by the Central Bureau of Investigation in an alleged corruption case. Police arrested AAP members.

On 27 February 2023, AAP members and MLAs staged a protest in Delhi - New Delhi city, against the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) over the arrest of the Delhi deputy chief minister by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) over the alleged irregularities in the formulation and implementation of the now-scrapped excise policy in Delhi. They accused the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) government of using the central agencies to target political rivals. Police detained scores of protesters.

On 27 February 2023, AAP activists staged a protest march in the Ghanta Ghar area in Ghaziabad city (Uttar Pradesh), against the government over the arrest of the Delhi deputy chief minister by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) over the alleged irregularities in the formulation and implementation of the now-scrapped excise policy in Delhi. They had blocked the GT Road which resulted in a long traffic jam. The police resorted to a mild lathi charge to disperse the protesters. The police also detained many protesters.

On 27 February 2023, members of AAP staged a protest outside the BJP office in Bengaluru city (Bengaluru Urban, Bengaluru North, Karnataka) against the arrest of Delhi Deputy Chief Minister. Police detained the protesters.

On 27 February 2023, ABVP members staged a protest in front of the Kakatiya Medical College in Warangal city (Warangal Urban, Khila Warangal, Telangana), demanding legal action against the responsible for the death of medical student undergoing treatment at NIMS hospital. Police stopped and detained the protesters.

On 27 February 2023, AAP workers led by the party leaders and Rajya Sabha (Council of States) MP staged a demonstration at the Haryana BJP headquarters in HUDA Complex in Rohtak city (Haryana), against the government over the arrest of the Delhi deputy chief minister by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) over the alleged irregularities in the formulation and implementation of the now-scrapped excise policy in Delhi. They clashed with the police as they tried to cross the police barriers near the BJP office. The police resorted to a mild lathi charge to disperse the crowd and detained 29 rioters.

On 27 February 2023, villagers held a demonstration and forcibly stopped the personnel from Aurobindo Realty and Infrastructure Pvt Ltd (ARIPL) from restarting work at the Takli-Jena-Bellora coal mine in Belora village under Bhadravati tehsil (Chandrapur district, Maharashtra) demanding that the village land should be acquired at the rate of Rs 50 lakh per acre and rehabilitation of directly affected villages before starting any work. Company officials had a scuffle with the women demonstrators, and police had to intervene and rescue the company officials.

The supporters of the candidate were demanding a re-poll in the constituency, leaading to the clash with paramilitary forces. Three youths and and IRB soldier were injured in the clash.

The two parties threw stones at each other. Police lathi-charged against the rioters. 1 policeman and 3-4 BRS members were injured by the stone throwing.

On 28 February 2023, members of AAP staged a protest in Mysuru city (Mysore district, Karnataka) against the arrest of Delhi Deputy Chief Minister.

On 28 February 2023, twelve Councillors of Sirkazhi Municipality from DMK, AIADMK and DMDK, and an Independent staged a protest at the monthly municipal council meeting in Sirkazhi town (Sirkali, Nagapattinam district, Tamil Nadu) against the late garbage disposal.

On 28 February 2023, members of the Bajrang Dal and other Hindu groups held a protest at Kaman town in Kaman tehsil (Bharatpur, Rajasthan) against remarks by Rajasthan Congress MLA's husband describing the cow vigilantes as ' gundas (goons)'.

On 28 February 2023, members of the BJP led by the former municipal chairman held a sit-in protest in Bhopal city (Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh) after BJP's Vikas Yatra was stopped by the police while it passing through the Bhopal South-West Assembly constituency. The protest ended after a discussion with the collector.

On 28 February 2023, the kin of three CRPF troopers killed in the Pulwama suicide attack four years back along with a BJP MP and MLAs held a protest outside Vidhan Sabha (Assembly) in Jaipur city (Jaipur, Rajasthan) demanding that the state government fulfill the promises made to families of CRPF killed in the Pulwama attack.

On 28 February 2023, farmers under the aegis of Bharatiya Kisan Sangh (BKS) held a dharna (sit-in protest) in Ujjain city (Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh) demanding the release of compensation to hail-hit farmers.

On 28 February 2023, the Biju Mahila Janata Dal (BMJD), the women's wing of the BJD, led by Rajya Sabha MP staged a dharna (sit-in protest) in front of the Raj Bhavan in Bhubaneswar city (Khordha, Odisha) against the plan to discontinue PMAY in the state.
On 28 February 2023, CPI(M) staged a protest in Krishnagiri city (Krishnagiri, Tamil Nadu) against the union budget for cutting social expenditure and prioritizing businesses over the poor.
