On 28 February 2023, scores of farmers held a tractor march and staged a sit-in protest outside Kharkhoda tehsil's office in Karnal city (Haryana), against the government and opposed the amendments in the Land Acquisition Act, 2013. They demanded double compensation for their land, which was being acquired for the railway orbital corridor on the Kundli-Manesar-Palwal (KMP) highway. They also demanded the government declare the KMP as either a state highway or a national highway.

On 28 February 2023, sugarcane farmers staged a protest march from the Gun House Circle towards the Deputy Commissioner's office in Mysuru city (Mysore district, Karnataka) demanding a fair price for their sugarcane sales as well as denouncing the non-payment of FRP by some sugar factories and other issues.

On 28 February 2023, INC members staged a protest outside the residence of an INC MLA, who announced his retirement from politics, in Mysuru city (Mysore district, Karnataka) urging him to reconsider his decision. Two of his supporters attempted to kill themselves.

On 28 February 2023, a large number of Congress workers and residents, led by the former Haryana Deputy Chief Minister staged a protest rally in Panchkula city (Haryana), against the removal of names of poor people from BPL lists in the district.

On 28 February 2023, farmers belonging to the district unit of the Krantikari Kisan Union staged a protest in front of the office of the XEN and Punjab State Power Corporation Limited (PSPCL) in Fatehgarh Sahib city (Punjab), against the power corporation over the erratic and irregular electricity supply from the Chorwala grid.

Around 28 February 2023 (as reported), villagers held a protest and blocked the Indore-Khandwa road in Simrol village under Mhow tehsil (Indore district, Madhya Pradesh) after a laborer was electrocuted to death, demanding financial assistance and a job for the deceased family.

On 28 February 2023, villagers under the aegis of Khuntkati Bikash Manch (KBM) held a protest and blocked the road at Telighana village in Kutra tehsil (Sundargarh district, Odisha) against JSW's SCL plant expansion demanding employment or local area development.

On 28 February 2023, members of different industry bodies in Nashik staged an agitation in front of the district collector's office in Nashik city (Nashik, Maharashtra) to protest against the 37% power tariff hike proposed by the state electricity distribution company.

On 28 February 2023, hundreds of traders held a shutdown, protest march and a sit-in at Katra city (Reasi district, J&K) against the proposed Tarakote-Sanji Chhat ropeway project that may affect their livelihood of local traders.
On 28 February 2023, scores of locals and traders held protest at Kulgam city (J&K) against a militant attack targeting a Kashmiri Pandit in Shopian district (coded as a separate event).
On 28 February 2023, shopkeepers held a protest at Srinagar city (J&K) against the Indian army over closure of their shops in Khrew.

On 28 February 2023, Haibowal shopkeepers staged a protest in Ludhiana city (Punjab), against the government and police over the rising theft cases in the locality. They claimed that the police were not doing anything to stop such incidents.

On 28 February 2023, members of Dehati Mazdoor Sabha staged a protest in front of the office of the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Development) in Tarn Taran city (Punjab), against the government. They demanded payment for the MGNREGA workers.
On 28 February 2023, sanitation workers staged a protest in Mohali city (SAS Nagar district, Punjab), against the government. They demanded the payment of their salary.

On 28 February 2023, a large number of shopkeepers from Mapusa Municipal Council market staged a protest outside Mapusa Municipality office in Mapusa town (Bardez, North Goa, Goa) against the show-cause notices issued to them for subletting their shops.
On 28 February 2023, NCP MLAs held a protest at the steps of the Assembly in Mumbai - Nariman Point city (coded to Mumbai City, Maharashtra) against falling wholesale onion prices.

On 28 February 2023, a large number of displaced persons community members along with its women wing leader, displaced from Pakistan administered Kashmir held a protest by engaging in sloganeering at Jammu city (J&K) to demand distribution of the relief package, issuance of id cards, 12 assembly seats, reservations among other demands and against the J&K administration over conducting the land eviction drive.

Around 28 February 2023 (as reported), members of SFI held protests at Kasaragod Government College in Kasaragod city (Kerala) against the former Principal for not solving the issue of contaminated drinking water in the campus.

On 28 February 2023, family members of a murder victim and students associated with the Sanjha Vidyarthi Morcha staged a protest at the Punjabi University and Government Rajindra Hospital in Patiala city (Punjab), against the police and university administration. They raised questions regarding the law and order situation at the university.

On 28 February 2023, members of the Rourkela Nagarik Suraksha Manch (local citizens' body) took out protest rallies for the second consecutive day to mobilize public opinion in Rourkela city (Sundargarh district, Odisha) against the move to hand over Ispat PG Institute and Super Speciality Hospital (IPGISSH), a hospital currently under PSU, to Apollo Hospitals Enterprise Ltd (AHEL).

BJP councillors manhandled and injured INC councillors, including a woman, during the protest.

On 28 February 2023, hundreds of BJYM members threw eggs, stones, and water packets at the police in Bhubaneswar (Khordha, Odisha) during a demonstration to highlight lawlessness in the state. Police resorted to lathicharge when the demonstrators tried to march towards the state assembly. 21 policemen were injured.

On 1 March 2023, more than 30 Hindu men vandalized a book stall at the World Book Fair organized by The Gideons International, a Christian organization distributing, among other items, copies of the Bible in Delhi - New Delhi city. The rioters accused the volunteers of converting people and forcing others to take the books.

On 3 May 2023, rioters (likely Tribal) attacked the Forest office and clashed with police forces in Phougakchao Ikhai area (Bishnupur, Manipur), demonstrating against Meitei opposition to the pro-Tribal Solidarity March of ATSUM. Police fired rounds of tear gas shells and blank shots, and demonstrators also shot rounds in retaliation and set on fire at least six houses and vehicles including a van, Maruti Alto, Honda Activa and two heavy vehicles (JCB). People on both sides sustained injuries.

On 3 May 2023, members of Tribal community clashed with members of Meitei community and police forces in Moirang town and surrounding villages of Torbung, Bangla, Kangvai (Bishnupur, Manipur) during demonstrations against counter agitations launched against the pro-Tribal Solidarity March of ATSUM. Cases of arson and vandalism of houses, shops and vehicles were also reported from the area. Police Forces clashed with the agitators as they moved village to village, tear gas and blank firing was used by the police, while reports of firing and stone pelting by demonstrators was also noted. Many people from Kaprang, Torbung, Phougakchao Ikhai and over 100 people who were housed at a relief camp set up at Durga Mandop at Saiton have been displaced.

On 3 May 2023, rioters (likely Tribal) vandalised a Forest Beat office in Saikot town (Churachandpur, Manipur). This was after demonstrations were earlier held by the All Tribal Students Union Manipur against the demand for Scheduled Tribe status by Meitei Community. The state High Court had recently passed the order to seek state governments inputs for the demand.

On 3 May 2023, over 100,000 locals, members of Kuki-Zo and Naga tribal groups and members of All Tribal Students Union Manipur clashed with members of the Meitei community and vandalised property while staging a 'solidarity march' demonstration from the Public school at Hiangtam Lamka to Tuibung locale in Churachandpur town (Churachandpur, Manipur) against the demand by Meitei community for Scheduled Tribe status. The Tribal community feels that the ST status will give the Meitei community dominance over state politics as they have a larger population and more representation in the government. Police forces resorted to open fire to control the situation. In Thenra Leirak locality, a mob (likely Meitei) shot and killed two members of the Chin-Kuki-Mizo tribe, and injured another, as they were protecting their village. The injured person was hospitalized with 17 bullet injuries. In Khumujamba Meitei Leikai locality, Kuki men set ablaze several houses and a group of 5-6 Kuki men sexually assaulted and gang-raped a Meitei woman while she was fleeing her house. This case was reported in a 'Zero FIR' on 9 August 2023. In total, around 80 people were injured, 3-5 persons killed, and nearly 5000 people from the Meitei community displaced from the Churachandpur area. Fatalities coded as 3 based on the lowest estimate.

On 3 May 2023, three persons including sarpanch's husband assaulted an (government) agriculture assistant in Beed city (Beed, Maharashtra) for refusing to do illegal work. A hand and a leg of the assistant was fractured due to the assault.

On 4 May 2023, a mob of members of the Meitei community set ablaze multiple houses, vehicles and other property belonging to the Kuki-Zo community, including properties of an ex-Kuki legislators (one from the INC), at multiple localities across Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) as suspected retaliation to escalating violence against the Meitei community in the Hill district areas. In Lamphel area, a mob of Meitei community members, including Meira Paibis, attacked the family of a (female) State Government employee (Kuki), bludgeoning her son and her to death and sexually assaulting her daughter-in-law. In Kakwa Nameirakpam area, a mob of Meitei community members assaulted and killed three individuals. In Khongsai Veng locality, about 2000-3000 locals (likely Meitei) attacked the Christian Church after bulldozing down its gates with JCBs and killed 3 persons (Christian, likely Kuki-Zo)- 2 were lynched while the third was shot dead by a sniper. On RIMS road, a mob of Meitei locals abducted, assaulted and tortured a Kuki-Zo BJP MLA and one of his companions using electric shocks, when they were returning after a meeting with the state Chief Minister regarding the devolving condition of law and order in the state; the driver succumbed to his injuries and died. Police forces tried to disperse the mob using tear gas shells when they were targeting the property of former legislators. In Porompat, a mob of around 40 Meitei men and women barged into a nursing institute hostel, demanding the identification cards of students, and assaulted and seriously injured two female Kuki-Zo nursing students. Women members of the mob exhorted the mob to 'rape' the women. The two women were 'abused', 'tortured' and 'left to die' on the roads until they were rescued by state police. One of the survivors has filed a police complaint under the charge of 'outraging the modesty of a woman'. Additionally, a mob (likely Meitei) of around 800, lynched a 21 year old Kuki who had been in police custody after dragging him out of a police vehicle at Popular High School in Porompat. Police personnel were also assaulted by the mob. Total fatalities 10.

On 4 May 2023, two groups of Kuki Tribe students and Meitei students clashed in Noingrim hills area of Shillong city (East Khasi Hills, Meghalaya) as violence amongst the two communities spread across Manipur. 16 students were arrested by state police forces to make sure the violence does not spread into Meghalaya.

On 14 May 2023, candidates of Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission (UPPSC) staged a protest, raising slogans, at Gramodaya Inter College in Gaurabadshapur Town (Jaunpur, Uttar Pradesh) against the examination centre employees' suspected misbehaviour with the examinees.

Around 14 May 2023 (as reported), many supporters of the SP candidate for local elections staged a protest, raising slogans, in Bewar Village (Bhogaon, Mainpuri, Uttar Pradesh) against claimed electoral fraud.
On 14 May 2023, locals held a protest at Sangoor city (Udhampur district, J&K) over the opening of a liquor store in the area.
On 14 May 2023, villagers staged a protest by blocking the road in Viluppuram district (coded as Viluppuram municipality, Tamil Nadu) after many people died after drinking spurious liquor.

On 14 May 2023, villagers staged a candle light protest march in Delhi - Palam city (Najafgarh, South West Delhi, Delhi) in solidarity with the wrestlers protests in New Delhi, who have accused the Wrestling Federation of India's President of sexual harassment against many women wrestlers including a minor, and an institutional failure to prevent the sexual harassment of women athletes.

On 14 May 2023, a group of residents staged a sit-in protest, raising slogans, in Greater Noida City (Gautam Buddha Nagar, Uttar Pradesh) against Greater Noida Industrial Development Authority (GNIDA) for the delay in provision of services such as road surfacing, footpath construction, and drain cover.

On 14 May 2023, residents staged a protest at Ramprastha City Township, Sector 37D, in Gurgaon City (Gurugram, Haryana) against the Township's developer for the poor quality and inadequate supply of water.

On 14 May 2023, volunteers of Meira Association (Women Torch bearers) staged a sit-in demonstration at Bashikhong Keithel in Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) demanding clarification from gun men who shot at a house in the locality the night before (coded separately).

On 14 May 2023, local residents and members of 26 clubs under the banner of Singjamei Apunba Lup staged a sit-in demonstration at Singjamei Oinam Thingel locale in Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) demanding state government to work on bringing back normalcy to the state amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities across the state.

On 14 May 2023, members of the CPI (M) and the DYFI staged a protest in Batlagundu town (Dindigul, Tamil Nadu) against the Tamil Nadu governor and demanded that the Union government relieve him of his duties for his actions against the DMK led state government. Protesters shouted slogans and held black flags and balloons. Police detained the protesters.

On 14 May 2023, a group of 40-50 farmers and members of AAP waved black flags and staged a protest during the second day of the Haryana Chief Minister's 'Jan Samvad' program in Mandi Dabawali Town (Sirsa, Haryana). The farmers protested against the refusal of their demand to meet the Chief Minister, while AAP members protested against the government's policies. Some protestors, including farmers and AAP members, were detained.

On 14 May 2023, scores of villagers, led by BJP Kisan Morcha leader, staged a demonstration, by blocking the Lucknow-Varanasi highway, burning a truck, pelting stones and bricks at the police and police vehicle, near Kulhanamau Village (Jaunpur, Uttar Pradesh) against the death of two bike-borne youth who were hit and killed by a truck. The police had to use force to control the demonstration, 5 policemen were injured, and damage was done to a police vehicle. The BJP kisan morcha leader on 20 May consumed poison in response to claimed police harassment.

On 15 May 2023, suspected kidnappers took hostage and assaulted an Anti Human Trafficking Unit team in Haldwani City (Nainital, Uttarakhand), who had come to arrest the kidnappers. The team escaped after the intervention of the police, and a case has been registered against 8 people.
On 15 May 2023, locals led by an AAP leader held a protest at Kathua city (J&K) over lack of drainage facility in their area.

On 15 May 2023, wrestlers protesting at Jantar Mantar (Delhi) staged a protest march, along with Bhim Army Chief, to Connaught Place in Delhi - Connaught Place (New Delhi, Delhi) as a step towards making their protest against the sexual harassment of female wrestlers by the Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) President a pan-India movement. This event marks 'Day 23' of the wrestlers protest.

On 15 May 2023, members of the BJP led by a former MLA staged a protest in Puttur town (Dakshina Kannada, Karnataka) after an offensive banner showing the BJP state president and a former Chief Minister was put up on display near the Puttur KSRTC bus stand.

On 15 May 2023, activists of the Bhartiya Janata Yuva Morcha (BJYM), led by its executive committee member, staged a protest in front of the Kotwali Police Station in Meerut City (Uttar Pradesh) against the suspected case of communal conflict where two hijab-clad Muslim women were molested and their Hindu male companion was beaten, on 12 May (coded separately).

On 15 May 2023, about 30 to 50 members of a Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe organisation staged a protest at the Mahatma Gandhi Memorial Hospital in Warangal city (Warangal Urban, Telangana) after an accident victim passed away at the hospital. Protesters raised slogans and used derogatory language against the staff in the casualty accusing them of negligence. Police registered cases against the protesters and the doctors.
On 15 May 2023, Dogra Front and Shiv Sena members joined by fruit sellers held a protest at Jammu city (J&K) against the claimed misbehaviour of municipal commission employees.

On 15 May 2023, members of the Goa Forward Party staged a protest by entering the Junta House building in Panaji city (North Goa, Goa) against officials at the Civil Supplies Department for supplying contaminated rice to ration card holders, and demanded action against the government officials and department responsible for it. Protesters also sang songs accusing the supply of food grains through fair prices shops to be a scam.

On 15 May 2023, hundreds of medical students held a protest at Jammu city (J&K) against a clash between students involving outsiders over sharing a link of a movie (likely the Kerala story) (coded separately).

On 15 May 2023, members of the Hindustan Makkal Sevai Association (Hindu group) staged a protest at the Coimbatore Collectorate in Coimbatore city (Tamil Nadu) asking the state to screen a movie called 'The Kerala Story' in theatres. Protesters also submitted a petition at the Collectorate.

On 15 May 2023, BJP members joined an ongoing dharna (protest), wearing black badges and raising slogans, staged by Congress members and a Congress MLA of Phagwara at the office of the Municipal Commissioner in Phagwara City (Kapurthala, Punjab) against the Municipal Commissioner's suspected use of abusive language with the Congress MLA when he had met her to discuss a local issue.

On 15 May 2023, scores of traders staged a protest in Bhubaneshwar City (Khordha, Odisha) and demanded immediate action against the officials conducting the eviction drive launched by the Bhubaneswar Municipal Corporation (BMC) for misbehavior.

On 15 May 2023, locals and traders held a protest by blocking a road at Sunderbani town (Rajouri district, J&K) over the late arrival of fire brigade and demanded opening of a fire station within the city.

On 15 May 2023, port workers affiliated to various trade unions including the All India Water Transport Workers Federation staged a protest in front of the Old Harbour in Thoothukudi city (Tamil Nadu) with a list of demands including new wages, settling bonuses before the sale of properties, filling vacancies and reintroducing the old pension scheme. Protester raised slogans to press for their demands.
On 15 May 2023, railway hawker union members under INTTUC held a protest at Siliguri city (Darjeeling district, WB) over claimed harassment of hawkers by railway police force.

On 15 May 2023, shopkeepers, residents, and local villagers staged a massive protest near Dugri Police Station in Ludhiana City (Ludhiana East, Punjab) over the failure of successive governments to repair the Dugri-Dhandra Road despite several complaints.

On 15 May 2023, hundreds of players staged a protest at the Sports Authority of India Center in Bhiwani City (Haryana) demanding an increase in athlete seats and the provision of hostel facilities for female players.
On 15 May 2023, members of the SFI staged a protest in front of a corporate college in Hyderabad city (Telangana) against the decision to hold classes during the summer vacation.
On 15 May 2023, members of the VCK staged a protest in Thalavapalli hamlet in Veppanapalli town (Krishnagiri, Tamil Nadu) demanding the allotment of village land to 24 Dalit families.

On 15 May 2023, members of the Vokkaliga (Hindu caste group) community staged a protest in Mysuru city (Karnataka) demanding the INC to announce the Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) president and MLA as the next Karnataka Chief Minister.

On 15 May 2023, people gathered and held a protest at Panwasa police station in Panwasa village (Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh) against those accused of vandalizing vehicles, including a police jeep, and a liquor shop in the village.

On 15 May 2023, a large number of local residents gathered outside the collector's office and held a protest rally in Sardarpur city (Dhar, Madhya Pradesh) demanding construction of a road in Minda village.

On 15 May 2023, members of the Federation of Residents Associations Kerala staged a protest outside the venue of a public hearing organised by the Kerala State Electricity Regulatory Commission in Thiruvananthapuram city (Kerala) demanding the commission to not approve the hike in power tariffs in the state.

On 15 May 2023, residents staged a protest and blocked the road in Yenagunte village (Bengaluru Rural, Karnataka) after an Ambedkar statue was vandalised. Protesters demanded the immediate arrest of the accused.

On 15 May 2023, more than 100 residents of Thalamalai Nagar in Ward 60 staged a protest and submitted petitions to officials at the Collectorate in Salem city (Tamil Nadu) asking the district administration to not open a Tasmac outlet (state government owned liquor outlet) in the locality.

On 15 May 2023, victims who had invested in various schemes offered by a jewellery store staged a protest at the Police Training College in the Mogappair neighbourhood in Chennai city (Tamil Nadu). Protesters accused the company of cheating them and filed a complaint with the police.

On 15 May 2023, locals staged a protest at Thapli Baba Mazar in Ramnagar Town (Nainital, Uttarakhand) over the removal of illegal structures in the forest area under Corbett Tiger Reserve. The police pacified the protestors.

On 15 May 2023, villagers, including family members of the deceased, staged a protest by raising slogans and blocking the Kanpur-Sagar Highway NH-34 near Narayach Village in Maudaha Block (Hamirpur, Uttar Pradesh) against the death of 3 people after a truck hit the bike of the deceased, and demanded that speed breakers be built on the road. The protest concluded after the intervention of the police.

On 15 May 2023, thousands of residents across the city who faced eviction during the demolition drive staged a protest, under the banner of Mazdoor Awas Sangathan Samiti, at Jantar Mantar in Delhi - Connaught Place (New Delhi, Delhi) demanding the government to provide rehabilitation.

On 15 May 2023, members of the Zameen Prapti Sangharsh Committee (local group) staged a protest outside the Deputy Commissioner's office in Patiala City (Punjab) over issues such as allocating one-third of village panchayat lands to members of the Dalit community.

On 15 May 2023, locals along with Meira Paibi (Women Torch Bearers) staged a sit-in demonstration at Langmeidong village (Kakching, Manipur) demanding central government not renew Suspension of Operation agreements with Kuki Militia Groups for their involvement in attacking Meitei community members during the ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities.

Around 15 May 2023 (as reported), locals staged a sit-in demonstration at Khumbong village (Imphal West, Manipur) demanding authorities find two locals who went missing on 6 May 2023 amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal community in the state. The demonstrators were stopped by state police forces when they tried to march to submit a memorandum to the local MLA.

On 15 May 2023, locals staged a sit-in demonstration at Wangkhei in Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) demanding central government not renew Suspension of Operation agreements with Kuki Militia Groups for their involvement in attacking Metei community members during the ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities.

On 15 May 2023, locals staged a sit-in demonstration at Yairipok town (Thoubal, Manipur) demanding central government not renew Suspension of Operation agreements with Kuki Militia Groups for their involvement in attacking Metei community members during the ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities.

On 15 May 2023, members of the BJYM staged a protest in Kochi city (Ernakulam, Kerala) against the Kochi Corporation and accused the administration of being responsible for the waste disposal and management issues persisting in the city. Police used water cannons to disperse the protesters.

On 15 May 2023, a former deputy CM (current INC MLA) and his supporters concluded a 5-day padayatra (protest march) 'Jan Sangharsh Yatra', by marching from Mahapura to Jaipur city (Jaipur district, Rajasthan), against claimed corruption and question paper leaks in the state.
On 15 May 2023, contractual employees of the Numaligarh Refinery staged a demonstration in Numaligarh town (Golaghat, Assam) demanding payment of their due for work done since March.
Around 15 May 2023 (as reported), members of the SFI and the KSU clashed at the Cochin University of Science and Technology (Cusat) in Kochi city (Ernakulam, Kerala) for unknown reasons.

On 16 May 2023, two groups within the TDP supporting two different leaders clashed with each other in G.Kothapalli village (West Godavari, Andhra Pradesh) over intra-party rivalry during the TDP national general secretary's Yuva Galam padayatra. One of the leaders was injured during the clash.

On 16 May 2023, local residents, carrying sticks, rods and sharp objects, attacked a team of Chief Minister's Flying Squad, accompanied by the police and other local government officials, in Islampur Village (Gurgaon, Gurugram, Haryana) when the team visited the area to evict squatters. The team suffered injuries and 6 accused have been booked.

On 16 May 2023, two groups clashed, while throwing stones, at Majra Nagla Mahasukh in Sadabad Town (Hathras, Uttar Pradesh) during a procession celebrating the birth anniversary of Emperor Prithviraj Chauhan. The clash was spurred by an argument over the installation of a board celebrating the anniversary of the Emperor. Many people were injured.

actor2: Police Forces of India (2014-) Indian Reserve Battalion
text: On 16 May 2023, unidentified assailants (likely Kuki-Zo based on the location) pelted stones at a IRB bus on National Highway 37 near the Kuki-dominated Keithelmanbi village (Kangpokpi, Manipur) while the bus was going to pick up IRB personnel from Jiribam, amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and tribal, including Kuki-Zomi, communities in the state.

On 16 May 2023, members of the AIMC staged a 12 hour fast in front of the Secretariat in Thiruvananthapuram city (Kerala) to protest against the attack on a doctor who was stabbed to death and to demand for strict action against the perpetrators.

On 16 May 2023, farmers staged a protest in Peddavoora village (Nalgonda, Telangana) after waiting for days to sell their grain at the purchasing centres and for the lorries to arrive to transport their produce. Farmers threw away the grain and burned it in protest.

On 16 May 2023, farmers belonging to the Amaravati farmers Joint Action Committee staged a protest in Krisnayapalem village (Guntur, Andhra Pradesh) against the changes to the master plan including the decision to allocate houses to the poor in the R5 Zone and the deployment of police personnel. Protesters also raised slogans against the Chief Minister and the state government.
Around 16 May 2023 (as reported), dozens of farmers staged a dharna (protest) in Rajatalab Tehsil (Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh) against claimed arbitrariness of the police administration.
On 16 May 2023, members of the BJP staged a protest by marching to the Kozhikode Corporation office in Kozhikode city (Kerala) against the increase in building permit fees.

On 16 May 2023, members of the Democratic Youth Federation of India (DYFI), led by State President of DYFI, staged a protest march in Mandi City (Himachal Pradesh) demanding that the state government fulfil, in a timely manner, the guarantees that it had given during the assembly elections.

On 16 May 2023, members of the GFP staged a protest in Panaji city (North Goa, Goa) against officials at the Civil Supplies Department for supplying adulterate rice infested with maggots, mites and fungus to ration card holders, and demanded action against the government officials and department responsible for it.

On 16 May 2023, supporters of a INC MLA staged a protest in Bengaluru city (Bengaluru Urban, Karnataka) demanding the INC to appoint their leader who was a member of the Dalit community as the Chief Minister after the Karnataka state assembly elections.

On 16 May 2023, corporators from the INC led by the leader of the opposition staged a protest outside the office of BMC commissioner in Bhopal city (Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh) for not issuing work orders from the corporator's fund.

On 16 May 2023, regular employees of Bhopal Municipal Corporation (BMC) under the aegis of BMC Employees Association held a protest in Bhopal city (Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh) against non-payment of salaries to 4,000 employees.

On 16 May 2023, Siliguri Bidhan Market Byabasayee Samity (trader's organization) held a sit-in protest at Siliguri city (Darjeeling district, WB) in support of various demands including ownership of shops.

On 16 May 2023, members of the Federation of Tamil Nadu All Corporation Employees Association launched a protest in Tiruchirappalli city (Tamil Nadu) against the execution of a government order in urban local bodies which aims to organise employees according to a city's population, which according to the protesters, would be a threat to job security. Protesters distributed pamphlets.

On 16 May 2023, a Congress parliamentary leader in Lok Sabha and a former Member of parliament (Congress leader) joined the wrestlers protesting at Jantar Mantar in Delhi - Connaught Place (New Delhi, Delhi) against the sexual harassment of female wrestlers by the Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) President a pan-India movement. This event marks 'Day 24' of the wrestlers protest.
On 16 May 2023, a large number of locals and traders led by a BJP member held a protest at Jammu city (J&K) against the barricading done by the traffic police at Jewel Chowk.

On 16 May 2023, unemployed members belonging to a Joint Action Committee along with a YSRCP MP staged a protest in front of the office of the Education Commissioner in Hyderabad city (Telangana) demanding the immediate filling up of vacant teacher posts.

On 16 May 2023, members of the District Bar Association, led by its Secretary, boycotted work and staged a protest, by blocking the road, outside the District Court in Ghaziabad City (Uttar Pradesh) demanding the release of an advocate who was arrested for a suspected assault on the police.
On 16 May 2023, members of the Muslim community staged a protest in Gangavathi city (Koppal, Karnataka) demanding that the INC appoint a Muslim INC leader as the Deputy Chief Minister.
On 16 May 2023, supporters of a murdered RJD member (coded separately) held a protest and blocked the Hajipur-Mahnar road (coded as Hajipur, Vaishali, Bihar) demanding action against the culprits.

On 16 May 2023, members of the Shiv Sena (UBT) held a protest rally in Kolhapur city (Kolhapur, Maharashtra) demanding that a case be registered against the previous governor for his alleged role in the toppling of the Maha Vikas Agadhi (MVA) government in June 2022.
On 16 May 2023, as many as 50 women held a protest at Sahapur village (Howrah district, WB) over lack of drinking water supply in their area.
On 16 May 2023, people staged a protest by placing empty earthen pots and other utensils on the road in Bhanjanagar town (Ganjam, Odisha) demanding water.
On 16 May 2023, people staged a protest by placing empty earthen pots and other utensils on the road in Mahabirod village (Dhenkanal, Odisha) demanding water.
On 16 May 2023, people staged a protest by placing empty earthen pots and other utensils on the road in Nilagiri town (Baleshwar, Odisha) demanding water.
On 16 May 2023, locals held a protest at Egra town (Purba Medinipur district, WB) against the bomb explosion at an illegal factory at Egra on the same day (coded separately).

On 16 May 2023, friends and relatives staged a protest by blocking the Puducherry-Tindivanam road in Viluppuram municipality (Viluppuram, Tamil Nadu) after many people died after drinking spurious liquor and demanded a ban on the sale of spurious liquor.

On 16 May 2023, relatives of a woman who died after giving birth to a baby at the Primary Health Centre in Maripeda staged a protest with the deceased's body on the Warangal-Khammam Highway in Maripeda mandal (Mahabubabad, Telangana) accusing the hospital staff of medical negligence.

On 16 May 2023, villagers, including family members of the deceased, staged a protest by blocking the Babatpur-Jamalapur Road in Phulpur Police Station in Varanasi City (Uttar Pradesh) over the death of a man who was killed when a truck hit his bike, leaving his wife and child seriously injured.
On 16 May 2023, villagers staged a protest in Kharoudi Village (Guhla, Kaithal, Haryana) against the Guhla MLA (Jannayak Janta Party) over claimed lack of development.
On 16 May 2023, local residents staged a protest in Gunji Village (Dharchula, Pithoragarh, Uttarakhand) against the felling of trees in the area for an official project by a Indian Army contractor.
On 16 May 2023, a large number of residents staged a protest at Lohar Nangal Locality in Jalandhar City (Jalandhar-I, Punjab) demanding the closure of a newly opened liquor store in the locality.

On 16 May 2023, locals under the aegis of Coordinating Committee on Manipur Integrity (Meitei organization) staged demonstrations at Wangkhei Palace Compound, Sega Road Thouda Bhabok Leikai, Keishamthong Keithel, Keishamthong Top Leirak, Keishamthong Elangbam Leikai, Wangkhei Ayangpali and Haobam Marak Keisham Leikai localities, while members of the Nongmeibung Women Development Meira Paibi Association (Women Torch Bearers) staged a sit-in demonstration at the Multipurpose hall at Nongmeibung locality, in Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) demanding the state government to protect the unity of Manipur and implement the National Register of Citizenship. They also demanded punishment for cadres under Suspension of Operation agreement but violated it amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state.

On 16 May 2023, employees of the Meghalaya Energy Corporation Limited under the aegis of Coordination Committee of Registered MeECL Employees Associations and Unions and Coalition Part of All Unions and Associations staged a sit-in demonstration in Shillong city (East Khasi Hills, Meghalaya) against the government's failure to release their salaries for the month of April.

On 16 May 2023, members of the DVK staged a black flag protest in Palani city (Tamil Nadu) against the Tamil Nadu governor's visit and accused the official of acting against the interests of the state and its people. Protesters wore black shirts and shouted slogans. Police detained the protesters.

On 16 May 2023, hundreds of employees of the Visakhapatnam Steel Plant (VSP) affiliated to the INTUC, CITU, AITUC and the YSRTUC (trade union wing of YSRCP) staged a protest by blocking the roads and laying siege to the plant's administrative building in Visakhapatnam city (Andhra Pradesh) against the union government's decision to privatise the VSP. Police blocked the roads and did not allow the employees into the building leading to a 'brief scuffle' with the protesters.

On 16 May 2023, members of the Zameen Prapti Sangharsh Committee (local group) staged a protest outside the Deputy Commissioner's office in Patiala City (Punjab) over issues such as allocating one-third of village panchayat lands to members of the Dalit community. Some protestors were detained.

On 16 May 2023, a large number of Bajrang Dal and Vishwa Hindu Parishad members staged a demonstration, by raising slogans, outside the Mini-Secretariat in Yamunanagar City (Jagadhri, Haryana) against Ranjitpur police outpost in-charge for suspectedly misbehaving with a villager. The police intervened to stop the demonstrators who tried to forcefully make their way to the office of the Superintendent of Police, leading to a clash with the demonstrators.

On 16 May 2023, villagers, including family members of the deceased, staged a demonstration by throwing stones and blocking the Ramghat Road with the body of the deceased, outside Talaspur Kalan village (Koil, Aligarh, Uttar Pradesh) over the death of teenage boy who died of electrocution when a power line fell on him. The demonstrators demanded compensation and the arrest of officials from the power department. The demonstration concluded after the police both lathi-charged, detained villagers, and, later, assured the fulfilment of their demands.

Around 16 May 2023 (as reported), a large number of villagers staged a demonstration, by throwing stones at the team of Varanasi Development Authority (VDA), in Karnadadi Village (Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh) who had visited the area to demarcate the land for Transport Nagar. The villagers demanded that the land for which compensation has not been paid should not be demarcated. The police lathi-charged and detained a large number of villagers, and several policemen and villagers were injured.

On 16 May 2023, INC members led by a local MLA held a protest outside the municipal office in Sardarpur town (Dhar, Madhya Pradesh) demanding the removal of the chief municipal officer (CMO). The protestors gave a memorandum to SDM Rahul Chouhan threatening to remove CMO within 15 days.

On 17 May 2023, devotees and staff members of a gurdwara (Sikh place of worship) suspectedly assaulted a Sikh man at Kendri Gurdwara Shri Singh Sabha in Rajpura City (Patiala, Punjab) for violating Maryada (a Sikh code of conduct) by entering the gurdwara wearing shoes and with an uncovered head.
On 17 May 2023, villagers lynched and killed a migrant laborer from Odisha in Morbi district (Gujarat) on suspicion of theft. Police arrested seven persons.

Around 17 May 2023 (as reported), three youths pelted stones at the police in Nauranga Bass Rajputan Village (Dadri, Chakhri Dadri, Haryana) when the police arrived after a call regarding a dispute in the area. One police officer was injured, police vehicle was damaged and one accused has been arrested.

On 17 May 2023, four villagers, carrying sticks, assaulted a former District President of AAP in Gopalpur Village (Hathras, Uttar Pradesh) over unidentified reasons. The assailants also broke goods in the house and stole thousands of rupees (Indian currency).

On 17 May 2023, members of ABVP staged a protest at Lucknow University in Lucknow City (Uttar Pradesh) against the University administration for being unable to fulfil demands such as provision of water coolers and sweepers.

On 17 May 2023, farmers affiliated to the Tamil Nadu Vivasaya Sangalalin Kootamaippu led by the All India Kisan Sabha staged a protest in Krishnagiri city (Tamil Nadu) demanding a roll back of the Tamil Nadu Land Consolidation (for Special Projects) Act.

On 17 May 2023, hundreds of grape farmers under the aegis of Swabhimani Shetkari Sanghatana (farmers' group) held a protest march to the district collector's office in Sangli city (Sangli district, Maharashtra) demanding compensation for losses incurred by them due to the steep decline in raisin price. Police stopped the protesting farmers when they tried to break into the collector's office premises.

On 17 May 2023, members of the Andhra Pradesh Vyavasaya Karmika Sangham (agricultural labor union) NTR district committee staged a sit in protest at the office of the District Water and Management Agency (DWMA) in the Gollapudi area in Vijayawada city (Andhra Pradesh) demanding the payment of a summer allowance to workers and an increase in budget allocation and wages. Protesters raised slogans.

On 17 May 2023, a large number of fishers from Vasco staged a protest in front of the municipal council building in Vasco Da Gama city (South Goa, Goa) to demand the administration to ban the illegal trade of wholesale fish vendors.

On 17 May 2023, members of the BJP held a protest and burned the effigy of a local BJD MLA in Kendrapara town (Kendrapara, Odisha) demanding a thorough probe into claims of dowry harassment made by his daughter-in-law.

Around 17 May 2023 (as reported), members of Sakal Hindu Samaj (Hindu group) held a protest in Trimbak town (Nashik, Maharashtra) against a claimed attempt by a group of Muslim youth to 'forcibly' enter the Trimbakeshwar temple premises.

On 17 May 2023, supporters of an INC MLA staged a protest in Belagavi city (Karnataka) demanding the Karnataka Deputy Chief Minister post for their leader. Protesters held placards and shouted slogans.

Around 17 May 2023 (as reported), members of the Class III and IV employees of Vikram University and the National Teachers Union held a protest in the university in Ujjain city (Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh) over their nine-point charter of demands including pension to all retired employees under 7th Pay Commission, appointment of permanent staff to the vacant posts.

On 17 May 2023, members of the Tamil Nadu Cable TV Operators' Federation staged a protest and observed a fast in the Palanganatham area in Madurai city (Tamil Nadu) against the price hike for channels approved by the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI).

Around 17 May 2023 (as reported), a large number of employees, under the banner of Municipal Employees Union, staged a protest, and clapped and banged steel plates, outside the residence of a local MLA (BJP) in Ambala City (Haryana) against the government's lack of initiative in fulfilling their demands.

On 17 May 2023, the protesting wrestlers and supporters, on 'day 25' of their protest, staged a protest march from Jantar Mantar to Bangla Sahib Gurudwara in Delhi - Connaught Place (New Delhi, Delhi) accusing the Wrestling Federation of India's President of sexual harassment against many women wrestlers including a minor, and an institutional failure to prevent the sexual harassment of women athletes.
On 17 May 2023, employees of '108' ambulance service staged a protest in Zirakpur Town (Dera Bassi, SAS Nagar, Punjab) demanding regularisation and improvement in pay and other benefits.

On 17 May 2023, school heads, led by the District President, recruited through the Punjab Public Service Commission (PPSC) staged a dharna (protest) outside the District Education Office in Nawanshahr Municipal Council (Shahid Bhagat Singh Nagar, Punjab) against the delay in clearance of their pay fixation.

On 17 May 2023, several leaders from political parties such as Congress Provincial Unit President, a former SP MP and others, under the banner of Mohansarai Kisan Sangharsh Samiti (KSC), joined the farmers' sit-in protest in Rajatalab Tehsil (Varanasi, Uttar Pradesh) against the Varanasi Development Authority (VDA), district administration and police for trying to take possession of land for Transport Nagar Project.

Around 17 May 2023 (as reported), villagers, led by an advocate and Head of Road Bachao Sangharsh Samiti, staged a protest by banging steel plates, marking 'day 100' of their strike, in Talwandi Rana Village (Hisar, Haryana) demanding the development of a permanent road.

On 26 May 2023, about 400 people under the aegis of Adivasi Ekta Parishad staged a protest in Palghar town (Palghar, Maharashtra) against claimed atrocities towards the Adivasi families in Dhanivari, demanding action against those who forcefully evicted them from their homes.

On 26 May 2023, family members, members of Karni Sena, Rajput organizations, and some other Hindu outfits staged a protest in Udaipur city (Udaipur, Rajasthan) over the death of a person in police custody due to claimed custodial torture (coded in a separate event).
On 26 May 2023, locals held a protest at Kathua city (J&K) against the overflowing of the drainage in the area.
On 26 May 2023, locals held a protest at Saroga village in Bashohli tehsil (coded as Basohli city (Kathua district, J&K) against the power department and demanding a change in the transformer.
On 26 May 2023, members of Bidhan Market Byabasayee Samity (a traders' group) held a protest at Siliguri city (Darjeeling district, WB) to demand ownership of all shops in the Bidhan market.
On 26 May 2023, villagers held a protest by encircling the block development office at Naxalbari town (Darjeeling district, WB) over a stench in the area due to inadequate waste management.

On 26 May 2023, all Bengal electricity consumers association members held a protest rally at Kharibari city (Darjeeling district, WB) against the doubling of fixed charges, price increments, and introduction of prepaid meters etc.

On 26 May 2023, villagers staged a protest outside the house where the Haryana Chief Minister was residing during his visit in Dongra Ahir Village (Mahendragarh, Haryana) against the decision to provide Sihama Village (which is claimed to be smaller than Dong Ahir) the status of a sub-tehsil (sub-division).

On 26 May 2023, farmers from Parasia, Rasulpur and Sonraich villages staged a protest at Panchayat Bhawan in Saraiya Village (Chauri Chaura, Gorakhpur, Uttar Pradesh) against the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) and the government over inadequate compensation for their land which is being acquired for the construction of a four-lane ring road.

On 26 May 2023, farmers, led by the President of Kisan Mazdoor Sangharsh Committee Zone Sultanpur Lodhi, staged a protest in Sherpur Dogran Village (Sultanpur Lodhi, Kapurthala, Punjab) against the officers of District Development and Panchayat Office (DDPO) who had come to remove encroachers from panchayat land. The protesters refused to let go of the land citing that they had settled in the area since the time of their forefathers.

On 26 May 2023, hundreds of women and men, from Chiranjeev Colony and Labor Colony, staged a protest and raised slogans outside the Ghantaghar Grievance Centre in Bhiwani City (Haryana) against the lack of supply of clean drinking water despite several complaints. The Station House Officer (SHO) of the local police station arrived at the protest site and assured the protesters of remedial action.

On 26 May 2023, lawyers from the District Bar Association, led by the Association's President, staged an indefinite strike and protest outside the District Court in Fatehabad Town (Haryana) against the lack of judges in the District Courts.

On 26 May 2023, students staged a protest and raised slogans at Samvidhan Chowk in Jalandhar City (Jalandhar-I, Punjab) demanding the payment of Scheduled Caste Scholarship. The police intervened and manhandled and detained protesters.

On 26 May 2023, persons from the Kudumi Mahato caste community held a demonstration by blocking the road and later vandalised the car of TMC state minister, hurled stones and assaulted TMC members and other locals, and clashed with police at Garh Salboni village (Jhargram district, WB), demanding Scheduled Tribe status. Around a dozen policemen and one car driver were left injured. Four persons were later arrested by the police. TMC later claimed BJP was responsible for the incident.

On 26 May 2023, members of the DMK clashed with officials from the Income Tax (I-T) department in the Ramakrishnapuram area in Karur city (Tamil Nadu) when the I-T officials arrived for a raid at the residence of a DMK minister's brother. DMK members damaged the windshield and the rear-view mirror of the officials' car and assaulted the officials who were later hospitalised. DMK members also accused the I-T officials of assaulting and injuring them. Police filed cases against both the groups.

On 26 May 2023, residents of a locality in Chennai city (Tamil Nadu) assaulted a man who was caught breaking into a home and sexually harassing a 11 month old girl. Rioters chased and assaulted the abuser and then handed him over to the police.

On 26 May 2023, hundreds of farmers, under the banner of Kirti Kisan Union (KKU), led by KKU President and accompanied by KKU State Press Secretary and General Secretary, staged a protest at a grain market in Moga District (coded as Moga City, Punjab) demanding the provision of canal water for farming and drinking purposes. The protesters also demanded for legal guarantee on minimum support price (MSP) for crops.

On 26 May 2023, members of 'Sewerman Sanitaiton Workers' union staged a protest at the Municipal Corporation's (MC) Zone A office in Ludhiana City (Ludhiana East, Punjab) against the delay in the disbursal of salaries of recently regularised Class four MC employees.

On 26 May 2023, scores of street hawkers staged a protest near the Lieutenant Governor's residence in Delhi - Civil Lines (Central Delhi, Delhi) during 'International Hawker's Day' against the exclusion of many street hawkers in an ongoing survey (due to strict eligibility requirements) which has resulted in 80 percent of the street hawkers becoming ineligible to carry out their business on the streets.

On 26 May 2023, city lawyers staged a dharna (protest) at the District Court Complex in Ludhiana City (Ludhiana East, Punjab) against judicial employees utilising the parking space at the District Court Complex and the suspected misbehaviour of a judicial employee against a lawyer. Judicial employees also staged a counter protest against claimed misbehaviour by lawyers against judicial employees when they tried to park their vehicle.

On 26 May 2023, local residents staged a protest in Timberpur Village (Fatehgarh Sahib, Punjab) against the non-disposal of sewage and the lack of proper drainage system in the area. The protestors were assured of remedial action by the Block Development and Panchayat Officer.

On 26 May 2023, members, councillors, and leaders of AAP, led by a AAP councillor, and accompanied by local residents and members of the Joint Action Committee staged a protest, while burning an effigy of the Mayor (BJP), at Dadru Majra Locality in Chandigarh City against the UT Administration and Municipal Corporation for proposing a waste processing plant in the locality.

On 26 May 2023, old age pension beneficiaries staged a sit-in protest at Sadanga Panchayat office under Hatadihi block (Keonjhar district, Odisha) over the non-payment of pension money. The Sarpanch intervened and managed to pacify the old-age pension beneficiaries following which the sit-in was called off.

On 26 May 2023, a collective of more than 10 residents associations Puthiya Road and Kadavanthra took out a protest march to the office of Kerala Water Authority executive engineer in Kochi city (Ernakulam, Kerala) to demand a solution to the acute shortage of drinking water in the area.
On 26 May 2023, members of backward caste groups held a roadblock as a mark of protest in Bansjor town (Simdega, Jharkhand) for removing the reservation of backward castes from several districts.

On 26 May 2023, members of the All Odisha Roadside Vendors' Association staged a protest in Bhubaneswar city (Khordha, Odisha) demanding the state government allow them to restart their business near the Puri Jagannath Temple.
On 26 May 2023, locals held a protest at Udhampur city (J&K) against an Udhampur official over claimed corruption and misbehaviour with people.

On 26 May 2023, activists, under the banner of the Sangharash Samiti, staged a protest and blocked Balmiki Chowk in Phagwara City (Kapurthala, Punjab) demanding the repair of the dilapidated road near the Balmiki Temple. The protest ended on May 30th after the Phagwara Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) and Deputy Superintendent of Police assured the protestors of remedial action.

On 26 May 2023, residents protested in front of the deputy commissioner's office in the Mylapore area in Chennai city (Tamil Nadu) after a man, who had been assaulted (coded separately) for sexually abusing an 11-month-old girl, escaped from a government hospital. Police promised the protesters that they would catch the accused.

On 26 May 2023, locals including Wangjing Meira Paibi (Women Torch Bearers) pelted stones and damaged the residence of a BJP MLA while staging a demonstration in Wangjing town (Thoubal, Manipur) against repeated attacks by Kuki Militias and the governments failure to curb ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. On 26 May 2023, local residents (likely from Khasi and Jaintia communuities based on location and demand) staged a demonstration in front of the residence of the local MLA at Mylliem village (East Khasi Hills, Meghalaya) demanding a review to the existing reservation policy in the state for employment and education.

On 26 May 2023, local residents (likely from Khasi and Jaintia communuities based on location and demand) staged a demonstration in front of the residence of the local MLA at Nongstoin village (East Khasi Hills, Meghalaya) demanding a review to the existing reservation policy in the state for employment and education.
On 27 May 2023, six persons assaulted and injured three Sikh teenagers in Parbhani town (Parbhani, Maharashtra) over suspicion of theft. One of the teenagers later succumbed to his injuries.
On 27 May 2023, residents held a protest at Kauri town (Reasi district, J&K) to demand a railway station in the area after having given up land for the construction of a bridge.
On 27 May 2023, a group of Kashmiri Pandits held a protest at Tulmulla city (Ganderbal district, J&K) against the administration over poor provision of facilities for the pilgrims at a temple site.
On 27 May 2023, INC members led by sarpanches (village government heads) held a protest at Ranbir Singh Pura city (Jammu district, J&K) against a hospital administration over lack of facilities.

On 27 May 2023, JKNPP members led by a former minister held a protest march at Udhampur city (J&K) against the claimed manhandling of a senior leader of the party by the police during an earlier protest at Udhampur city (coded separately) and demanded action.

On 27 May 2023, villagers staged a protest outside the Municipal Corporation office in Hisar City (Haryana) against the MC's decision to set up a waste segregation plant in Satrod village. The protest forced the MC to halt work on the plant.

On 27 May 2023, members of the ASHA Workers and Facilitators Union staged a dharna (protest) at the PUDA ground in Patiala City (Punjab) against the government for imposing unnecessary conditions on ASHA workers and reducing their allowances.

On 27 May 2023, sanitation workers, who are currently on strike, staged a protest and waved black flags at Siddheshwar Chowk in Gurgaon City (Gurugram, Haryana) demanding the regularisation fo contractual workers and timely disbural of salaries.

On 27 May 2023, many residents of Dhudi village, inlcuding family members of the deceased, staged a sit-in protest at the Railway Station in Faridkot City (Punjab) demanding the arrest of a couple from Bhana village over suspicions of abetment to suicide in relation to the death of the youth. Residents of Bhana village also staged a counter protest demanding the cancellation of the First Information Report (FIR) against the couple.

On 27 May 2023, family members and relatives of the deceased staged a protest outside the office of the Deputy Commissioner in Shimla City (Himachal Pradesh) demanding the arrest of the accused suspected of murdering a 17 year old boy (previously missing) whose dead body was found in the city.
Around 27 May 2023 (as reported), hundreds of farmers staged a protest in Changanassery town (Kottayam, Kerala) over the inordinate delay in clearing paddy procurement dues.
On 27 May 2023, members of the tribal community held a protest in Badnawar town (Dhar, Madhya Pradesh) against the site chosen for PM Mitra Textile Park in Bhensola village.

On 27 May 2023, members of the INC led by a former Union minister staged a protest in front of the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD) in Tirupati city (Chittoor, Andhra Pradesh) demanding a wage increase and houses for staff, and the implementation of reservations and promotions for staff. Protesters accused the TTD of harassing pregnant staff and low-cadre workers.

On 27 May 2023, a large number of the tribals under the aegis of Janjati Suraksha Manch held a protest in Ahmedabad city (Ahmedabad, Gujarat) demanding that tribal people who have converted to other religions not be given the benefits accorded to members of scheduled tribes (ST).

On 27 May 2023, locals led by a JKNPP elected leader held a protest by burning an effigy at Udhampur city (J&K) against an Udhampur official over claimed corruption and misbehaviour with people. This was the second consecutive day of the protest.

On 27 May 2023, thousands of locals (likely Meitei) staged a demonstration march from two separate locations, Kakching Sumak Leikai Model Ground and Keirak, to converge at the basic ground in Kakching town (Kakching, Manipur) demanding the abrogation of suspension of operations agreements with Kuki Rebel groups, check on influx of illegal migrants and implementation of NRC in the state. The demonstration was staged amidst ongoing violence between the Meitei and Tribal communities in the state.

On 27 May 2023, locals residents staged a sit-in demonstration in Nongpok Sekmai village (Thoubal, Manipur) demanding deployment of more security forces to the village to protect properties that have been abandoned amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. There are only 10 families left in the village protecting all properties.

On 27 May 2023, internally displaced persons staged a sit-in demonstration at the Regional Water Sports Laisoi relief camp in Bishnupur district (Bishnupur, Manipur) against the lack of assistance from state authorities, while demanding abrogation of suspension of operation agreements with Kuki Rebel groups amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. Families from Torbung, Bangla and other areas of Churachandpur are seeking shelter at the relief camp.

On 27 May 2023, teacher aspirants and student union leaders along with AIYF and DYFI leaders staged a protest in Kurnool city (Andhra Pradesh) demanding the state government to address various employment-related issues including the filling up of vacancies.
On 27 May 2023, villagers staged a protest in Ayyanki village (Krishna, Andhra Pradesh) after a group of people attempted to mine gravel at the village pond. Villagers also alerted the police.

On 27 May 2023, parents of a 15 year old boy who drowned in a swimming pool at a recreation club staged a protest in the Madanayakanahalli area in Bengaluru city (Bengaluru North, Karnataka) accusing the club management of negligence. Protesters also demanded compensation.

On 27 May 2023, members of the Andhra Pradesh Employees Association (APGEA) staged protests in front of all tahsildar's offices across Srikakulam district (coded as Srikakulam city, Andhra Pradesh) against the YSRCP government and accused it of neglecting its employees out sourcing employees and not clearing dues.

On 27 May 2023, local residents staged a demonstration on the National Highway between Assam and Agartala near Chakmaghat village (Khowai, Tripura) demanding a solution to rampaging elephants in the area, destroying property at night.

On 27 May 2023, members of the Zo Re-Unification Organisation staged a demonstration march in Aizawl city (Aizawl, Mizoram) expressing solidarity with people from their tribe embroiled in violence with Meitei community in Manipur. They stated the members will take steps to support their fellow tribes people in Manipur if the 'atrocities' against them don't stop.

On 27 May 2023, four gang members led by a DMK panchayat union president attacked a revenue inspector in Narasingapuram village (Tiruchirappalli, Tamil Nadu) when he attempted to stop the illegal excavation of red earth. The assailants assaulted the official by striking his head with a stone and biting his neck.

On 27 May 2023, women staged sit-in protests in four locations in New Lamka town (Churachandpur, Manipur) demanding total separation from Manipur amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. Protesters held banners and placards and raised their concerns.

actor2: Police Forces of India (2014-) Manipur Rifles
text: On 28 May 2023, a mob of around 10,000 unidentified assailants (likely Meitei) laid siege to the armouries of 7 Manipur Rifles and 8 Indian Reserve Battalion at Khabeisoi in Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur), looting all arms and ammunition at the facility, amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. Looted arms included nine AK rifles with 256 magazines and 6,520 units of ammunition, 165 Insas rifles with 934 magazines and 44,770 units of ammunition, 57 Insas LMGs with 53 magazines, and MP5 and a magazine, eight Excalibur rifles with 50 magazines, 69 pistols (9mm) along with 142 magazines and 1,200 units of live ammunition, and 58 carbines with 234 magazines and 24,570 units of ammunition.

On 28 May 2023, local residents clashed with 5 youth from a private company at Hans Colony in Fatehabad City (Haryana) when the residents objected against the installation of a mobile tower by the private company in the locality, resulting in the injury of one woman. The 5 youth were suspected to have fired shots in the air and two of them were detained by the police.
On 28 May 2023, locals blackened the face of a man, paraded him with a garland of shoes and assaulted him in Kunwar Gaon Town (Budaun, Uttar Pradesh) for eloping with a girl.

On 28 May 2023, mobs (suspected Meitei) torched multiple abandoned buildings in Pureiromba Khongnangkong, Khongsai Veng and Chingmeirong localities in Imphal East district (coded as Porompat, Manipur) after widespread armed clashes with Kuki militants were reported from across the state, amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state.

On 28 May 2023, an irate mob (coded as Meitei) vandalised and set ablaze the residence of a former MLA of Saikul Assembly Constituency belonging to BJP in Mantripukhri in Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. The former MLA and his family were not at the house when it was besieged. Three cars, one two wheeler, and a granary were burned. The former MLA belonged to the Kuki-Zomi community. Suspected Meitei mob also torched multiple abandoned buildings at Lamphel Fisheries, the Kuki Independence War Memorial Complex and several houses belonging to the Kuki-Zo communities in Imphal city, amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state.
On 28 May 2023, BRS supporters assaulted a supporter of a suspended BRS leader and former MP near the NTR statue at the bypass road in Khammam city (Telangana) over unknown reasons.

On 28 May 2023, a few members of the KSU clashed with each other at the Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) office in Thiruvananthapuram city (Kerala) over a disagreement regarding the inclusion of married members as officers of the KSU. Congress leaders intervened to restore peace.

On 28 May 2023, members of the AIDSO, AIDYO, AIMMS, AIKKMS and the AIUTUC staged a protest in Dharwad city (Karnataka) against the detention of wrestlers and leaders of various organisations protesting in New Delhi against a BJP MP and the president of the Wrestling Federation of India facing sexual harassment allegations.

On 28 May 2023, civil society activists, writers and sportspersons staged a protest at the Freedom Park in Bengaluru city (Bengaluru Urban, Karnataka) in solidarity with the wrestlers protests in New Delhi, who have accused the Wrestling Federation of India's President of sexual harassment against many women wrestlers including a minor, and an institutional failure to prevent the sexual harassment of women athletes.

actor2: Police Forces of India (2014-) Rapid Action Force
text: On 14 June 2023, a mob (likely Meitei) torched the house of a BJP state Minister (Kuki) and burned down belongings from abandoned houses at PDA complex in Lamphel locality in Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. No one was injured in the incident. RAF resorted to firing tear gas and mock bombs to disperse the mob. The Minister is the sole women in the state cabinet and belongs to the Kuki community, she was also one of the 10 Kuki lawmakers who raised the demand for a separate administration when the violence between communities began.

On 14 June 2023, a dozen miners assaulted, using sticks, a team of 8 mining officers in Sancholi village (Gurugram, Haryana) during a raid on sand mining. 1 officer suffered injuries and an FIR has been registered against 12 people.

On 14 June 2023, nearly 100 armed TMC members clashed with ISF members, vandalised police vehicles and assaulted journalists at Bhangore-II town (South 24 Parganas district, WB) ahead of filing nominations for the panchayat (village government) elections. Police used force to disperse the mob.

On 14 June 2023, two factions of TMC clashed, fired at each other and lobbed crude bombs at Canning town (South 24 Parganas district, WB) ahead of filing nominations for the panchayat (village government) elections. Two TMC members were left injured in the clash. Police engaged in baton charge.

On 14 June 2023, TMC members clashed with ISF and CPI(M) members at several locations and firearms were also used at Canning town (South 24 Parganas district, WB) ahead of the panchayat (village government) elections. One person was left with a bullet injury.

On 14 June 2023, some people assaulted a granthi (Sikh ceremonial scripture reader) and a treasurer, using swords, at Gurdwara (Arjun Nagar) in Jagadhri city (Yamunanagar, Haryana) for opposing the sale of illegal liquor in the area. 2 people (granthi and the treasurer) suffered serious injuries.

On 14 June 2023, security guards and members of the Resident Welfare Association (RWA) suspectedly assaulted and kept hostage a Haryana Shehri Vikas Pradhikaran (HSVP) team at Rosewood City in Gurgaon city (Gurugram, Haryana) when the team arrived to carry out an inspection on the unauthorized construction of a gate.

The state has been under strict curfew timing since the violence began.

On 14 June 2023, AAP councilors staged a protest at the Delhi Mayor's office in Delhi - New Delhi city (Delhi) against the suspected involvement of MCD employees (Karol Bagh zone) in illegal activities together with the construction mafia.
On 14 June 2023, a large number of Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) members staged a protest in DAVV in Indore city (Indore, Madhya Pradesh) against paper leak and delayed results.

On 14 June 2023, BJP and CPI(M) members including a minister held a protest at Siliguri city (Darjeeling district, WB) against frequent power cuts in the area.

Protesters submitted a memorandum and threatened to launch a strike of the government did not heed to the employees' demands.

On 14 June 2023, 210 members of the affiliates of All India Bank Pensioners' and Retirees' Confederation (AIBPARC) staged a protest at the Dharna Chowk in Vijayawada city (Andhra Pradesh) highlighting their demands which included a pension, special allowance, dearness allowance and medical insurance.

On 14 June 2023, members of the Joint Forum of the Punjab Pensioners' Association (Ludhiana) staged a protest outside the Deputy Commissioner's office in Ludhiana city (Ludhiana East, Punjab) demanding the state government to increase their dearness allowance.

Protesters accused the contractors of paying only a part of their wages for the last 14 months and asked for their dues.

On 14 June 2023, members of the Sikh community staged a protest at the Mini Secretariat in Jagadhri city (Yamunanagar, Haryana) against the assault on 2 people at a Gurdwara earlier in the day (coded separately).

Protesters demanded action against the college administration.

The RU vice-chancellor reached the spot and announced a compensation of Rs 400000 and a contractual job in the university to one member of the deceased's family according to merit.

On 14 June 2023, locals held a protest at Sopore town (Baramulla district, J&K) over lack of water supply in the area. This was the third consecutive day of the protest.

Police used water cannons to disperse the protesters.

Police took the rioters into custody when they attempted to enter the office premises.

Police used force to disperse the mob.

actor2: Police Forces of India (2014-) Border Security Force
text: On 26 June 2023, a mob of villagers attacked an outpost of BSF at Umsyiem village (West Jaintia Hills, Meghalaya) after materials being smuggled to Bangladesh were seized by the security personnel. The mob pelted stones while the security forces pushed them back and resorted to firing in the air. Two BSF personnel and three civilians were injured in the clash. The villagers denied that they were smuggling goods and claimed that the BSF personnel were intoxicated during their duty.
