On 15 July 2023, local people staged a protest at Sirhind Choe banks in Sirhind-Fatehgarh city (Fatehgarh Sahib, Punjab) against garbage dumping in the area.
On 15 July 2023, over three dozen people held a protest by blocking a road at Srinagar city (J&K) against the installation of smart meters in the area that may lead to higher bills.

On 15 July 2023, a group of locals held a protest at Kolkata city (WB) over the state transport department's decision to withdraw tram services along a route that connects several schools, colleges, universities and markets in central Kolkata.
On 15 July 2023, INC members held a protest rally towards the CM's residence in Bhopal city (Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh) against the 'patwari exam scam'. Police used water canons to disperse them.

On 15 July 2023, dozens of JKPDP members held a protest march at Jammu city (J&K) against the BJP-led administration over claimed attempts to settle outsiders in J&K and over installation of smart power meters. Police detained several protestors.

On 15 July 2023, parents of children studying in Jayaram Government High School locked up all the 10 teachers in the in the headmaster's office in Karilopatana village (Kendrapara district, Odisha), during a demonstration demanding the appointment of more teachers.

Around 15 July 2023 (as reported), candidates elected for assistant professor posts staged a protest at the Freedom Park in Bengaluru city (Bengaluru Urban, Karnataka) demanding the authorities to issue their appointment orders.

On 16 July 2023, a former MLA and his supporters snatched the keys of cells and set free the prisoners, besides damaging CCTV cameras and assaulted jail officials in Beur Central Jail in Patna city (Patna district, Bihar) over their prison ward being 'deliberately kept open'. 11 prison employees were injured.

On 16 July 2023, members of the YSRCP and the TDP clashed with each other in Narasaraopet city (Guntur, Andhra Pradesh) over a property dispute which evolved into a political clash. Rioters hurled stones and attacked each other with sticks and iron rods. At least two persons were injured and two vehicles were damaged in the clash. Police intervened and brought the situation under control.

On 16 July 2023, BJP members assaulted a person and set him on fire at Tikashi village (Purba Medinipur district, WB) when he resisted their attempt to encroach upon his agricultural land post panchayat (village government) elections. He was left severely injured in the incident.

On 16 July 2023, large number of women (likely Meitei) staged a demonstration in the Khoirok village area (Kangpokpi, Manipur) blocking the roads for security forces for arresting three village volunteers involved in a gunbattle in the area (coded separately), amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. The women came from Keinou, Nambol and Bishnupur areas. The village volunteers were handed over to the demonstrators.

On 16 July 2023, thousands of women (likely Meitei) staged a demonstration on the road at Bungte Chiru village (Kangpokpi, Manipur) blocking the way of a Gorkha Regiment convoy, suspecting them of supporting Kuki militants, while information of armed clashes near Tingkai Khullen area spread, amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state.

On 16 July 2023, large number of women (likely Meitei) staged a demonstration on the road at various points between Kwakeithel to Bishnupur (coded as Bishnupur, Bishnupur, Manipur) blocking the road for movement of security forces after news of armed clashes in Tingkai Khullen area spread (coded separately), amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state.

On 16 July 2023, members of United Youths Club and Meira Paibi (likely Meitei) staged a sit-in demonstration at the United Youth Club at Maisanam Leikai of Khangabok Part II in Khangabok village (Thoubal, Manipur) demanding implementation of NRC, filing of FIRs (First Information Reports) against 10 Kuki MLAs who demanded a separate administration for Kuki community and abrogation of Suspension of Operation agreements with Kuki militants, amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state.
On 16 July 2023, members of the AAP held a protest in Ichhawar town (Sehore, Madhya Pradesh) against the 'Patwari Examination Scam' and demanded a CBI probe.
On 16 July 2023, members of BJP held a protest in Redhakhol town (Sambalpur, Odisha) against the visit of 5T Secretary.
On 16 July 2023, members of BJP held a black-flag protest in Deogarh town (Deogarh, Odisha) against the visit of 5T Secretary.

On 16 July 2023, family members of the deceased and members of BKU and Pagri Sambhal Jatta staged a protest by refusing to take the body of the deceased at Civil Hospital in Hisar city (Haryana) demanding the arrest of the driver of the car which hit the deceased's scooter, resulting in his death.
On 16 July 2023, around 1000 persons led by Roman Catholic archdiocese held a peace protest march at Kolkata city (WB) to demand restoration of peace in Manipur.

On 16 July 2023, relatives of a man who died while cleaning an underground sewer, members of the CITU and the CPI(M) staged a protest at the Government General Hospital in Vijayawada city (Krishna, Andhra Pradesh) demanding justice for the deceased's and compensation for his family.

On 16 July 2023, a large number of people, including the former home minister under the aegis of Jeev Maitri Pariwar held a dharna (sit-in protest) outside Nagar Nigam in Ratlam city (Ratlam, Madhya Pradesh) to protest felling of trees and death of birds at the site of upcoming Gold Complex.

Around 16 July 2023 (as reported), villagers and Kanwariyas (followers of Lord Shiva) staged a protest in Sadipur Chhidoli village (Gautam Buddha Nagar, Uttar Pradesh) against the police for being stopped from creating a religious worship site on government land.

On 16 July 2023, hundreds of members of the local unit of INC held a dharna (sit-in protest) and burned the effigy of the OPCC president in Jagatsinghpur city (Jagatsinghapur, Odisha) against the suspension of a former MLA for anti-party activities.

On 16 July 2023, members of the JSP staged a protest in the Gajuwaka area of Visakhapatnam city (Andhra Pradesh) against the ruling YSRCP and accused the party of misinterpreting the JSP chief's statements regarding the volunteer system. Protesters demanded that the YSRCP members stop targeting the JSP chief and also stop collecting personal information from the public.
On 16 July 2023, physically challenged persons held a protest at Jammu city (J&K) to demand resumption of pensions already sanctioned to them.

On 16 July 2023, students of the forestry department held a protest at Srinagar city (J&K) against the amendment by the government of Jammu and Kashmir to the eligibility criteria for the range officer gazetted post.

On 16 July 2023, a group of tribal farmers staged a protest in Bollepally village (Mahabubabad, Telangana) and blocked the work of forest officials to demand them to stop planting saplings on their cultivated land.

On 16 July 2023, local people staged a protest march, raising banners and slogans, at Millennium City metro station in Gurgaon city (Gurugram, Haryana) against various administrative departments over the lack of basic civic amenities, including good roads and drainage systems.

Around 16 July 2023 (as reported), family members of the deceased staged a protest at BRD Medical College in Gorakhpur city (Uttar Pradesh) against the pediatric department's negligence which led to the death of a 9-month-old child.

On 16 July 2023, local residents staged a protest at South Civil lines in Roorkee city (Haridwar, Uttarakhand) against the residents of another colony who were digging in the clear the drain that was waterlogged due to the rains. Police were deployed to control the situation.

On 16 July 2023, local people staged a protest in Kheri village (SAS Nagar, Punjab) against the Punjab State Power Corporation Limited (PSPCL) for the lack of electricity and water supply in the area.
On 16 July 2023, a group of residents from various Orris housing colonies staged a protest at Sector 85 in Gurgaon city (Gurugram, Haryana) against the supply of contaminated water in the area.

On 16 July 2023, residents of five colonies under Bag Mugaliya, (Ward No. 53) staged a protest by taking bath in muddy sewage water in Bhopal city (Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh) to draw attention to the problems faced by them due to unmetalled roads and heavy sewage.
On 16 July 2023, locals held a protest at Jammu city (J&K) against the increase in number of unauthorized vendors in the area and rise in theft cases.
On 16 July 2023, members of the AAP youth wing staged a protest at the AAP office in Lucknow city (Uttar Pradesh) against the rise in inflation. The police lathi-charged and detained protesters.

On 16 July 2023, two families clashed using sharp weapons in the Mudhisahi area under Gaumal panchayat (Bhadrak, Odisha) over a land dispute. Nine persons including four women sustained grievous injuries in the clash.

Around 16 July 2023 (as reported), a few youths and a BJP councillor suspectedly assaulted a traffic officer and two constables at Chaudhary More locality in Ghaziabad city (Uttar Pradesh) for drinking and playing loud music while on duty. The constables claimed that the assaulters were trying to free a man the traffic officer had caught. The assaulters counter claimed that they were assaulted by the constables. The assaulters were booked by the police and the traffic officer and constable were suspended from duty. A video of the incident was circulated online.

Around 16 July 2023 (as reported), local residents staged a hunger strike and a sit-in protest in Sissu town (Lahul and Spiti, Himachal Pradesh) demanding the government withdraw the Town and Country Planning Act from the district.

actor2: Police Forces of India (2014-) Assam Rifles
text: On 16 July 2023, hundreds of Meira Paibis (Women Torch Bearers, Meitei) intercepted an Assam Rifles truck carrying food supplies and vegetables for troops, and stole the ration, in Kakching town (Kakching, Manipur) amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. The women also threatened to burn the truck.

On 16 July 2023, hundreds of locals stopped the Tatanagar-Badampahar MEMU train, shouted slogans against railway authorities at Badamouda village under Gorumahisani police limits (Mayurbhanj, Odisha) claiming faulty design of a bridge and its low-quality work.

On 16 July 2023, locals held a protest, blocked National Highway-353 in Birunpadar village (Mayurbhanj, Odisha) demanding INR 20 lakh compensation for the deceased's family in the Bear attack. They also demanded free medical treatment for the injured.

On 17 July 2023, a mob of almost 1000 internally displaced people clashed with forest and range officers at the Burha Chapori Wildlife Sanctuary in Sonitpur district (coded as Tezpur, Sonitpur, Assam) using knives, machetes and sharp objects, after the officers tried to make the IDPs leave the area. The officers fired a few gunshots in claimed self-defence, one of them hit a woman and she succumbed to her injuries and died. 6 others were injured including three officers. The IDPs had moved to the area after their relocation shelters had been inundated due to flooding.

Around 17 July 2023 (as reported), mobs burned down houses of four persons suspected of killing a Naga woman (coded separately), and vandalised the main suspect's house, in Yumnam Huidrom village (Imphal West, Manipur) amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state.

On 17 July 2023, 150 people from villages Dhani Babbanpur and Musakhera, including a Block Development and a Panchayat officer, clashed, involving firing shots, in Musakhera village (Fatehabad, Haryana) over the issue of drawing a bundh (embankment) around Musakhera village to prevent flooding in the village.

On 17 July 2023, members of local organizations (likely Meitei) staged a sit-in demonstration at the market in Naransena village (Bishnupur, Manipur) against the filling of a case against a singer who published a song regarding the ongoing conflict in Manipur between Meitei and Tribal communities of the state.

On 17 July 2023, members of the Apunba Nupi Lip of Sinusiphai and Phubala (likely Meitei local groups) staged a sit-in demonstration at the Market Shed in Sinusiphai village (Bishnupur, Manipur) against the filling of a case against a singer who published a song regarding the ongoing conflict in Manipur between Meitei and Tribal communities of the state.

On 17 July 2023, members of Manipur Tent House Group and locals (likely Meitei) staged a sit-in demonstration under the banner 'Save Manipur, save Indigenous people' at Thangmeiband locality of Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) demanding implementation of NRC and action against Narco-terrorism in Manipur, amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. Additionally, a large number of women staged a demonstration at the Uripok Cheirap Court in Imphal city, against the killing of a Naga woman in Imphal East (coded separately).

On 17 July 2023, a large number of locals (likely Meitei) staged a demonstration on the Imphal-Dimapur road in the Awang Sekmai area (Imphal West, Manipur) against the arrest of 19 individuals for burning of three LPG transportation trucks at Sekmai area (coded separately), amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state.

On 17 July 2023, internally displaced people (likely Meitei) from Serou and Sugnu village living at relief camps staged a demonstration march and sit-in at Naohal Lei Lampak in Kakching town (Kakching, Manipur) demanding resettlement at their villages, implementation of NRC in Manipur, removal of Assam Rifles and abrogation of Suspension of Operation agreements with Kuki militants, amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state.

On 17 July 2023, members of the Naga community staged a demonstration on National Highway 102 at the bridge in Pallel village (Tengnoupal, Manipur) against the killing of a Naga woman in Imphal East (coded separately), they also demanded restoration of peace in Manipur, amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state.

On 17 July 2023, members of the Coordination Committee of Khongjom Circle and Apunba Meira Paibi (Women Torch Bearers) staged a sit-in demonstration at the market in Khongjom village (Thoubal, Manipur) against the killing of Naga woman in Imphal East district (coded separately) while demanding a probe into the murder and justice for the victim, amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state.

On 17 July 2023, locals staged a sit-in demonstration in Thoubal district (coded as Thoubal town, Thoubal, Manipur) against the killing of a Naga women in Imphal East (coded separately) while demanding justice for the victim, amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state.

On 17 July 2023, members of the All Wangjing Lamding Kairembikhok Club Organization staged a sit-in demonstration ate the Maring market in Wangjing town (Thoubal, Manipur) condemning the killing of a Naga women in Imphal East (coded separately), amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state.

On 17 July 2023, members of the Apunba Clubs and Salaai Kanba Lup staged a sit-in demonstration at the grounds of the city club in Heirok town (Thoubal, Manipur) against the killing of Naga women in Imphal East (coded separately) while demanding justice for the victim, amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state.

On 17 July 2023, 119 students of Sangal Government High School along with their parents and villager protested by staging a hunger strike in front of the school in Ramdurg town (Belagavi, Karnataka) demanding the state government's to revoke a Kannada teacher's transfer request. Students boycotted classes and locked the school doors.
On 17 July 2023, members of ABVP staged a protest outside Bikaner House in Delhi - Connaught Place (New Delhi, Delhi) against the suspected gangrape of a Dalit girl in Rajasthan.

On 17 July 2023, students various degree colleges under the aegis of the AIDSO staged a protest in front of the Crawford Hall in Mysuru University in Mysuru city (Karnataka) demanding the postponement of their examinations. Protesters said that the university had decided to hold the exams without completing the entire syllabus and urged the administration to postpone the exams by at least 15 days.

On 17 July 2023, members of AISA staged a protest at the office of the regional joint director of collegiate education (RJDCE) in Madurai city (Tamil Nadu) against the management of a government aided college for demanding a high fee to issue transfer certificates to students. Protesters demanded the state government to ensure that all government aided colleges collect only the government prescribed fees.
On 17 July 2023, scores of Bakarwal community members held a protest at Srinagar city (J&K) to demand designated pieces of land for graveyards.
On 17 July 2023, scores of farmers, under the banner of BKU, staged a protest in Makhwada village (Bijnor, Uttar Pradesh) demanding the capture of a leopard, which mauled a woman to death.

On 17 July 2023, members of the CPI(M) staged a protest in front of the Salem Collectorate in Salem city (Tamil Nadu) demanding the police to arrest people participating in the illegal sale of lottery tickets.
On 17 July 2023, DAP members held a protest at Jammu city (J&K) against the power department and administration for introducing prepaid electricity bills system.
On 17 July 2023, Shiv Sena and Dogra Front members held a protest at Jammu city (J&K) against the surge in tomato prices and demanded the government to set price fixing committee.

On 17 July 2023, farmers belonging to the KRRS staged a protest on the premises of the Zilla Panchayat Office in Belagavi city (Karnataka) demanding the government to start constructing cowsheds and provide employment to farmers under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS) (social welfare scheme guaranteeing the right to work) since farmers were struggling to work due to the lack of rain.

On 17 July 2023, farmers under the aegis of the KRRS staged a protest in front of the Cauvery Neeravari Nigam Limited office in Mandya city (Karnataka) demanding the release of water from the Cauvery river to the Visvesvaraya Canal to save their standing crops which were drying up due to a late monsoon.

On 17 July 2023, a section of residents of the fishermen's colony in Poompuhar in Mayiladuthurai district staged a protest during the weekly grievance redress meeting at the Mayiladuthurai Collectorate in Mayiladuthurai city (Nagapattinam, Tamil Nadu) accusing the members of the panchayat of discriminating against them for converting to Christianity. Protesters also submitted a petition to the Collector seeking his intervention.

On 17 July 2023, a significant number of members from the Jain community staged a protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi - Connaught Place (New Delhi, Delhi) demanding a CBI investigation into the murder of Jain monk in Karnataka.

On 17 July 2023, scores of transporters and local residents staged a protest outside the Regional Transport Authority (RTA) office in Ludhiana city (Punjab) against mismanagement at the RTA office which has led to delays in approving driving license applications, among others.
On 17 July 2023, newly selected candidates held a protest in Bhopal city (Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh) against the ban on appointment.
On 17 July 2023, shopkeepers held a protest at Batamaloo town (Srinagar district, J&K) against the municipal authorities over unfair demolition of property resulting in huge financial losses.
On 17 July 2023, a large number of locals including labourers held a protest at Srinagar city (J&K) against the installation of smart meters in the area that may lead to higher bills.
On 17 July 2023, retired tourism department employees held a protest at Srinagar city (J&K) to demand settlement of gratuity, leave salary and seventh pay commission arrears.

On 17 July 2023, MLAs of Maha Vikas Agadhi led by the leader of the opposition held a protest on the steps of the state assembly in Mumbai - Nariman Point city (coded to Mumbai City, Maharashtra) against the incumbent state government.

On 17 July 2023, members of the NSUI and ABVP held a massive protest outside the police headquarters in Jaipur city (Jaipur, Rajasthan) demanding strict punishment for three students arrested for allegedly raping a Dalit minor girl on Jai Narain Vyas University (JNVU) campus (coded separately).

On 17 July 2023, members of various progressive organisations and students under the banner of the Odanadi Seva Samsthe (organisation for trafficked and sexually exploited women and children) took out a protest march in Mysuru city (Karnataka) demanding a reinvestigation by a Special Investigation Team into a rape and murder case reported in Dharmasthala in 2012.

On 17 July 2023, members of the ABVP held a massive protest outside the police headquarters in Jodhpur city (Jodhpur, Rajasthan) demanding strict punishment for three students arrested for allegedly raping a Dalit minor girl on Jai Narain Vyas University (JNVU) campus.

On 17 July 2023, students of KN Girls' College assembled and held a protest at the district collectorate in Jodhpur city (Jodhpur, Rajasthan) demanding better security provisions on the college campus.

On 17 July 2023, members of the Adi Tamilar Peravai along with families from Kunnoothupatti staged a protest in front of the Collectorate in Dindigul city (Tamil Nadu) accusing some people of threatening them and attempting to evict them from their farmland to set up a stone quarry.

On 17 July 2023, guest faculty and contract teachers of the Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalayas (KGBVs) staged a protest at the Dharna Chowk in Hyderabad city (Telangana) against their contract termination. Protesters demanded that they be reinstated and accused the institute management of terminating them for no reason and recruiting new employees overnight.
On 17 July 2023, local residents staged a protest at Sheller Road in Ludhiana city (Punjab) against the contamination in the water supply.

On 17 July 2023, local people staged an indefinite dharna (sit-in protest), raising slogans, at Sirhind Choe banks in Sirhind-Fatehgarh city (Fatehgarh Sahib, Punjab) against garbage dumping in the area.

Around 17 July 2023 (as reported), family members of the deceased locked the water house and staged a protest at the railway gate within Chattargarh Patti locality in Sirsa city (Haryana) against the administration's negligence in failing to build the wall of the water house which led to the drowning of two children.

On 17 July 2023, villages and family members of a minor girl who was suspected to have been raped and murdered staged a protest in Gulbarga city (Kalaburagi, Karnataka) demanding action against the accused, one crore rupees compensation and a government job for the family members of the deceased, and the strengthening of the Prevention of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act.

On 17 July 2023, scores of beneficiaries from six wards gheraoed (surrounded) the cooperative samiti office at Tarasa village under Rajkanika block (Kendrapara district, Odisha) to protest against the embezzlement of 2 months' quota of PDS rice by the concerned dealer.

On 17 July 2023, locals held a protest by blocking a road at Nangalan village in Billawar tehsil (Kathua district, J&K) against the school management over sending students back in heavy rain two of whom drowned and demanded action against the management.
On 17 July 2023, locals held a protest by blocking a road at Tota Gali village (Poonch district, J&K) to demand investigation into a case of a person missing since yesterday.
On 17 July 2023, locals held a protest by blocking a railway track at Barrackpore city (North 24 Parganas district, WB) to demand a foot over bridge near the railway station.

On 17 July 2023, family members of the deceased staged a protest march to Punjab Raj Bhavan in Chandigarh city against the death of a 22-year-old female after falling from the third floor of a building. The protesters claimed that she was murdered and demanded justice. The police prevented the protesters from reaching Raj Bhavan.

On 17 July 2023, residents of Dokkampatty in Irumathur panchayat staged a protest at the Collectorate in Dharmapuri city (Tamil Nadu) demanding the District Collector to retrieve a piece of graveyard land from an AIADMK member who had encroached upon it. Protesters enacted a funeral scene to highlight their protest and threatened to their Voter IDs and Aadhaar card to the government if their demands were not met.

On 17 July 2023, around 200 sugarcane farmers under the banner of the Gomantak Uss Utpadak Sangathana (agricultural organisation) staged a protest outside the Sanjivani sugarcane factory premises and on the Ponda-Belgaum National Highway in Ponda city (North Goa, Goa) to demand the state government to inform the protesters whether the Sanjivani sugarcane factory would be reopened or not. Police detained around 120 protesters and released them late ar night.

On 17 July 2023, a large group of Meitei community members staged demonstrations along the road in Sinjamei and Kwakeithel localities of Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur), demanding a meeting with the Chief Minister over the killing of Meiteis by Kuki militants in Khamenlok (coded separately), amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. Mothers of the victims were among the demonstrators. Police fired tear gas and mock bombs to disperse the demonstration, following which more locals (Meitei) joined the demonstrators, threw stones and sling shots at police and vandalised two vehicles belonging to the Rapid Action Force. A convoy of an Indian Police Service officer was caught in the demonstration at Kwaikathel, during which a mob attacked the convoy, causing the policemen to flee, and torched one vehicle. 27 people were injured in the clashes and 30 were arrested.

On 17 July 2023, locals and traders held a demonstration at Pallanwala town (Jammu district, J&K) against the opening of a liquor shop in the area and looted the liquor stock and the vehicle it was brought it in.

On 17 July 2023, two BJP ministers along with BJP members held a demonstration as part of a 12-hour strike and assaulted the police and vandalised a police outpost at Bamangola town (Maldah district, WB) over the claimed murder of a BJP member over political reasons on 16 July 2023 (coded separately).

On 17 July 2023, around 50 assailants (some armed), including members of AAP (as claimed), opened fire and pelted stones at local villagers and ransacked four vehicles in Rasulpur Jaura village (Patiala, Punjab) in opposition to the installation of a new gate at the house of a local villager. 4 people were injured, including a retired police officer, with one receiving bullet injury to the jaw.
On 17 July 2023, members of BJP and former local MLA held a protest front of Tata Power (TPWODL) office in Patnagarh town (Bolangir district, Odisha) against power cuts.

Around 17 July 2023 (as reported), all the girl students of the Unit-9 Govt Girls' High School and their parents held a sit-in protest in Bhubaneswar city (Khordha, Odisha) against the merger of girl's school with nearby boys' high school.

On 18 July 2023, locals demonstrated, chanted Hindu slogans, and clashed with state police forces at Rangirkhari point in Silchar town (Cachar, Assam), after a missing woman's mutilated body was found. The mob threw stones at police personnel, and police resorted to lathi charge and blank fire to disperse them. Around 25 people were injured, while 11 were arrested.

On 18 July 2023, villagers from Farwai and Vaidwala on one side and Panihari and Burj Karamgarh on the other side clashed, using lathis, stones, and sharp-edged weapons, near Panihari village (Sirsa, Haryana) over the opening of an underpass to drain out water from Panihari village and divert he flow of Ghaggar river. 4 people were injured, and police were deployed to control the situation.

Around 18 July 2023 (as reported), 3 youths (likely Hindu) assaulted, and brandished a gun at a Muslim youth in Baghpat district (Uttar Pradesh) for refusing to chant 'Jai Shri Ram' (a Hindu religious chant). The Muslim youth is the son of a local imam (a Muslim religious head). The 3 accused have been arrested.

On 18 July 2023, locals staged sit-in demonstrations at a school ground at Khurai Heikrumakhong and Khurai Salangthong in Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) demanding restoration of peace in Manipur while condemning the killing of a Naga woman, amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state.

On 18 July 2023, locals along with members of Asomiya Yuba Macha, All Tai Ahom Students Union, and INC staged a demonstration at Demow Chairali town (Sivasagar, Assam) against the proposed delimitation draft published by the Election Commission of India.

On 18 July 2023, members of Thoubal district Langathel Meira Paibi (Women Torch Bearers) staged a sit-in demonstration at the market in Langathel village (Thoubal, Manipur) against the killing of a Maring Naga woman by a mob of Meitei community members (coded separately), amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state.
On 18 July 2023, a large number of locals led by AAP members held a protest at Jammu city (J&K) against the J&K administration and BJP over prepaid power proposal.

On 18 July 2023, members of the AIADMK including an MLA staged a protest near the Assembly in Puducherry city (Puducherry) demanding the implementation of a 7.5% reservation for students from government schools in medical colleges in the Union Territory.

On 18 July 2023, members of the BJP, including a BJP MLA, a former Mayor (BJP), and the BJP State Vice-president, accompanied by local residents, staged a protest near Delhi Gate in Delhi - Darya Ganj (Central Delhi, Delhi) against an AAP MLA who the protester's claimed was depriving his constituency of tanker water supply.

On 18 July 2023, sugarcane farmers of Mysuru and Chamarajanagar districts under the aegis of the Karnataka Sugarcane Farmers Association staged a protest in front of the Deputy Commissioner's office in Siddharthanagar area in Mysuru city (Karnataka) demanding the state government to pay them their dues from last season. Protesters raised slogans and were stopped by the police while marching to the Deputy Commissioner's office, before being allowed to submit a memorandum.

On 18 July 2023, members of the Rythu Sangham (farmers' group), an outfit affiliated to the CPI(M), along with members of the Cashew Farmers' Association staged a protest at Palasa town (Srikakulam, Andhra Pradesh) demanding the state government to take action against a consortium of cashew traders and accusing them of being responsible for the drop in the prices of cashew nuts due to the strike called by cashew processing units.

On 18 July 2023, local residents, joined by the former senior deputy mayor (INC), former BJP councilor, social activists, and several other political leaders, staged a protest outside the Municipal Corporation's (MC) zonal office in Amritsar city (Punjab) against the issue of water contamination in the area.
On 18 July 2023, locals led by panches (village government head) held a protest at Pallanwala city (Jammu district, J&K) against the opening of a liquor shop in the area.

On 18 July 2023, doctors staged protests outside the office of the Director of Medical Education (DME) in Hyderabad city (Telangana) against the promotion of associate professors and accused the state government of underreporting the number of vacancies in medical colleges.

On 18 July 2023, Asha workers belonging to the Asha Workers Union under the aegis of the CITU staged a protest in front of the District Medical and Health office in Srikakulam city (Andhra Pradesh) against the mental stress and heavy workload that Asha workers were subjected to. Protesters demanded basic facilities such as good quality mobiles phones and internet and submitted a memorandum to the administration.

On 18 July 2023, scores of ASHA workers under the aegis of the ASHA Workers Union along with the CITU and the AIDWA staged a protest in front of the District Medical and Health office in Visakhapatnam city (Andhra Pradesh) against the mental stress and heavy workload that ASHA workers were subjected to. text: On 3 August 2023, a mob of around 500 persons (likely Meitei) stormed and looted the 2nd Indian Reserve Battalion armoury at Naransena village (Bishnupur, Manipur) amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. text: On 8 September 2023, thousands of men and women (likely Meitei) from Kakching and Thoubal sides gathered in Pallel area (Tengnoupal, Manipur), tried to storm the Assam Rifles beat office, and blocked roads to suspectedly prevent reinforcements from reaching the area, after hearing about the gunfight between armed assailants (likely Meitei) and security forces in Molnoi village (coded separately), amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. Security forces, comprising military, AR and state police, attempted to stop them from marching forward. On 2 November 2023, rural workers gathered in large numbers under the banner of the Democratic MNREGA Front and staged a dharna (sit-in protest) outside the Deputy commissioner's (DC) office in Fatehgarh Sahib city (Punjab) over various demands including raising the minimum wage as per the law, and the provision of various benefits including pension, and support for the construction of houses. The protesters also condemned the derogatory language used against women by the BDPO of Sirhind and Khera blocks.

On 2 November 2023, members of the Jagatjit Cotton Textile Mills (JCT) shifted their dharna (sit-in protest) ' day 31' outside the JCT premises (as directed by the High court) in Phagwara city (Kapurthala, Punjab) demanding the payment of pending salaries including for overtime work.

On 2 November 2023, hundreds of students staged a sit-in protest outside the Director's office at Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Banaras Hindu University (BHU) in Varanasi city (Uttar Pradesh) demanding action against the accused involved in sexual harassment of a woman in the early hours of the morning. The protesters also demanded the improvement of security in the university.

On 2 November 2023, some people led by an AAP MLA gathered and staged a protest at Loni Gola Chakkar in Delhi - Gokalpur city (North East Delhi, Delhi) condemning the summoning of the Delhi Chief Minister (AAP) over suspicions of his involvement in, or awareness of, the Delhi excise policy-related money laundering case. 17 protesters were detained and later released. The protest was being held alongside the 'Red Light On, Gaadi Off' campaign - to control vehicular pollution.

On 2 November 2023, family members of the deceased staged a protest along the Patiala-Delhi National Highway in Narwana town (Jind, Haryana) against the police for suspectedly assaulting a man who later succumbed to his injuries (coded separately).
On 2 November 2023, locals held a protest by blocking a road at Sopore town (Baramulla district, J&K) over lack of water supply in the area.

On 2 November 2023, local people including members of the Dr. Abdul Kalam Welfare Front staged a protest outside the Deputy commissioner's (DC) office in Malerkotla city (Sangrur, Punjab) against the state government for falsely claiming to have fulfilled their demands for improvement in health facilities and appointment of specialized doctors at the Civil hospital.

On 2 November 2023, family members of the deceased staged a protest and placed the body of the deceased along the road near Kapia Mishra village under Jogia police station area (Siddharth Nagar, Uttar Pradesh) against the death of a newborn and a woman (the mother) which the protesters blamed on the hospital's negligence.

Around 2 November 2023 (as reported), local people staged a protest, raising slogans, in Sabdalpur Shumali village (Amroha, Uttar Pradesh) demanding action against the electricity department and contractor whom the protesters accused of negligence which led to the electrocution and death of a man (laborer).

On 2 November 2023, dental students staged a sit-in protest on 'day 2' of their protest at Dr Harvansh Singh Judge Institute of Dental Sciences & Hospital (Panjab University) in Chandigarh city demanding an increase in stipend.

On 2 November 2023, members of KKU, led by its State vice president, staged a protest march from Bhandari bridge to Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar city (Punjab) condemning the portrayal of Sikhs as separatists and demanded action against those involved in the 1984 anti-Sikh riots in Delhi.

On 2 November 2023, local people staged a protest at the Dhandari Khurd area in Ludhiana city (Punjab) against the municipal corporation for failing to resolve the issue of sewage overflow in the area.

On 2 November 2023, members of the BJP from Nagarkurnool staged a protest at the BJP office in Nampally (Nalgonda, Telangana) over rumours that the BJP might allot seats to members of the JSP for the upcoming Telangana state assembly elections.

On 2 November 2023, members of the INC staged a protest outside an INC leader's farmhouse in Shamshabad city (Rangareddy, Telangana) after officials of the Income Tax department arrived at the farmhouse to conduct raids. Protesters said that the raids were meant to harass all those contesting in the upcoming Telangana state assembly elections.
On 2 November 2023, tea estate workers held a protest by encircling the management at Trihana Tea Estate (Darjeeling district, WB) to demand a bonus.

On 2 November 2023, members of joint coordination committee of Meitei community staged a sit-in protest in Thoubal district (coded to Thoubal, Manipur), against the killing of a police personnel (coded separately), amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities.

On 2 November 2023, people (likely Meitei) staged protests in Tengnoupal district (coded to Tengnoupal town, Manipur) condemning the killing of a police officer by unidentified armed assailants (coded separately) amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities. Protesters also demanded additional security forces in the border town of Moreh.
Around 2 November 2023 (as reported), women held a protest in Jamshedpur city (East Singhbhum, Jharkhand) against the demolition of an illegal liquor vend by the police personnel.

On 3 November 2023, locals held a protest in Ibrisingh village (Jagatsinghapur, Odisha) against the construction of a proposed mega grid sub-station project by a private agency, engaged by Odisha Power Transmission Corporation Ltd (OPTCL), over the acquisition of land.

Around 3 November 2023 (as reported), the members of the Western Ri Bhoi branch of Hynniewtrep (Khasi-Jaintia) Achik National Movement (HANM) staged a protest at Patharkhmah village (Ri Bhoi district, Meghalaya) demanding the inclusion of the Khasi Language in the Eighth Schedule and the implementation of the Inner Line Permit (ILP).

On 3 November 2023, hundreds of students of Rajendra Institute of Medical Sciences (RIMS) under the aegis of Junior Doctor's Association took out a candle march in the hospital premises in Ranchi city (Jharkhand) to protest the death of a post-graduate student under mysterious condition in the hostel campus. They also submitted a memorandum to the hospital director demanding compensation to the dependent of the deceased and the installation of cameras in and around the hostels.

On 3 November 2023, over 1,000 candidates and members of the Jharkhand State Students Union (JSSU) organized an 'Adhikar March' (right march) on foot, from Morabadi to the Raj Bhavan gate in Ranchi city (Jharkhand) demanding a CBI investigation into the claimed irregularities in the Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC) selection.

On 3 November 2023, thousands of Anganwadi workers, assistants, BTT employees union, building construction and contract workers, health department staff, municipal corporation, municipality, electricity distribution, and sanitation workers under the aegis of Jharkhand Pradesh Bharatiya Mazdoor Sangh staged a protest in front of Raj Bhavan in Ranchi city (Jharkhand) over various issues such as widespread corruption in government departments, challenges faced by the Jharkhand State Cooperative Bank, concerns of overweight laborers, issues concerning MNREGA workers, corruption in the coal industry, and efforts to combat coal theft. They also submitted a memorandum of their demands to the governor.

On 3 November 2023, drivers of Assam State Transport Corporation (ASTC) buses staged a protest at the National Highway bus depot in Silchar city (Cachar, Assam) against claimed assault on an ASTC bus driver by some auto-rickshaw drivers.

On 3 November 2023, members of the BJP staged a protest in Perambalur town (Tamil Nadu) against the attack on some BJP members by DMK members at the District Collectorate (coded separately). Protesters demanded that a case under the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989, be booked against the DMK members including a minister.

On 3 November 2023, over 1500 workers under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS) (social scheme) staged a protest in front of the block development office at Sathyamangalam town (Erode, Tamil Nadu) accusing the administration of not paying their wages for the past three months.

On 3 November 2023, workers under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS) (social scheme) staged a protest in Bhavanisagar town (Erode, Tamil Nadu) accusing the administration of not paying their wages for the past three months.

On 3 November 2023, over 650 workers under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS) (social scheme) staged a protest in Thalavadi town (Erode, Tamil Nadu) accusing the administration of not paying their wages for the past three months.

On 3 November 2023, tribal people of various villages in Alluri Sitharama Raju (ASR) district along with a ZPTC member, sarpanches (village heads), and members of the CPI(M) staged a protest at the special Spandana programme organised under the aegis of the ITDA Project Officer and the Joint Collector in Anantagiri town (East Godavari, Andhra Pradesh) demanding basic amenities including electricity supply and roads. Protesters carried 'dolis' (dolls) and torches and raised slogans to mark their protest.

On 3 November 2023, a large number of INC members including members of the IYC under the aegis of the Aryadan Foundation staged a protest march in Malappuram city (Kerala) in solidarity with the people of Palestine amidst ongoing conflict between Israel and Palestine.

On 3 November 2023, state and central government employees, including CITU General Secretary, gathered under the banners of the Confederation of Central Government Employees and Workers, All India State Government Pensioners Federation, All India State Government Employees Federation, and School Teachers Federation of India and staged a protest rally at Ramlila Maidan in Delhi - Kotwali (Central Delhi, Delhi) over various demands including regularization of contractual jobs, payment of pending arrears, and ban on privatization, among others.

On 3 November 2023, family members of the deceased and Bajrang Dal members staged a protest in Sampurna Nagar town (Kheri, Uttar Pradesh) against the death of a girl who committed suicide over an objectionable video - and circulated it online - made by a young man from another community (likely Muslim). The protesters demanded action against the young man.

On 3 November 2023, over 500 members of BJKM members held a protest march at Kolkata city (WB) over claimed irregularities in a food distribution scheme by a TMC minister under the TMC-led state government.

On 3 November 2023, Asha workers (female health workers) held a protest at Kathua city (J&K) to demand an increase in wages.

On 3 November 2023, a massive protest was held by locals (coded as Hindu Group) in Jammu city (J&K) against a murder case involving a interfaith couple claiming it was a case of 'love jihad' (a theory that attributes a religious motive to marriage between interfaith couples from the Hindu and Muslim community, intended to convert people to Islamic faith) and to demand justice.

On 3 November 2023, members of Kuki-Zo groups gathered under the banner of the joint UNAU Student's, Kuki-Zo Women's, and the UNAU Tribal Women's Forums (Delhi) at Jantar Mantar in Delhi - Connaught Place (New Delhi, Delhi) condemning the BJP-led central and state government's for failing to stop the ongoing communal violence in Manipur. The protesters also demanded a separate administration for tribal communities.

On 3 November 2023, members of the Kuki-Zo communities including mostly women under the aegis of the Committee on Tribal Unity (COTU) staged protests in Gamgiphai village (Kangpokpi, Manipur) against the deployment of state forces in Moreh town amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and tribal, including Kuki-Zomi, communities in the state. Protesters held placards, condemned the use of excessive force by the armed forces and demanded their withdrawal.

On 3 November 2023, the people of Kangpokpi district led by the leaders of the Committee on Tribal Unity (CoTU) staged a protest march on the National Highway-2 in Kangpokpi town (Manipur) against Meitei armed assailants from Myanmar for occupying Moreh town and against the deployment of state forces in Moreh town, midst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities. Protesters also submitted a memorandum to the authorities to mark their protest and held placards, condemned the use of excessive force by the armed forces and demanded their withdrawal.

On 3 November 2023, sanitation workers held a protest at Udhampur city (J&K) against the delay in release of pending wages.

On 3 November 2023, employees staged a hunger strike alongside their protest (ongoing) atop a liquor factory's six-storied process plant at Rauser Kothi area in Chauthera village (Shahjahanpur, Uttar Pradesh) against the notice of termination of service.

On 3 November 2023, several dozen students including members of AISA and NSUI staged a protest and burned an effigy at Banaras Hindu University (BHU) in Varanasi city (Uttar Pradesh) against the sexual harassment of a woman at the Institute of Technology (IIT) Banaras Hindu University (BHU) campus area around 2 November. The protesters also condemned the university administration's decision to build a wall between BHU and IIT-BHU.

On 3 November 2023, parents of the students staged a protest and locked the gate of the school in Hisar city (Haryana) demanding action against the Dean of the school whom the protesters accused of feeding intoxicants and molesting 4 students.

On 3 November 2023, hundreds of people including family members of the deceased and local people staged a protest and placed the body of the deceased along the road at Dholeda bus stand near Khatoli Ahir village (Mahendragarh, Haryana) against the death of a man and a child who were hit and killed by an overloaded dumper truck. The protesters demanded a government job for the wife of the deceased.

On 3 November 2023, family members of the deceased staged a protest along the road in Sirsa district (Haryana) demanding action against the police whom the protesters accused of assaulting and killing a young man who was under custody over a drug supply charge (coded separately).
On 3 November 2023, consumers held a protest at Cooch Behar city (WB) over distribution of low quality rice by the ration dealer for a prolonged duration.

On 3 November 2023, six unidentified persons assaulted TMC members and a private security guard and vandalised furniture at Madhyamgram town (North 24 Parganas district, WB) over an unspecified issue. TMC claimed they were BJP supporters however BJP denied the claim. Police later arrested all six persons.

On 3 November 2023, a large number of farmers gathered under the banner of BKU (Sidhupur) and staged a protest in the Fatehgarh Sahib district (Punjab) and accused state government officials of harassing farmers for burning stubble. The protesters also claimed that the farmers lacked the necessary support from the government to procure and adopt proper machinery for stubble management.

On 3 November 2023, farmers gathered under the banner of BKU, led by the BKU District President, and staged a protest at the Sub Divisional Magistrate's (SDM) office in Radaur town (Yamunanagar, Haryana) demanding the appointment of a SDM at the soonest, since the lack of an SDM has negatively hampered work related to registration of vehicles, and issuance of driving licenses, among others.

On 3 November 2023, local councillors staged a hunger strike and a sit-in protest at the Municipal corporation in Mainpuri city (Uttar Pradesh) over a six-point demand which includes the removal of irregularities at the municipality and the processing of work through councillors at every ward office.

On 3 November 2023, dental students went on a hunger strike on 'day 3' of their sit-in protest at Dr Harvansh Singh Judge Institute of Dental Sciences & Hospital (Panjab University) in Chandigarh city demanding an increase in stipend.

On 3 November 2023, members of various organizations including AITUC, Hind Mazdoor Sabha, INTUC, AICCTU, and others, staged a protest in front of the Kirat Bhawan in Mohali city (SAS Nagar, Punjab) demanding an increase in salaries and the withdrawal of the state government's decision to increase the work hours for industrial workers.

On 3 November 2023, local traders and Sarafas (jewellers) staged a protest and closed the Sarafa market in Mainpuri (Uttar Pradesh) demanding the withdrawal of the central government's decision to impose a one percent excise duty on Sarafas.

On 3 November 2023, a group of farmers including members of BKU (Sidhupur) (likely) forcibly detained a team of government officials and made them burn paddy straw in Mehma Sarja village (Bathinda, Punjab) when the team arrived in the area to advise farmer to stop burning paddy straw. 2 farmers were later arrested.

On 3 November 2023, members of the Valmiki community staged a protest outside a temple at the Amber Talab (Pond) area in Roorkee city (Haridwar, Uttarakhand) against the temple priest for banning women from the Valmiki community from entering the temple and for misbehaving with a woman and using casteist slurs.

On 3 November 2023, locals assaulted a man (shopkeeper) and his family members, and vandalized his shop, at Vishwakarma Nagar locality in Ludhiana city (Punjab) after the man confronted the children playing outside his shop and objected to their use of abusive language against girls.

On 3 November 2023, members of the Bajrang Dal members assaulted two Muslim youths in Bhopal city (Madhya Pradesh) accusing the duo of conducting 'love jihad' (religious conversion through a relationship/marriage), after finding them with a Hindu girl at a private hotel.

On 3 November 2023, members of the BJP assaulted students of New Socialist Initiative, a left-leaning student group, at Savitribai Phule Pune University (SPPU) in Pune city (Maharashtra) during a demonstration against 'objectionable' graffiti on PM. Four students were injured. Police briefly detained four students.

On 3 November 2023, leaders of various Dalit organisations, members of the BSP and the INC along with family members of a Dalit youth who died by suicide staged a protest outside the Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Medical Sciences (RIMS) mortuary in Adilabad city (Telangana) against the BRS-led state government for not implementing any welfare schemes for members of the Dalit community. The youth in his suicide note had stated this reason for his death. Protesters also demanded compensation and a double bedroom house for the deceased's family. Police detained the protesters.

On 3 November 2023, members of the INC including an MLA staged a protest march to the office of the KSEB Executive Engineer in the Palarivattom locality in Kochi city (Ernakulam, Kerala) against the increase in electricity charges in the state. Protesters said that the increase in the prices of essential commodities and other charges would be a financial burden on the people of the state.

On 3 November 2023, members of the INC including an MLA and an MP staged a protest by organising a hunger strike in the Division 51 area in Kochi city (Ernakulam, Kerala) demanding the government to take measures to dismantle remnants of an old bridge that was obstructing the smooth flow of vehicles on the bridge and the barges through the backwaters.

text: On 3 November 2023, women of the area (likely Kuki) vandalized and dismantled a post of CRPF near Khousabung village area (Bishnupur, Manipur), after it was moved from the buffer zone further towards their village, amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities. The women claimed that the new location would be used to attack their village.

On 3 November 2023, thousands of Kuki women staged a protest rally in Tuibong village (Churachandpur, Manipur), demanding justice for the Kuki-Zo people, amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities.

On 3 November 2023, Village Administrative Officers staged a protest at the Sivaganga collector's office in Sivaganga city (Tamil Nadu) against the attack on a Village Administrative Officer by unidentified assailants suspected to be illegal soil miners.

On 3 November 2023, people (likely Meitei) staged protests in Tengnoupal district (coded to Tengnoupal town, Manipur) condemning the killing of a police officer by unidentified armed assailants (coded separately) amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities. Protesters also demanded additional security forces in the border town of Moreh.

On 3 November 2023, members of the Meitei Community Joint Coordinating Committee, an apex body of 18 local clubs of Waithou, Kiyam, Kiyam Siphai, Haokha, and Thoubal Khunou staged protests at the Babu bazaar in Thoubal town (Manipur) condemning the killing of a police officer by unidentified armed assailants (coded separately) amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities.

On 3 November 2023, family members blocked the Morena-Ambah State Highway in Kachnodha village (Morena, Madhya Pradesh) demanding the arrest of the Sarpanch (village head) of the village for killing their relative.

On 3 November 2023, family members and relatives of a man who died by suicide due to suspected dowry (payment paid by the bride's family to the groom) harassment staged a protest before the mortuary at KIMS Hospital in Hubballi city (Dharwad, Karnataka) demanding action against the wife's family members for harassing the victim.

On 3 November 2023, volunteers under the aegis of the All Commercial Vehicle Owners Association (ACVOA) picketed 'chakka bandh' (road block) in various strategic locations at Mokokchung town (Nagaland) to protest against the state government's failure to fulfill its assurance concerning the payments to the vehicles requisitioned during the 14th Assembly election 2023. The volunteers also seized some vehicles for defying the bandh call. Unclear how the seizure took place, no further information.

On 4 November 2023, members of the AAP women's wing, led by its State president, staged a protest march from Darul Shafa to the BJP office in Lucknow city (Uttar Pradesh) against inflation and condemned the arrest of an AAP leader (MP and Uttar Pradesh State-in-charge) over accusations of his involvement in the Delhi excise police scam.

On 4 November 2023, dental students, on 'day 4' of their protest, staged a candlelight protest march, raising slogans, at Dr Harvansh Singh Judge Institute of Dental Sciences & Hospital (Panjab University) in Chandigarh city demanding an increase in stipend.

On 4 November 2023, members of INC, led by a former MLA (INC), staged a protest in Ludhiana city (Punjab) demanding action against the accused who assaulted an INC leader and his wife in the city on 3 November (coded separately).
On 4 November 2023, members of the Mid-Day Meal Workers' Union staged a protest in Fatehgarh Sahib (Punjab) demanding a hike in the honorarium amount.

On 4 November 2023, hundreds of students staged an 'Akrosh' (anger) protest march, carrying banners, to Banaras Hindu University (BHU) in Varanasi city (Uttar Pradesh) condemning the university administration's decision to build a wall between BHU and BHU-Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) - at a time when a female student was molested (recently) on campus premises (coded separately).

On 4 November 2023, local people including members of Hindu right-wing groups pelted stones and set a shop on fire in Sampurna Nagar village (Kheri, Uttar Pradesh) which belonged to the family of a young man (Muslim) who was suspected to have shared an 'objectionable video' of a girl (Hindu) - that led her to commit suicide.

On 4 November 2023, around 80-100 people from two groups, including members of a farmers' union, clashed at Rajpura village under the Bhadson police station area (Patiala, Punjab) over a dispute regarding the possession of village land. 11 people were injured.

Around 4 November 2023 (as reported), a woman and her children assaulted a team from the King George's Medical University (KGMU) construction department, by pelting bricks and stones, at KGMU in Lucknow city (Uttar Pradesh) when the team attempted to remove the woman and her children for illegally residing at a house in nurses hostel area.

On 4 November 2023, local people staged a protest along the Hisar Chandigarh Road near Sher Garh village (Kaithal, Haryana) against the death of a Sarpanch (village chief) who the protesters claimed was murdered and not killed in an accident.

On 4 November 2023, around 30 members of the BJP staged a protest attempted to lay siege to the office of the DMK MLA in Kanchipuram city (Kancheepuram, Tamil Nadu) for asking the public to question the Prime Minister about his promise to deposit 15 lakh rupees to everyone's bank accounts during election campaigning in 2014. Protesters raised slogans against the MLA. Police detained the protesters.
On 4 November 2023, BJP members including ministers held a protest at Kolkata city (WB) against the TMC-led state government over claimed corruption. Police detained four BJP members.

On 4 November 2023, members of the VHP and the BJP staged protests at a private school in Visakhapatnam city (Andhra Pradesh) against the school authorities for not allowing a student who was wearing an Ayyappa scarf (Hindu religious clothing) from entering the classroom. Protesters demanded an apology from the principal and teachers and sought action against them.

On 4 November 2023, CPI(M) members held a massive sit-in and a protest rally at Diglipur town (North and Middle Andaman district, A&NI) against the BJP-led central government to demand a CBI investigation into renovation work of a national highway, end to frequent power cuts and adequate supply of water.

On 4 November 2023, CPI(M) members held a sit-in protest at Billiground town (North and Middle Andaman district, A&NI) against the BJP-led central government to demand a CBI investigation into renovation work of a national highway, end to frequent power cuts and adequate supply of water.

On 4 November 2023, CPI(M) members along with auto union members held a massive protest march at Rangat town (North and Middle Andaman district, A&NI) against the BJP-led central government to demand a CBI investigation into renovation work of a national highway, end to frequent power cuts and adequate supply of water.

On 4 November 2023, almost 150 DSS supporters joined by Shiv Sena (Uddhav Balasaheb Thackeray) held a protest at Jammu city (J&K) against the BJP-led central government and enforcement directorate over summons to their leader (a former minister) on false charges.

On 4 November 2023, farmers of Khejdiya, Gujran, and other villagers staged a protest on Tal-Alote road (Ratlam, Madhya Pradesh) demanding action against a fertilizer shop operator for selling sub-standard fertilizer. police confiscated a few sacks of fertilizers and asked the agriculture department to investigate the allegations.
