On 6 November 2023, villagers staged a protest near the near Hosakote forest quarters in Bandipur Tiger Reserve (BTR) in Sargur town (Mysuru, Karnataka) after a farmer and former member of the gram panchayat (village administrative unit) was attacked and killed by a tiger. Protesters accused the forest officials of negligence and demanded compensation for the deceased's family.

On 6 November 2023, a large number of locals staged demonstrations in Lamshang town (Manipur) demanding the police to take action and rescue two students who had been abducted by unidentified assailants (coded separately) amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities. The rioters burned tyres and put boulders in the middle of the road to mark their demonstration.

On 6 November 2023, locals held a protest at Chandihar area in Bani block area (Kathua district, J&K) against the authorities over not constructing drainage along the roads damaging their lands alongside the road and demanded compensation for the loss.

On 6 November 2023, family members and relatives of a deceased person held a protest by blocking a road at Kathua city (J&K) to demand police action in the claimed murder of their son by the in-laws and demanded justice.
On 6 November 2023, locals held a protest by locking the gates of a pump station at Udhampur city (J&K) over lack of water supply in their area.

On 7 November 2023, over 100 students from ABVP and Aryan organization clashed with each other at DAV PG college in Dehradun city (Uttarakhand) over a dispute regarding the distribution of fake student identity cards during the ongoing student elections. The police lathi-charged and diffused the clash.

On 7 November 2023, members of BKU staged a protest outside the police station in Nehian Wala village (Bathinda, Punjab) demanding the release of BKU leaders and farmers who were arrested on 6 November.

On 7 November 2023, hundreds of farmers and weavers, led by an SP MLA, staged a protest at the Urja Bhawan headquarters of Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam in Meerut city (Uttar Pradesh) against the increase in power tariffs.

On 7 November 2023, Anganwadi workers (female health workers) from across the state staged a protest and burned an effigy at Tikoniya Park in Mainpuri city (Uttar Pradesh) condemning the central government for failing to address the needs of Anganwadi workers in the Union Budget. The police attempted to stop the protesters from burning an effigy but to no avail.

Around 7 November 2023 (as reported), a Hindu leader and his supporters sat on an indefinite hunger strike and dharna at the Delhi and Uttar Pradesh border near Delhi - New Delhi city (Delhi) when they were stopped from entering into Delhi - where they planned to join a protest demanding for population control law.

On 7 November 2023, around 500 people including forest guards and contractual workers staged 'day 2' of their protest outside the office of the Forest Department in Dehradun city (Uttarakhand) against the non-payment of salaries to contractual workers and failure to promote forest guards.
On 7 November 2023, students staged a protest at the PC Bagla PG College in Hathras city (Uttar Pradesh) against the non-declaration of examination results.

On 7 November 2023, several contractual female employees of 'Dial 112' emergency service went on strike and staged a sit-in protest on 'day 2' outside the Dial 112 office in Lucknow city (Uttar Pradesh) demanding better pay and benefits, and the distribution of appointment letters. The police used force to intervene and detain some protesters, which resulted in some injuries (as claimed).

On 7 November 2023, members of the Computer Teachers' Union from various districts, led by its District and State presidents, staged a protest in Tarn Taran city (Punjab) over various demands including the provision of allowances and pay scales similar to that of government employees.

On 7 November 2023, family members of the deceased staged a protest along with the body of the deceased outside the police station in Sasni town (Hathras, Uttar Pradesh) against the death of a girl which the protesters claimed was caused by a wrong medicine prescribed by an untrained doctor at the community health center.

On 7 November 2023, family members of the deceased staged a protest and placed the body of the deceased along the Degree college road in Bisalpur city (Pilibhit, Uttar Pradesh) against the death of a boy, claiming that he did not drown but was murdered.

On 7 November 2023, family members of the deceased staged a protest at the Khatu Shyam Hospital in Kasganj city (Uttar Pradesh) against the death of a woman, post-delivery, which the protesters claimed was caused by the doctor's negligence.

On 7 November 2023, a gangster-turned-social activist and his supporters staged a protest, raising slogans, at the Sarvhitkari Vidya Mandir School in Rampura Phul city (Bathinda, Punjab) accusing the school of ignoring the Punjabi dialect. The police intervened and detained the protesters.

On 7 November 2023, thousands of DSS supporters held a protest at Jammu city (J&K) against the BJP-led central government and enforcement directorate over the arrest of their leader (a former minister) on claimed false charges.

On 7 November 2023, thousands of farmers drawn from Paikamal, Rajabodasambar, Jharbandh, Gaisilet, Sohela, and Bijepur under the aegis of Padampur Upakahanda Rajabodasambar Krushak Sangathan, a farmer's forum, took out a protest rally through Padampur town (Bargarh, Odisha) demanding the creation of a separate district.

On 7 November 2023, fishermen along with the with family members of 64 fishermen who were arrested by the Sri Lankan Navy, led by the All Mechanised Boats Fishermen Association staged a protest by launching a hunger strike in Thangachimadam village (Ramanathapuram, Tamil Nadu) demanding the DMK-led state government to demand the immediate release of the arrested fishermen. Protesters also demanded compensation and said that all the 133 fishing boats seized by the Sril Lankan Navy should be released.
On 7 November 2023, several paramedics held a protest at Srinagar city (J&K) over being disengaged without prior notice and demanded their reinstatement.

On 7 November 2023, thousands of Anganwadi workers (community health workers, mostly women) held a protest march in Patna city (Bihar) demanding an increase in their honorarium. Police used water cannons and batons to disperse the Anganwadi workers when they crossed the barricade and attempted to gherao (surround) the Bihar assembly.
On 7 November 2023, a large number of Asha workers (female health workers) held a protest at Jammu city (J&K) to demand implementation of minimum wages and increase in wages.

On 7 November 2023, Asha workers (female health workers) held a protest march from Satwari town to Jammu city (coded as Jammu city (J&K)) to demand implementation of minimum wages and increase in wages.

On 7 November 2023, scores of INC members staged protests at the INC headquarters and at the INC state president's residence in Hyderabad city (Telangana) against the INC leaders for denying tickets to their leaders for the upcoming Telangana state assembly elections.

On 7 November 2023, members of the INC staged protests in many parts of Telangana state (coded to Hyderabad) after their leader for denied tickets to contest in the upcoming Telangana state assembly elections.

On 7 November 2023, members of the INC including former Union ministers and members of the AIMC and the Kisan Cell (farmers) staged a Rythu Garjana (peasant march) protest march in Kurnool city (Andhra Pradesh) against the YSRCP-led state government for not supporting the farmers. Protesters demanded the government declare 449 mandals as drought-hit, pay compensation for the crop loss and implement an integrated crop insurance scheme.

On 7 November 2023, members of the KSU staged a protest outside the Secretariat in Thiruvananthapuram city (Kerala) against the police violence against KSU members during a protest at the Higher Education minister's residence (coded separately) against the suspected manipulation of college union election results by the members of the SFI at the Sree Kerala Varma College in Thrissur. Police used water cannons to disperse the protesters and to stop them from climbing over the barricades. A few protesters were injured and shouted slogans to mark their protest.

On 7 November 2023, members of the Unorganised Workers Federation (UWF) staged a protest in Chennai city (Tamil Nadu) demanding the BJP-led Union government to withdraw four sets of anti-labour laws. Protesters also submitted a petition to the authorities and demanded the renewal and payment by unions to be simplified, a sexual harassment complaints committee to be set up, and the benefits to the members of the board to be increased.

On 7 November 2023, IT professionals under the aegis of the Progressive Techie took out a night walk' protest march in n front of Info park Kochi campus in Kochi city (Ernakulam, Kerala) against the Thrikkakara municipality's decision to close eateries in the area between 11 p.m. and 4 a.m.

On 7 November 2023, almost 200 shopkeepers held a sit-in protest at Satwari town (Jammu district, J&K) against the closure of the shops and the potential damage that maybe caused to their shops and houses due to highway construction.
On 7 November 2023, a large number of traders held a protest at Jammu city (J&K) against the widening of the highway by the national highway authority of India affecting their livelihood.

On 7 November 2023, several organisations including the Langthabal Kendra Clubs' Coordinating Committee and the Langthabal Kendra Meira Paibi Coordinating Committee (Women Torch Bearers) (likely Meitei) staged sit-in protests at the gate of the MLA's residence in Mayang Imphal town (Imphal West, Manipur) condemning the attack amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities.

On 7 November 2023, several organisations including the Langthabal Kendra Clubs' Coordinating Committee, the Langthabal Kendra Meira Paibi Coordinating Committee (Women Torch Bearers) (likely Meitei), the Taragi Cheishu (Meitei group), the JNIMS Auto Drivers' Association, the JNIMS teaching & non-teaching staff, the JNIMS Students' Association, nurses and other staffers staged a sit-in protest in front of the Jawaharlal Nehru Institute of Medical Sciences (JNIMS) Administrative Block and at the gate of the JNIMS director's residence in Imphal town (Imphal West, Manipur) condemning the attack amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities.

On 7 November 2023, the people of Awang Sekmai and Kangla-tongbi under the aegis of the Coordinating Committee Sekmai-Kanglatongbi Kanba Lup, Awang Sekmai Kanba Nupi Lup and Sekmai SC Development Committee staged a protest in Awang Sekmai village (Imphal West, Manipur) demanding the authorities to take action and rescue two students who had been abducted by unidentified assailants (coded separately) amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities.

On 7 November 2023, representatives of Imagi Meira (Women) (likely Meitei) staged a protest at the Raj Bhavan in Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) demanding the free movement of traffic on the national highway, the adequate deployment of security and a plea to find the bodies of two Meitei students who had been abducted by unidentified assailants (coded separately) amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities. Protesters also submitted a memorandum to the Governor to mark their protest.

On 7 November 2023, around 500 people from Olavanna and Perumanna villages along with a National Secular Conference MLA staged a protest at the Kozhikode Collectorate in Kozhikode city (Kerala) demanding the authorities to release the compensation due to the landowners who had surrendered their property to the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) for the Palakkad-Kozhikode Greenfield Highway.

On 7 November 2023, students at a government school staged a protest at the school in Lakkalakatti village (Gadag, Karnataka) against the school authorities for not providing them good food under the government's midday meal scheme. Protesters locked up the school and raised slogans to mark their protest. They also demanded the officials to transfer the school headmaster.

On 7 November 2023, students of Don Bosco High School (likely Meitei) staged a sit-in protest in front of the school in Langjing village (Imphal West, Manipur) demanding the police to take action and rescue two students who had been abducted by unidentified assailants (coded separately) amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities. Protesters held placards to mark their protest.

On 7 November 2023, TMC members and residents including professionals and traders holding a sit-in protest were joined by a former BJP minister at Shantiniketan city (Birbhum district, WB) over the name of a renowned Bengali writer missing from the plaque at a university and demanded that the name be included.

On 7 November 2023, TMCP members held a protest at Siliguri city (Darjeeling district, WB) against the college administration not allowing third and fifth semester students from appearing in the upcoming examination.
On 7 November 2023, scores of acid attack victims (women) held a protest in Bhubaneswar city (Khordha, Odisha) demanding justice and compensation.

On 7 November 2023, inmates of all the ladies' hostels and other students blocked the entrance of Sambalpur University's administrative building and staged a dharna (sit-in protest) in Sambalpur city (Odisha) against the entry of outsiders into the campus after a student was harassed.

On 7 November 2023, as many as 500 residents of the Tamil Nadu Urban Habitat Development Board tenements staged a protest on the Vandalur-Wallajah Road in Serapanacheri hamlet in Sriperumbudur town (Kancheepuram, Tamil Nadu) demanding basic civic amenities including drinking water, street lights and roads.

On 7 November 2023, members of Chodnekarancho Awaz (rights group) staged a protest in Chorao island (North Goa, Goa) against the decision to increase the prices of ferry tickers at the Chorao ferry point. Protesters also condemned the government for not proper ferry services for the people of Chorao. Protesters demanded 24-hour ferry services and the construction of a bridge connecting the island of Chorao to the main land.
On 7 November 2023, locals held a protest at Kathua city (J&K) against the anti-encroachment drive by the authorities.

On 7 November 2023, members of the Adivasi Hakkula Porata Samiti, also known as Tudum Debba (tribal rights organisation) staged a protest Adilabad town (Telangana) against the INC for replacing an Adivasi candidate with a member of the Lambada community in the Boath assembly constituency for the upcoming Telangana state assembly elections. Protesters burned an effigy of the Telangana state president and demanded an explanation from the INC as why the nominee was changed.

On 7 November 2023, BJP members and supporters of a BJP leader staged a protest at the BJP state office in Hyderabad city (Telangana) after their leader was not given a ticket to contest from the Vemulawada constituency for the upcoming Telangana state assembly elections.
On 7 November 2023, BJP MLAs staged a protest outside the legislative assembly in Patna city (Bihar) over the use of water cannons on Anganwadi workers (coded separately).

actor2: Police Forces of India (2014-) Assam Rifles
text: On 7 November 2023, Kuki-Zo women staged a protest and attempted to dismantle the Assam Rifles check post along Tiddim road to rescue 5 armed Kuki assailants in Mata village (Churachandpur, Manipur) following their arrest amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. Assam Rifles personnel lathi (baton) charged the crowd to disperse them and injured around 17 women. The arrested were later released following a minor scuffle between the protesters and Assam Rifles personnel.

On 8 November 2023, members of ABVP staged a protest outside the Deputy commissioner's office in Shimla city (Himachal Pradesh) demanding action against members of the Students Federation of India (SFI) whom the protesters accused of spreading violence in educational institutions.

On 8 November 2023, a large number of members and leaders of BJP and the BJP-MM staged a protest, raising slogans, near the Bihar Bhawan in Delhi - Chanakya Puri (New Delhi, Delhi) demanding the resignation of the Bihar Chief Minister (Janata Dal) for his vulgar (as claimed) remarks against women - stating that women's education is essential for population control.

On 8 November 2023, members of the BJP-MM and former Municipal Commissioner (MC), led by the BJP-MM State president, staged a protest at the Sheran Wala Gate in Patiala city (Punjab) demanding the resignation of the Bihar Chief Minister (Janata Dal) for his vulgar (as claimed) remarks against women - stating that women's education is essential for population control.

On 8 November 2023, the Haryana BKU Chief and a BKU District president joined hundreds of farmers and weavers, led by an SP MLA, during 'Day 2' of their protest at the Urja Bhawan headquarters of Pashchimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam in Meerut city (Uttar Pradesh) against the increase in power tariffs.

On 8 November 2023, members of INC staged protests in the Delhi National Capital Region (NCR) (coded as Delhi - New Delhi city, Delhi) against the lack of action from the state authorities against the drastic rise in air pollution in the region.

On 8 November 2023, members of INC staged a protest, led by the INC and AIMC District presidents, outside the police station in Doiwala town (Dehradun, Uttarakhand) against the lack of police action against members of the BJP who had a dispute with a female INC District president during the student elections. Both INC and BJP members had filed a case against one another.

On 8 November 2023, a large number of members of INC, led by an INC MLA (former state minister), staged a protest in Faridabad city (Haryana) against the state government's lack of action against the drastic rise in air pollution in the city.

On 8 November 2023, members of the Punjab State Ministerial Staff Union initiated a '5-day' pen-down strike and staged a protest at the Government Medical College in Amritsar city (Punjab) demanding the implementation of the old pension scheme and the disbursal of dearness allowance arrears.

On 8 November 2023, local people, led by the President of Naujawan Bharat Sabha (NBS), staged a protest in Kurukshetra city (Haryana) against the state government's decision to allocate land from a Theme Park towards the development of a Sikh museum.

On 8 November 2023, MGNREGA workers from various villages gathered under the banner of Pendu Mazdoor Union and staged a protest outside the Block Development and Panchayat Officer (BDPO) office in Mehatpur village (Jalandhar, Punjab) against the non-implementation of certain guarantees provided to workers under the MNREGA Act and demanded the disbursal of pending dues.

On 8 November 2023, students staged a sit-in protest along the road outside the gate of Punjabi University in Patiala city (Punjab) demanding action against a professor whom the protesters accused of mentally harassing a student who later committed suicide. The protesters also demanded the cancellation of FIRs registered against students for assaulting the accused (professor) (coded separately).

Around 8 November 2023 (as reported), students supporting a professor facing harassment allegations staged a hunger strike and protest at the university in Patiala city ( Punjab), demanding action against the students who assaulted a professor and called for better security at the university.

On 8 November 2023, students of Banaras Hindu University (BHU), including members of NSUI, staged a protest march, carrying banners and posters, in Varanasi city (Uttar Pradesh) demanding action against the accused involved in the molestation of a female student within the university compounds (coded separately).

On 8 November 2023, 6 people assaulted 3 members of a family, with a rod, resulting in the death of one, in Marha Macchi Jhil village (Auraiya, Uttar Pradesh) after the family members of the woman raised objections against one of the assailants for urinating outside their house. 2 members of the family suffered injuries.

On 8 November 2023, leaders of the state unit of BJP Mahila Morcha staged burned the effigy Bihar Chief Minister and held a protest near Ram Mandir in Bhubaneswar city (Khordha, Odisha) against the derogatory remarks made by Bihar Chief Minister on women in the State Assembly.

On 8 November 2023, members of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) staged a protest in Jharsuguda town (Odisha) demanding a detailed investigation to ascertain who was involved in the road accident involving the Jharsuguda MLA's brother. The police commissioner has assured a detailed probe into the incident.
On 8 November 2023, BJP members held a protest at Kharibari town (Darjeeling district, WB) against the TMC-led state government over claimed corruption in ration distribution in the state.
On 8 November 2023, BJP members held a protest at Nidhirampur village (Bankura district, WB) over the claimed murder of a BJP member in same area (coded separately).

On 8 November 2023,Left parties, including CITU, and civil society organizations organized an 'Ekjutta March' (United Front) from Sainik Market to Albert Ekka Chowk in Ranchi city (Jharkhand) in protest against the war in the Gaza strip, the 'massacre' of Palestinian civilians, and demanded an end to the war.

On 8 November 2023, members of the Loadmen Federation affiliated to the CITU staged a protest outside the Tamil Nadu State Marketing Corporation (TASMAC) warehouse in Ramanathapuram city (Tamil Nadu) demanding an increase in their wages for unloading boxes in TASMAC warehouses.

On 8 November 2023, members of the Loadmen Federation affiliated to the CITU staged a protests outside Tamil Nadu State Marketing Corporation (TASMAC) warehouses across Tamil Nadu state (coded to Chennai) demanding an increase in their wages for unloading boxes in TASMAC warehouses.

On 8 November 2023, members of left parties including the CPI, the CPI(M), the CPI (ML) Praja Poru and unions including the CITU, the AITUC, YSRCP MLAs, former TDP ministers, former TDP MLAs, MLCs, members of the JSP, the INC, journalists, the AICTU, AIDWA, NFIW, and members of the Mahila Samakhya (women's group) under the aegis of the Visakha Ukku Parirakshana Porata Committee (VUPPC) and the Praja Sanghala JAC (formed for the protection of Visakhapatnam Steel Plant (VSP) staged a protest near the Gurajada statue in Visakhapatnam city (Andhra Pradesh) to mark the 1000th day of relay hunger strikes against the BJP-led Union government's decision to privatise the Visakhapatnam Steel Plant.

On 8 November 2023, thousands of teachers, students and workers led by CPI, CPI(ML) Liberation, SUCI, RSP, CPI(M) and Left Front members held a protest at Kolkata city (WB) against Israel's military offensive in Gaza and demanded a US-brokered ceasefire to halt the war.

On 8 November 2023, Scheduled Caste (Dalit) residents of Arunachalapuram staged a protest on the Tirunelveli-Tenkasi state highway road in front of the Alangulam police station in Alangulam town (Tenkasi, Tamil Nadu) demanding protection after a Dalit resident was assaulted by members of a Most Backward Classes (MBC) group for unknown reasons (coded separately).

On 8 November 2023, a group of 12 masked men (likely farmers) burned down two tractors filled with sugarcane in Karadga village (Belagavi, Karnataka) for transporting the sugarcane to Maharashtra even before the price was announced. Farmers' organizations have asked farmers to not transport sugarcane until factories announce a price.

On 8 November 2023, postgraduate medical students, dental students and house surgeons staged protests in all government medical colleges across Kerala state (coded to Thiruvananthapuram) with a list of demands including an increase in their stipends, decreasing the PG course fee, increasing senior residency seats and more hostel facilities for resident doctors.

On 8 November 2023, house surgeons and resident doctors affiliated to the Kerala Medical Post Graduates Association, Kerala House Surgeons Association, and Dental House Surgeons Association staged a protest outside the Government Medical College in Kozhikode city (Kerala) as part of a 24-hour strike with a list of demands including an increase in their stipends, decreasing the PG course fee, increasing senior residency seats and more hostel facilities for resident doctors.

On 8 November 2023, members of the Kerala Medical Post Graduate Association and the Kerala Government Medical College Teachers' Association staged protests and protest marches in Thiruvananthapuram city (Kerala) with a list of demands including an increase in their stipends, decreasing the PG course fee, increasing senior residency seats and more hostel facilities for resident doctors.

On 8 November 2023, supporters of an INC leader staged a protest at the Gandhi Bhavan in Hyderabad city (Telangana) after the leader was not issued B-form (nomination form) even after announcement of his candidature for the upcoming Telangana state assembly elections.

On 8 November 2023, INC members held a massive protest by blocking a road at Rangat town (North and Middle Andaman district, A&NI) against the BJP-led central government to demand reconstruction and repair of a highway.

On 8 November 2023, INC members held a protest by blocking a road at Diglipur town (North and Middle Andaman district, A&NI) against the BJP-led central government to demand reconstruction and repair of a highway.

On 8 November 2023, INC members including an elected representative held a protest by blocking a road at Baratang Jetty town (North and Middle Andaman district, A&NI) against the BJP-led central government to demand reconstruction and repair of a highway.

On 8 November 2023, workers along with an INC MLA staged a flash sit-in protest in front of a coffee estate at Hedadalu in Chikkamagaluru town (Chikmagalur, Karnataka) after a worker was trampled to death by a wild elephant on the estate. Protesters condemned the forest officials for not taking measures to mitigate wild animal attacks and demanded compensation for the relatives of the victim.
On 8 November 2023, members of the All Assam Construction Workers' Union (AACWU) held a protest in Guwahati city (Kamrup Metropolitan, Assam) over various demands.

On 8 November 2023, members of the Tamil Nadu Village Administrative Officers' Association staged a protest in Krishnagiri city (Tamil Nadu) demanding justice for a Village Administrative Officer in Uthangarai who died by suicide over the delay in the payment of their salaries and subsequent personal debts.

On 8 November 2023, sanitation workers staged a protest at the panchayat office in Alangulam town (Tenkasi, Tamil Nadu) demanding the administration to pay them their pending salaries for the month of October.

On 8 November 2023, local residents, environmentalists and a retired IAS officer staged a protest at the Ooty Lake and Boat House in Udhagamandalam city (The Nilgiris, Tamil Nadu) demanding the administration to put a stop to the illegal construction of a zipline and rope bridge in the area. Protesters also condemned the destruction of the wetland surrounding the Udhagamandalam Railway Station.

Around 8 November 2023 (as reported), members of MNS vandalized the premises of Siddharth Multipurpose Society in Pune city (Maharashtra), during a demonstration, demanding strict action against the accused in a sexual assault case (coded separately).

On 8 November 2023, an MLA belonging to the PMK along with a few farmers staged a protest outside the Uzhavar Sandhai (farmers' markets) in the Suramangalam locality in Salem city (Tamil Nadu) saying that there were irregularities in all farmers' markets in Salem district. Protesters said that the price of goods were higher than the marker price and that government officials were buying tomatoes from a single trader after receiving commissions. Protesters demanded action against the authorities.

On 8 November 2023, students and youth leaders along with members of the SFI, the AISF, and the PDSU staged a protest as part of the 'KG-to-PG' bandh call at the SRR and CVR Degree College in Vijayawada city (Krishna, Andhra Pradesh) against the BJP-led Union government's decision to privatise the Visakhapatnam Steel Plant. Protesters said that thousands of people would lose their jobs if the plant was privatised. Police arrested the protesters.

On 8 November 2023, members of Swabhiman Paksha, led by a former Member of Parliament, started an indefinite sit-in protest in Jaysingpur town (Kolhapur, Maharashtra) demanding the sugar mills pay Rs 400 per tonne to sugar cane farmers for the past season as a share from the 'windfall' profits made.

On 8 November 2023, members of Shiv Sena (UBT), including a former corporator, held a 'halla-bol' protest at Kolhapur Municipal Corporation (KMC) headquarters in Kolhapur city (Maharashtra) over the poor condition of city roads.

On 8 November 2023, lecturers and a group of girl students staged protests at Emarti Devi Women's Degree College in Cuttack city (Odisha) demanding the immediate transfer of the principal over claimed misbehavior.

On 8 November 2023, thousands of people, mostly tribal students under the aegis of the Tangkhul Katamnao Saklong (TKS) students' union staged a protest march in Ukhrul town (Manipur) to demand the speedy implementation of the Indo-Naga peace process amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities. Protesters raised slogans to highlight their demands.

On 8 November 2023, fifty teachers staged a protest by laying siege to the Office Chamber of Education Minister in the Babupara locality in Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) demanding the release of their pending salaries amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities.

On 8 November 2023, local women from the Rayaibari-Killa area staged a protest and blocked the Udaipur Killa road in Udaipur town (Gomati, Tripura) over the acute shortage of drinking water plaguing their community.
On 8 November 2023, women held a protest at Rajouri city (J&K) against the water department over lack of water supply in their area.

On 8 November 2023, members of Subash Sangathan, a non-political body, held a protest with a commode in hand in front of the Cuttack Municipal Corporation (CMC) office in Cuttack city (Odisha) over defunct public toilets in the city.

On 8 November 2023, people staged a protest at the Azad Maidan in Panaji city (North Goa, Goa) demanding peace in the Middle East amidst the ongoing conflict between Israel and Palestine. Protesters said that thousands of people including women and children were being killed in the war and condemned the Indian government for abstaining from voting during the United Nations resolution calling for a ceasefire in Gaza.

On 8 November 2023, locals staged a protest in the Old Rajarajeswaripeta area in Vijayawada city (Krishna, Andhra Pradesh) after a minor boy died after falling into a drain. Protesters said that the municipal officials had not done anything about the open drains despite multiple complaints.

On 8 November 2023, residents of Iringal village near Vadakara under the aegis of the Iringal Underpass Protest Committee took out a protest march to the office of the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) in Kozhikode city (Kerala) demanding the authorities to construct an underpass across National Highway 66 at Iringal junction. Protesters said that the village had been divided in half by the highway and demanded a solution to their problem.

On 8 November 2023, residents of Sahakar Nagar staged a flash protest on the highway in Bengaluru city (Bengaluru Urban, Karnataka) against the issue of frequent flooding in the area. Protesters accused the accused Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike (BBMP) of negligence.

On 8 November 2023, about 50 residents of Mahatma Gandhi Nagar staged a protest in Tindivanam town (Villupuram, Tamil Nadu) after municipality officials removed a Vinayagar (Hindu) idol from a public spot. Protesters threatened to go on an indefinite strike.

On 8 November 2023, locals of Wangkhei AC staged a sit-in protest at the community hall of Citizens' Club at Wangkhei in Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) against the attack by unknown assailants on a truck transporting NFSA rice (coded separately). The police lathi-charged and arrested 7 people. Many people were injured.

The protesters demanded compensation for the family members of the deceased.

The rioters argued with the Vice President and grabbed him by the collar. Police intervened and escorted him out of the place.

On 15 November 2023, locals along with the Cuncolim Municipal Council (CMC) chairperson belonging to the INC and a lawyer staged a protest in Cuncolim town (South Goa, Goa) demanding the state government to implement rules and restrictions in the functioning of the Cuncolim industrial estate including removal of hazardous waste left behind by an industry.

On 15 November 2023, supporters of an INC leader (former MP) staged a protest in the Hayat Nagar locality in Hyderabad city (Telangana) after the police conducted a midnight search at his residence after they received a complaint about money distribution in connection with the upcoming Telangana state assembly elections. Protesters said that the police were acting on the behest of the BRS and raised slogans against the BRS and an MLA seeking re-election.

On 15 November 2023, members of the INC's Scheduled Caste department staged a protest on Anna Salai road in Chennai city (Tamil Nadu) against the BJP-led union government for reducing the funds meant for the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS) which guaranteed work for 100 days for unemployed persons in rural areas.

On 15 November 2023, people affiliated to the Anti-K-Rail SilverLine Janakiya Samithi along with an INC MP, a former Kerala Congress (M) MLA and a member of the INTUC staged a protest march in front of the railway administrative office in Kochi city (Ernakulam, Kerala) against the state government's plan to go ahead with a semi high-speed rail project. Protesters said that the project was not technically, financially and socially feasible and would hamper the development of the state.

On 15 November 2023, members of the BJP including a large number of women staged a protest in front of the Nadakkavu police station in Kozhikode city (Kerala) against the police for calling an actor and BJP member for questioning in a case filed by a woman journalist accusing him of misbehaving with her. Protester attempted to lay siege to the police station and held placards to express their solidarity.

On 15 November 2023, members of the CPI(M) including a former MP launched a 'Prajarakshana Bheri' (people's protection) protest march in Vijayawada city (Krishna, Andhra Pradesh) against the BJP-Union government and its internal policies favouring corporate companies and external policies supporting Israel amidst the ongoing Israel Palestine conflict.

On 15 November 2023, family members of a Dalit man who was assaulted by a group of assailants and died (coded separately) along with members of pro-Dalit organisations including the Dalit Sene staged a protest outside the Deputy Commissioner's office in Gulbarga city (Kalaburagi, Karnataka) with the deceased's body demanding action against the accused. Protesters raised slogans against the police department, a minister and the state government.

On 15 November 2023, unemployed youth and members of the IYC, the Telangana Jana Samithi, the CPI and the INC launched a bus yatra (journey) protest from the Martyrs' Memorial in Gun Park in Hyderabad city (Telangana) to highlight the faults of the BRS-led state government the BJP-led Union government including the failure to provide employment opportunities to the state's youth.

On 15 November 2023, members of the IYC staged a protest in front of the Deputy Superintendent of Police (DySP) (Margao) in Margao city (South Goa, Goa) demanding action against the hawkers and beggars at the Navelim feast fair, Protesters said that the locals were being troubled by the hawkers and asked the DySP to deploy additional police personnel at the fair.

On 15 November 2023, members of the KSU staged a sit-in protest at the Cochin University of Science and Technology (Cusat) in Kochi city (Ernakulam, Kerala) against the delay in punishing members of the SFI in connection with an incident where members of the members of the KSU and the SFI clashed with each other and KSU members were injured (coded separately).

On 15 November 2023, pournamikas (sanitation workers) under the aegis of the Karnataka State City Corporation, the City Municipal Council, and the Taluk Panchayat Outsourced Pourakarmikas Association held a protest march to the Deputy Commissioner's office in Mandya city (Karnataka) demanding the state government to bring their contracts under the direct payment system, to also fill up vacant posts and to regularise their services.

On 15 November 2023, teachers from 26 districts affiliated to the Andhra Pradesh Teachers' Federation (APTF) and the Andhra Non-Gazetted Government Officers Association (APNGO's Association) staged a protest at the Dharna Chowk in Vijayawada city (Krishna, Andhra Pradesh) against the YSRCP-led state government demanding the payment of pending arrears and the restoration of the Old Pension Scheme (OPS).

On 15 November 2023, over 1000 tribal people including members of the Mission Political Reservation for STs of Goa, and members of the INC staged a protest march from the Azad Maidan to the Chief Minister's residence in Panaji city (North Goa, Goa) to submit a memorandum with a list of demands including receiving political reservation for Scheduled Tribes (ST) communities before the 2024 general assembly elections. Police stopped the protesters from marching towards the Chief Minister's house.

On 15 November 2023, residents of Kottaramthuruth ward including women and children staged a protest on the coastal road in Perumathura village (Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala) demanding the administration to take measures to provide drinking water in the area.

On 15 November 2023, residents staged a protest on the Ocheri - Arakkonam main road in Melapulam village (Ranipet, Tamil Nadu) opposing the open discharge of waste water behind the settlements. Protesters said that it posed a health risk to the residents of the area and demanded alternative plot for the waste water to be directed to.

On 15 November 2023, residents staged a protest in front of the taluk (subdivision of a district) office in Annur town (Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu) demanding administration to take measures to prevent the inundation of rain water in residential localities that were caused by the encroachments near the water. Protesters also demanded the administration to clear the encroachments.

On 15 November 2023, members of the TDP including an MLA along with beneficiaries of an Andhra Pradesh Township And Infrastructure Development Corporation (TIDCO) colony staged a protest in Palacole town (West Godavari, Andhra Pradesh) against a bank loan issue. Members of the YSRCP staged a counter protest against the TDP. Police detained the TDP MLA.

On 15 November 2023, a section of fishermen affiliated to the Muslim Jamat staged a protest and attempted to lay siege at a function organised by the Kerala government at the Vizhinjam port in Vizhinjam village (Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala) demanding compensation from the government for giving up their land for the construction of the port. Police forcibly removed the protesters from the area but they continued to protest on the national highway.
On 15 November 2023, 5 men molested a minor Dalit girl and assaulted a Dalit man (the brother), with a rod, in Pilibhit district (Uttar Pradesh) for unidentified reasons.

Around 15 November 2023 (as reported), hundreds of BJP members gheraoed (surrounded) a police station in Jashpur district (coded to Jashpurnagar, Chhattisgarh) demanding action against INC members for intimidating a woman BJP supporter ahead of 2nd phase of legislative assembly elections.

Around 15 November 2023 (as reported), 10-12 persons assaulted a Ranchi Civil Court advocate, an elected member of the District Bar Association, and a local IYC leader at the advocate's farmhouse in the Silda area (Khunti district, Jharkhand) over a land dispute. The advocate and IYC leaders were injured.

On 15 November 2023, members of BJP gheraoed (surrounded) block offices and held a protest in various districts of Odisha (coded to Bhubaneswar city, Khordha district) as part of a statewide movement 'Janaakrosh Block gherao', against claimed corruption by the BJD-led government.

Around 15 November 2023 (as reported), conservancy workers staged a protest in Madurai city (Tamil Nadu) demanding the DMK-led state government to withdraw a government order which allowed the civic administration to recruit private agencies and outsource the task of clearing and disposing garbage.

On 15 November 2023, six members of a Hindu right-wing group stripped a tribal youth and assaulted him with a belt, slippers, and sticks in Betul city (Madhya Pradesh). Conflicting reports on the motive - some sources state that he was assaulted on suspicion of cow smuggling while others state that it was due to a dispute over non-payment of borrowed money.

On 16 November 2023, members of BJP, led by its District president, staged a dharna (sit-in protest) in Jalandhar city (Punjab) against the AAP-led state government for failing to address various issues including hooliganism, contaminated water supply, poor sanitation and sewage, among others.
On 16 November 2023, hundreds of CITU members held a protest at Port Blair city (South Andaman district, A&NI) to demand revision of minimum wages, action against inflation among other demands.

On 16 November 2023, a large number of people including family members (Dalit) of the victims and local people staged a protest, raising slogans, in Nuh city (Haryana) against the police for failing to take action against the accused (Muslim children) who pelted stones at a group of Dalit women who were visiting the Kailash temple (coded separately).

On 16 November 2023, Kuki-Zo women folk from Lungphou and members of the KYU under the banner of the Committee on Tribal Unity (CoTU) launched a protest at Kangpokpi town (Manipur) to demand the release of the two Kuki-Zo tribals arrested by the police in connection with the missing case of two Meitei students (coded separately) amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and tribal, including Kuki-Zomi, communities in the state. Protesters staged the protest as part of the 'Indefinite Economic Blockade' announced by the CoTU.

On 16 November 2023, non-teaching employees gathered under the banner of the Maharshi Dayanand University (MDU) Non-Teaching Employees Association and staged an indefinite dharna (sit-in protest) at MDU's administrative block in Rohtak city (Haryana) against the objections raised by the audit section over various bills relating to medical reimbursement, provident fund and others. The protesters demanded the transfer of the senior auditor.

On 16 November 2023, Public Works Department (PWD) workers gathered under the banner of the PWD Joint Employees Welfare Association and staged a protest, raising slogans, at the Martyr Memorial in Agra city (Uttar Pradesh) against the non-payment of salaries.

On 16 November 2023, a large number of students staged a protest in front of the University Vice Chancellor's Office gate in Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) demanding the administration to complete the admission process for incoming students, declare the examination results and to begin the academic year amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. Protesters raised slogans to mark their protest.

On 16 November 2023, over 1600 teachers from government colleges across the state gathered under the banner of the All Haryana Government College Teachers Association (AHGCTA) and staged a protest outside the headquarters of the Higher Education Department (Shiksha Sadan) in Panchkula city (Haryana) over various issues including promotions, senior selection grade, MPhil and Ph.D. increments, and the state's online transfer policy, among others.

On 16 November 2023, TMC members and locals held a protest at Amdanga town (North 24 Parganas district, WB) over the killing of a TMC panch (village government head) in the same area (coded separately) and demanded the arrest of the persons involved. The sit-in continued until the next day.
On 16 November 2023, TMC members held a protest at Raidhaka river area in Mahishkuchi block area (Cooch Behar district, WB) over illegal sand mining in the area.

On 16 November 2023, a group of children (likely Muslim since they were located inside a Madrasa/Mosque) pelted stones at a group of women from the Dalit community in Nuh city (Haryana) while going towards, and returning from, the Kailash temple where they offered prayers. 8 women were injured and the incident was captured on CCTV.

On 16 November 2023, around 100-150 locals vandalized the property of a person (likely while they were still inside) in Nayagarh town (Odisha) after a verdict was passed by a kangaroo court over claimed encroachment on government land.

text: On 16 November 2023, a hundred local people from nearby areas staged a protest, raising slogans, along the Mau-Azamgarh train route and stopped the train near Alinagar village (Mau, Uttar Pradesh) demanding the construction of an over bridge. RPF personnel detained 2 people.

On 16 November 2023, a local trader and his family members assaulted a police team with sharp-edged weapons, canes, and rods at Netampur village under Mohammad Pur Khala police station area (Barabanki, Uttar Pradesh) when the police team attempted to free a man (another trader) who was held captive by the assailants over a dispute. 3 police personnel were injured including one serious injury, and 3 of the accused were later arrested. A video of the incident was circulated online.
On 16 November 2023, locals held a protest at Udhampur city (J&K) over waste being dumped in a park in their area.

On 16 November 2023, members of the Bishnupur Youth Citizens' Forum staged a protest march from the Bishnupur forest office to the Bishnupur DC Complex in Bishnupur town (Manipur) demanding the authorities to find and hand over two missing Meitei students to their families and to punish the culprits involved in their abduction (coded separately) amidst ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. Protesters also demanded the deployment of state forces in the adjoining areas of hill and valley districts to finding the missing students.

On 16 November 2023, members of the Langsai Thouna Kakching, a civil society organisation based in Kakching district staged a protest in Imphal city (Imphal West, Manipur) demanding the BJP-led state government to resolve the resolve the ongoing violence between Meitei and Tribal communities in the state. Protesters also submitted a memorandum to the Chief Minister demanding the administration to remove Kuki armed assailants and 'illegal immigrants who are attempting to break the territorial integrity of Manipur.' Protesters also demanded that displaced individuals be allowed to return to their homes.

On 16 November 2023, family members of the deceased staged a protest along the Gorakhpur-Maharajganj Road outside BRD Medical College in Gorakhpur city (Uttar Pradesh) against the death of a man who succumbed to his injuries after an assault and demanded action against the assailants.

On 16 November 2023, members of the DMK including MLAs launched a signature mobilisation protest campaign in Puducherry city (Puducherry) demanding the Union government to cancel the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (Undergraduate) (NEET) pre-medical examination.

On 16 November 2023, scores of farmers, mainly women, under the aegis of the All India Krishi Karmikara Sanghatane took out a protest march from the Kala Bhavan and staged a protest in front of the Deputy Commissioner's office in Dharwad city (Karnataka) demanding the state government to launch drought relief work in the district. Protesters also demanded the extension of the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS) (social scheme) and the cancellation of crop loans and school fees for the children of farmers.

On 16 November 2023, members of the Federation of Government Doctors Associations (FOGDA) which included the Democratic Tamil Nadu Government Doctors Association, the Service Doctors and Post Graduates Association, the Tamil Nadu Medical Officers Association and the Government All Doctors Association (GADA) staged a protest on the premises of the Government Omandurar Medical College Hospital in Chennai city (Tamail Nadu) demanding the DMK-led state government to implement a government order which ensured time-bound pay and allowances for doctors.

On 16 November 2023, workers of the Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (TNSTC) staged a sit-in protest at the Papanasam bus depot in Papanasam town (Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu) demanding the arrest of three persons who attacked a driver and a bus conductor in Veeravanallur. Protesters condemned the attack.

On 16 November 2023, a large number of villagers including women staged a protest by stopping a bus at the Balasamuthiram Colony in Andipatti municipality (Theni, Tamil Nadu) against the administration for not providing basic civic amenities including water, good roads and streetlights.

On 16 November 2023, members of the TDP including a former minister and members of the JSP staged a protest outside the minister's house in the Gollapudi area in Vijayawada city (Krishna, Andhra Pradesh) accusing the YRSCP leaders of transporting ash from the NTTPS (Dr Narla Tata Rao Thermal Power Corporation) illegally to earn money. Police detained the former minister at his house and prevented his followers from going to Ibrahimpatnam. Protesters demanded the authorities to stop the illegal transportation of ash and to also protect people's health.

On 16 November 2023, locals (likely Dalit based on identity of the victim) staged a demonstration in Dommeru village (West Godavari, Andhra Pradesh) after a Dalit youth died by suicide after he was detained by the police in a petty case and could not bear the humiliation. The demonstrators also pelted stones at the police, prevented ministers from entering the village and meeting the deceased's family and raised slogans against a YSRCP minister. The demonstrators also demanded the arrest of those responsible for the victim's death.

On 16 November 2023, residents of Nejaru staged a demonstration and stopped a police vehicle carrying a murder accused in Udupi city (Karnataka) after the police arrested a man accused of murdering four people and injuring a fifth person. The demonstrators pelted stones at the police van carrying the accused when the accused was brought to the victim's house as part of the investigation. The demonstrators also raised slogans and the police resorted to mild lathi (baton) charge to disperse the demonstrators.

On 16 November 2023, members of two groups of a gurdwara management committee clashed in Nayagaon village (SAS Nagar, Punjab) for unidentified reasons, ahead of the Gurpurb (Sikh religious occasion) celebrations.

On 16 November 2023, members of families under the Below Poverty Line (BPL) and a local councilor staged a sit-in protest outside the Mini secretariat in Sonipat city (Haryana) against the failure of the state government to provide possession of land to eligible BPL families under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana.

On 16 November 2023, members of the INC and BJP clashed in the Rau area of Indore city (Madhya Pradesh) on the eve of the election to the legislative assembly. Six persons were injured. Police used teargas to disperse the two groups.

On 16 November 2023, overnight, unidentified persons threw stones at the car of a BJP candidate, during door-to-door campaigning, in Amla Nankar village of Susner tehsil (Shajapur, Madhya Pradesh) on the eve of the election to the legislative assembly. The car was damaged.

On 16 November 2023, members of SS (UBT) and Balasahebanchi Shiv Sena engaged in a brief scuffle and raised slogans against each other at the Shivaji Park memorial in Mumbai city (Maharashtra) over the ownership of Shiv Sena's undivided legacy.

On 16 November 2023, members of BJP gheraoed (surrounded) block offices and held a protest in various districts of Odisha (coded to Bhubaneswar city, Khordha district) as part of a statewide movement 'Janaakrosh Block gherao', against claimed corruption by the BJD-led government.

On 16 November 2023, more than 300 members of the Hindu Munnai staged a protest in front of the Arulmigu Subramanya Swamy temple in Tiruchendur town (Thoothukudi, Tamil Nadu) after a video was posted on social media showing a temple agent collecting money from devotees for special darshan (prayer ceremony). Protesters also condemned temple administration and Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowment department's decision to increase the fees for the ceremony. Protesters raised slogans and recited prayer sings to mark their protest. Police detained the protesters.

On 25 November 2023, members of the CITU, the ASHA workers union, anganwadi workers, the AITUC, INTUC, and the Andhra Pradesh Medical & Sales Representatives Union (APMSRU) took out a bike rally protest from the Bhanugudi junction to the Ambedkar statue centre in Kakinada city (East Godavari, Andhra Pradesh) demanding the YSRCP-led state government to give farmers remunerative prices for the crops they produced. Protesters also demanded a minimum wage to workers of all sectors and 200 days of employment.
On 25 November 2023, members of AIUDF assaulted a local INC leader in Nilambazar town (Karimganj district, Assam), over political rivalry.
On 25 November 2023, farmers held a protest at Udhampur city (J&K) against the agriculture department over lack of seeds for plantation and crop farming.

On 25 November 2023, members of the Zilla Raitha Hitarakshana Samithi (District Farmer Welfare Committee) staged a protest by organising a hunger strike in Mandya city (Karnataka) demanding the INC-led Karnataka state government to not release water from the Cauvery river to the state of Tamil Nadu.

On 25 November 2023, unidentified assailants (likely Hindu based on the slogans) assaulted a visually challenged Muslim man in Gangavathi town (Koppal, Karnataka) while the victim was waiting for an autorickshaw to take him home. The assailants came on bikes, took the man to an isolated place, assaulted him, passed derogatory comments about the Muslim community and made him chant 'Jai Shri Ram'. The assailants also set the victim's beard on fire and took his money.

On 25 November 2023, farmers, MGNREGA, and construction workers, including a CPI (M) leader (former MLA), gathered under the banner of the Himachal Kisan Sabha (AIKS) and CITU, led by CITU National secretary, and staged a protest, raising slogans, outside the State secretariat in Shimla city (Himachal Pradesh) against the union government whom the protesters accused of formulating 'anti-labor and anti-people' policies, including the introduction of online attendance for MGNREGA workers. The protesters also demanded higher minimum wages, regularization of contractual workers, and Minimum Selling Price (MSP) for farm produce, among others.
On 25 November 2023, locals led by a former councillor held a protest at Jakhani town (Udhampur district, J&K) against the forest department over objections to construction of a road.

On 25 November 2023, around 250 ex-servicemen (former military) staged a dharna (sit-in protest) along the railway tracks in Shambhu village (Patiala, Punjab) when the protesters were prevented from traveling to Delhi to stage a protest against suspected irregularities in the 'One Rank One Pension' (OROP) scheme.

On 25 November 2023, government employees on election duty, including presiding officers (POs), assistant presiding officers (APOs), and other polling officials (OPOs) staged a protest at the Zilla Parishad High School in Saroornagar area in Hyderabad city (Telangana) demanding that they be given the opportunity to vote for the upcoming Telangana state assembly elections. Protesters said that they were denied the right to vote since the election authorities did not provide them with postal ballots.

On 25 November 2023, local people, members of the panchayat (village council), and a former military officer staged a protest in Mana Talwandi village (Kapurthala, Punjab) against a private company whom the protesters accused of extracting soil beyond the permissible limit from agriculture land purchased for the construction of the Delhi-Katra Expressway.

On 25 November 2023, health workers, medical nursing and paramedical students staged a protest at the Government Medical College in Kochi city (Ernakulam, Kerala) in solidarity with the people of Gaza amidst the ongoing conflict between Israel and Palestine. Protesters condemned the death of health workers and paid tributes to the victims of the conflict.
On 25 November 2023, members of the INC and the BRS clashed with each other in the Khairatabad area of Hyderabad city (Telangana) in relation to the upcoming Telangana state assembly elections.

On 25 November 2023, members of the Kerala Pradesh School Teachers' Association (KPSTA) along with a former INC minister took out a protest march to the State Council of Educational Research and Training (SCERT) in the Poojappura locality in Thiruvananthapuram city (Tamil Nadu) against the LDF-led state government for preparing the new school curriculum without consulting people of different ideologies and beliefs.

On 25 November 2023, members of the UDF including an INC MP and members of the RMPI took out a protest march to the office of the District Police Chief in Vadakara town (Kozhikode, Kerala) against the police for not taking action against a group of DFYI members who attacked an INC leader and damaged his vehicle (coded separately). Protesters said that the CPI(M)-led state government was sanctioning violence against political rivals in the name of Navakerala Sadas (public outreach program).

On 25 November 2023, non-teaching employees staged a protest by forming a human chain and taking out a symbolic funeral procession of the university administration at Aligarh Muslim University (AMU) in Aligarh city (Uttar Pradesh) over a ten-point demand which included an increase in salaries of daily wage employees. The protesters have been on strike for the past 29 days.

On 25 November 2023, the producer of the Odia film 'Pratha', and many artists joined the indefinite dharna at lower PMG Square in Bhubaneswar (Khordha, Odisha) over the fulfillment of several demands, including 'Odia Chalachitra Banchao' (save Odiya cinema), making rules for multiplexes and cinema halls to mandatorily run Odia films for at least 15 days as in other states, making Odia films tax-free, etc.

On 25 November 2023, hundreds of laborers under the aegis of Paradip Port Labourers Union staged a dharna (sit-in protest) in front of the Paradip International Cargo Terminal (PICT) gate in Paradip town (Jagatsinghapur district, Odisha), demanding pending salary and reinstatement of laid-off employees among others.

On 25 November 2023, TAIT-qualified aspirants staged a protest outside the Education department's office in Pune city (Maharashtra) over the delay in the recruitment process of teachers in Zilla parishad, municipal council, corporation, and private aided and semi-aided schools.

On 25 November 2023, a section of Kerala State Road Transport Corporation (KSRTC) employees staged a protest march to the Nava Kerala Sadas (CPI(M) event) in Kozhikode city (Kerala) demanding the government to take measures to resolve the financial crisis faced by the KSRTC.

On 25 November 2023, locals assaulted two truck drivers on the outskirts of Jagdalpur town (Bastar, Chhattisgarh) after the duo was caught sexually assaulting a minor. The locals later handed over the duo to the police.

On 25 November 2023, two groups clashed in Fatehpur city (Sikar district, Rajasthan) over likely political rivalry during the voting for legislative assembly elections. One person was injured. Police detained some people in connection to the incident.

On 25 November 2023, two persons including a policeman were injured due to stone pelting in Sanwler village of Kaman taluka (Bharatpur district, Rajasthan) over likely political rivalry during the voting for legislative assembly elections.

On 25 November 2023, a vehicle was damaged due to stone pelting after an altercation between the polling agent and another person in Bari seat (Dholpur district, Rajasthan) turned violent over likely political rivalry during the voting for legislative assembly elections.
On 25 November 2023, students held a protest at Udhampur city (J&K) over not being given seats in buses and mini buses plying the roads in the city.

On 25 November 2023, family members of the deceased staged a protest, along with the bodies of the deceased, outside the Commander Hospital in Delhi - Hastsal area (West Delhi, Delhi) against the death of 3 people due to electrocution while repairing the hospital water tank's motor. The protesters accused the hospital of negligence.

On 25 November 2023, family members of the deceased and local people staged a protest near Tarash Temple in Vrindavan city (Mathura, Uttar Pradesh) against the death of a child who was hit and killed by a school bus.

Around 25 November 2023 (as reported), passengers staged a protest at the railway station in Moradabad district (Uttar Pradesh) demanding a ticket refund after train operations were disrupted due to the farmers' protest along railway tracks in Punjab (coded separately).

On 25 November 2023, locals held a protest at Sitalpur town (Maldah district, WB) against police over a road accident involving police in which two persons were killed and two others were left injured, claiming the driver to be under the influence of liquor and demanded justice.

On 25 November 2023, residents of the 17 villages within Section-(3) of Showuba-Pangsha (East-West Corridor road) under the aegis of a 'Public Forum' staged a protest at Satakha town (Zunheboto district, Nagaland) against bad roads.

On 25 November 2023, more than 150 persons under the aegis of the Members of Walk For Palestine (social media initiative) staged a protest near the Rajarathinam stadium in Chennai city (Tamil Nadu) in solidarity with the people of Palestine amidst ongoing conflict between Israel and Palestine. Protesters highlighted the 'genocide in Palestine' and called for a ceasefire.

On 25 November 2023, residents of Cottonpeta village along with an injured youth staged a protest at the camp office of the Rajamahendravaram MP in Rajahmundry city (East Godavari, Andhra Pradesh) against the increasing attacks and instances of vandalism by criminal groups in the area. Protesters said that they were living in fear especially after a recent attack against a youth. Protesters demanded the authorities to take action against the miscreants.

On 25 November 2023, members of the Hindu Munnani staged a protest near the Kasiviswanathar Temple in the Tirupparankundram locality of Madurai city (Tamil Nadu) against the 'Karthigai Deepam' (festival of lights) celebration that was scheduled to take place the next day. Police arrested around 300 protesters for trying to light the lamp on the ancient lamp post near temple.

On 25 November 2023, members of the IYC staged a demonstration at the Secretariat in Thiruvananthapuram city (Kerala) against the detention of several IYC members during the Navakerala Sadas (CPI(M) event) in Kannur. Demonstrators demanded the Chief Minister's resignation and had a minor scuffle with the police. Police attempted to disperse the demonstrators using water cannons.

On 25 November 2023, members of IYC and the KSU staged a protest in the Eranhipalam locality in Kozhikode city (Kerala) against the Chief Minister's Navakerala Sadas (LDF) event. Protesters attempted to wave black flags and were detained by the police.

On 25 November 2023, members of the IYC and the KSU staged a black flag protest near Koyilandy town (Kozhikode, Kerala) Against the Chief Minister's Navakerala Sadas (LDF) event. Police detained the protesters.

On 25 November 2023, hundreds of government teaching job candidates staged a protest at the BJP's State office in Lucknow city (Uttar Pradesh) demanding jobs at the Education Department and accusing the authorities of malpractice in the recruitment process. Protesters were briefly detained and released at Eco Park. The protesters also accused BJP members and the police of beating up the protesters during the protest.

On 25 November 2023, a group of people entered a polling booth, assaulted INC members, and damaged voting equipment in Suketi village under Nagar (Bharatpur, Rajasthan), over likely political rivalry, on the day of voting in legislative assembly elections. Five people were injured.
On 25 November 2023, aspiring teachers protested at various locations in Agartala city (West Tripura, Tripura) against the government for delaying recruitment processes.

On 25 November 2023, a protest march was staged by the All India Democratic Women's Association (AIDWA) in Agartala city (West Tripura, Tripura) demanding the government to implement stricter laws and policies for the protection of women. Protesters demanded effective measures to prevent and punish the cases of violence, torture and molestation of women. The rally is a part of a nationwide campaign.

On 25 November 2023, more than 500 members of the Hindu Munnani staged a protest near the 16 Pillar Hall in Thiruparankundram own (Madurai, Tamil Nadu) against the authorities for not lighting the Karthigai Deepamon (lamp) on the premises of the Uchipillayar temple on the hilltop because a Muslim dargah (shrine) was situated close by. Police detained 500 protesters when they attempted to go up the hill.

On 25 November 2023, locals (likely Muslim based on the issue) staged a protest in Raunda village within Moondapande police station area (Moradabad, UP) after Hindu villagers began constructing a temple without obtaining prior permission.
